## Requirements

### FR1: Error Handling — Narrow Exception Scope
Replace bare `except Exception` in `EpochWorkflow.run()` with `except TransitionError`. Failed transitions must be recorded in the audit trail (transition_history) with error context. Mutation test exception specificity (SLICE-1 bare except) must also be addressed.
- Findings: aura-plugins-3xe, aura-plugins-6wg, aura-plugins-i2g, aura-plugins-295

### FR2: Constraint Completeness — Full 22 C-* Coverage
Expand `RuntimeConstraintChecker.check_all()` to aggregate all 22 C-* constraint checks defined in schema.xml. Each constraint must have a dedicated method. `check_severity_tree()` must enforce the POSITIVE case of C-severity-eager (p10 MUST have 3 severity groups eagerly). EpochState needs a `severity_groups` field to enable runtime enforcement.
- Findings: aura-plugins-yno, aura-plugins-jwb, aura-plugins-947, aura-plugins-bnr

### FR3: Type Safety Hardening — Strongly-Typed Enums Throughout
Change `EpochState.current_role` from `str` to `RoleId`. Document TYPE_CHECKING Protocol limitations (isinstance checks only method name presence, not full signature) in interfaces.py module docstring. Add test verifying `RuntimeConstraintChecker` satisfies `ConstraintValidatorInterface` Protocol.
- Findings: aura-plugins-tcn, aura-plugins-don, aura-plugins-ngd, aura-plugins-5zf

### FR4: Temporal Integration Testing — Sandbox End-to-End
Add `WorkflowEnvironment.start_time_skipping()` integration tests for EpochWorkflow. Decouple timestamp from `advance()` by passing timestamp as explicit parameter. Test actual Temporal signal delivery (advance_phase, submit_vote) in sandbox.
- Findings: aura-plugins-68o, aura-plugins-gdx, aura-plugins-o83

### FR5: MINOR Bundled Cleanup
Address all MINOR findings alongside their IMPORTANT siblings:
- Duplicated `_advance_to` helper → shared conftest.py fixture (aura-plugins-sk6, aura-plugins-0yd)
- `DataPart.data` and `ToolCall` dict fields → `dict[str, Any]` (aura-plugins-utj, aura-plugins-eqy)
- `FilePart.file_uri` → document A2A migration path (aura-plugins-7d2, aura-plugins-hls)
- `SA_EPOCH_ID` per-transition upsert → document or make defensive (aura-plugins-xui, aura-plugins-r8f)
- `check_blocker_gate` constraint_id naming (aura-plugins-dvi, aura-plugins-qqf)
- `_SAME_ACTOR` frozenset → module-level constant (aura-plugins-pxo)
- `AuditEvent.payload` str → typed pattern (aura-plugins-h7x)
- Test `__import__` inline → top-level import (aura-plugins-v1b)
- Test hardcoded constraint subset → full set verification (aura-plugins-8jy)
- `TransitionRecord` post-hoc mutation → pass timestamp into advance (aura-plugins-x36, aura-plugins-3m4)
- `EpochState.current_role` str→RoleId (aura-plugins-1ic, aura-plugins-4hu)
- `ToolCall` hashability test documentation (aura-plugins-4u1)

## Constraints
- C-backwards: Must not break existing 475 tests
- C-no-new-deps: No new pip packages — only stdlib + existing deps (temporalio, pytest, pytest-asyncio)
- C-python-only: All code in aura-plugins must be Python (R7 from original URD)

## Priorities (User-Stated)
1. All 4 IMPORTANT themes equally prioritized
2. MINOR findings bundled with their IMPORTANT siblings (same-slice, same-pass)
3. Full 22 C-* constraint coverage (not a subset)

## MVP Goals
- check_all() covers all 22 C-* constraints with dedicated methods
- EpochWorkflow.run() catches only TransitionError, records failures
- EpochState.current_role typed as RoleId
- WorkflowEnvironment sandbox tests for signal delivery
- All MINOR cleanup addressed alongside IMPORTANT siblings
- 475+ tests pass (existing + new)

## End-Vision Alignment
This follow-up closes the gap between v1 MVP and the URD (aura-plugins-umi) requirements for:
- Forensic auditability (FR1: failed transitions recorded)
- Complete constraint enforcement surface (FR2: all 22 C-*)
- Strongly-typed protocol invariants (FR3: no str leaks)
- Temporal workflow confidence (FR4: sandbox tests prove signal delivery)"}

references:

VOTE: ACCEPT — Test strategy is comprehensive and well-grounded in existing project conventions. All 7 review focus areas are satisfied.

## Review Summary (Axis B — Test Quality)

### 1. Test Strategy Sufficiency

The 4 new test files (test_schema_parser.py, test_gen_schema.py, test_gen_skills.py, test_context_injection.py) plus extensions to test_schema_types_sync.py provide complete coverage mapped to all new modules. Each new module has a dedicated test file. The mapping is 1:1 with module boundaries (schema_parser ↔ test_schema_parser, gen_schema ↔ test_gen_schema, gen_skills ↔ test_gen_skills, context_injection ↔ test_context_injection). This aligns with the existing pattern (constraints.py ↔ test_constraints.py, state_machine.py ↔ test_state_machine.py). No module is untested.

ASSESSMENT: ADEQUATE.

### 2. Error Path Coverage

AC1a specifies 3+ error-path tests for SchemaParseError with named failure inputs: malformed XML (truncated), missing required sections (e.g. `<phases>`), and missing required attributes. SchemaParseError is defined as a proper exception class with a clear docstring. The validation checklist has a dedicated entry.

AC4a specifies three distinct marker edge cases for MarkerError: (1) missing END marker → raise, (2) missing both markers → generate full content (clean path), (3) reversed markers → raise. The "should not silently discard body on any boundary error" invariant is the correct safety clause. MarkerError is defined as a ValueError subclass.

Together these are 6+ named error scenarios across 2 error types. The mutation-based approach from test_validate_schema.py provides a strong conceptual model that test_schema_parser.py can follow (inject bad inputs, assert specific exception with correct type).

ASSESSMENT: ADEQUATE.

### 3. Round-Trip Test Design

AC3 specifies "field-by-field comparison" and the validation checklist says "(not count-only)". The existing test_schema_types_sync.py at lines 294-308 (TestConstraintSpecsMatchSchema.test_constraint_given_when_then_match_schema) already demonstrates the correct pattern: iterate schema elements, look up the Python spec by ID, and assert each field individually (given, when, then). This is the exact model for AC3.

The proposal names specific fields per entity type in AC3: ConstraintSpec.given/when/then/should_not, HandoffSpec.required_fields, SubstepSpec.startup_sequence. These are concrete anchors that prevent count-only assertions. The test_gen_schema round-trip direction is: types.py → gen_schema → parse_schema → field-level comparison, which is a true integration test of two new modules working together. The prior Round 2 review B (aura-plugins-qt1p) correctly identified that AC3 should cover should_not (missing from the existing test_schema_types_sync.py pattern) — and the proposal now includes it explicitly.

ASSESSMENT: ADEQUATE. The model is demonstrated in the existing codebase and the proposal correctly extends it.

### 4. Absence Testing

AC5a names concrete constraint IDs: C-worker-gates must NOT appear in get_role_context(SUPERVISOR); C-supervisor-no-impl must NOT appear in get_role_context(WORKER). AC6a: C-severity-eager must NOT appear in get_phase_context(P4_REVIEW); C-review-consensus must NOT appear in get_phase_context(P9_SLICE).

These are precise, falsifiable assertions against specific string identifiers. They test the SUT's output (the returned frozenset), not internal state. They follow the project's convention of asserting observable outcomes. The validation checklist has two dedicated entries ("get_role_context does NOT include irrelevant constraints", "get_phase_context does NOT include irrelevant constraints").

One observation: these absence tests rely on the static _ROLE_CONSTRAINTS and _PHASE_CONSTRAINTS dicts in context_injection.py being correctly populated. Since these dicts are hand-authored (not derived from schema.xml structurally), the tests need to be robust enough that they catch errors in that hand-authored data. The named constraint IDs (C-worker-gates, C-supervisor-no-impl) provide exactly the right anchors.

ASSESSMENT: ADEQUATE.

### 5. Regression Safety

AC7 states "all 554 existing tests pass" and AC11 (Temporal Isolation) states "all sandbox tests pass unchanged" with an explicit enumeration of the 6 Temporal-serialized types that must NOT be modified (EpochState, TransitionRecord, EpochInput, EpochResult, PhaseAdvanceSignal, ReviewVoteSignal). The "unchanged" files list explicitly includes state_machine.py, constraints.py, workflow.py, interfaces.py — all of which have comprehensive existing tests (test_state_machine.py ~120, test_constraints.py ~180, test_workflow.py ~60, test_interfaces.py ~40).

The HandoffSpec.content_level str→ContentLevel change (the one non-additive modification) is correctly called out in the proposal as requiring test_schema_types_sync.py to update (line 346 comparison `spec.content_level == h.get("content-level")` will need to compare the enum value string, not the enum itself).

One specific gap: the proposal does not explicitly call out that test_schema_types_sync.py's TestHandoffSpecsMatchSchema.test_handoff_roles_match_schema will need updating for the content_level field after the str→ContentLevel change. This is a valid implementation concern but it is traceable from the validation checklist ("test_schema_types_sync.py covers all new canonical dicts") and the "modified files" table (test_schema_types_sync.py listed as modified). A worker reading both sections can connect the dots.

ASSESSMENT: ADEQUATE. The regression strategy is sound. The one gap (content_level comparison update) is traceable from proposal text.

### 6. Integration Test Coverage

AC10 specifies the end-to-end pipeline test: parse_schema → populate types → gen_schema → validate_schema → gen_skills. This exercises all 4 new modules in sequence plus the existing validate_schema.py. This is a true integration test — not a mock-based test — because it runs the actual parsing, generation, and validation logic. It follows the project's convention (test_validate_schema.py already tests validate_schema.py via both the library API and subprocess CLI).

The prior Round 2 Review B (aura-plugins-qt1p) noted the "pipeline direction ambiguity" in AC10 (bootstrap vs. steady-state) as an IMPORTANT finding. PROPOSAL-3 does not resolve this ambiguity — AC10 still reads "parse_schema → populate types → gen_schema → validate_schema → gen_skills" which mixes bootstrap (schema→Python) and steady-state (Python→schema) steps. The validation checklist uses the slightly different phrasing "parse → gen_schema → validate → gen_skills" which omits "populate types".

This is the same IMPORTANT finding from Round 2 — not a new BLOCKER. Workers can resolve it by reading both documents together, and the checklist phrasing is the more actionable guide. Both pipeline directions are valid to test.

ASSESSMENT: ADEQUATE for a plan-review vote. The ambiguity is pre-existing, documented, and not a blocker.

### 7. Existing Test Pattern Alignment

Reading conftest.py and test_schema_types_sync.py reveals the following conventions:
- Class-per-concern grouping (TestPhaseIdMatchesSchema, TestConstraintSpecsMatchSchema, etc.)
- Module-scoped fixtures for expensive resources (schema_root fixture with scope="module")
- Field-level assertions with informative error messages (f-string showing both sides)
- pytest.mark.parametrize for combinatorial coverage (mutation tests, template rendering across 4 roles)
- from __future__ import annotations at the top
- Absolute Path construction via Path(__file__).resolve().parent

The proposal's test design aligns well with these conventions:
- AC8 uses pytest.mark.parametrize over 4 role templates (aligns with TestMutationDetection pattern)
- AC3 round-trip uses field-level assertions (aligns with test_constraint_given_when_then_match_schema pattern)

### Temporal Compatibility

**No breaking changes to Temporal-serialized types.** The Temporal workflow (workflow.py) serializes:
- EpochState (contains PhaseId, RoleId, VoteType, SeverityLevel)
- TransitionRecord (contains PhaseId)
- EpochInput, EpochResult, PhaseAdvanceSignal, ReviewVoteSignal

None of these types are modified. New types (RoleSpec, CommandSpec, ConstraintContext, etc.) are NOT used by Temporal — they're for code generation and context injection only.

**HandoffSpec.content_level str→ContentLevel change:** This is safe because HandoffSpec is NOT serialized by Temporal. It's only used in constraints.py for validation and in types.py as a static definition.

### context_injection.py Integration Points

context_injection.py is a pure lookup module — no side effects, no Temporal dependency:
- Reads from PHASE_SPECS, CONSTRAINT_SPECS, HANDOFF_SPECS (existing), ROLE_SPECS, COMMAND_SPECS, LABEL_SPECS (new)
- Called at skill invocation time (not from Temporal workflow)
- Called at phase transition time for prompt enrichment (not from Temporal workflow)
- Static mappings for constraint→role and constraint→phase (Python is SoT; gen_schema.py exports as role-ref/phase-ref into schema.xml)
- Returns frozen RoleContext / PhaseContext dataclasses with ConstraintContext (typed when+then)

### Temporal Compatibility

**No breaking changes to Temporal-serialized types.** The Temporal workflow (workflow.py) serializes:
- EpochState (contains PhaseId, RoleId, VoteType, SeverityLevel)
- TransitionRecord (contains PhaseId)
- EpochInput, EpochResult, PhaseAdvanceSignal, ReviewVoteSignal

None of these types are modified. New types (RoleSpec, CommandSpec, ConstraintContext, etc.) are NOT used by Temporal — they're for code generation and context injection only.

**HandoffSpec.content_level str→ContentLevel change:** This is safe because HandoffSpec is NOT serialized by Temporal. It's only used in constraints.py for validation and in types.py as a static definition.

### context_injection.py Integration Points

context_injection.py is a pure lookup module — no side effects, no Temporal dependency:
- Reads from PHASE_SPECS, CONSTRAINT_SPECS, HANDOFF_SPECS (existing), ROLE_SPECS, COMMAND_SPECS, LABEL_SPECS (new)
- Called at skill invocation time (not from Temporal workflow)
- Called at phase transition time for prompt enrichment (not from Temporal workflow)
- Static mappings for constraint→role and constraint→phase (Python is SoT; gen_schema.py exports as role-ref/phase-ref into schema.xml)
- Returns frozen RoleContext / PhaseContext dataclasses with ConstraintContext (typed when+then)

## Problem Space

**Axes:** code generation (schema → code, code → schema), drift elimination (38 SKILL.md files × 1 schema.xml), runtime context injection (role-level + phase-level), source-of-truth inversion (schema.xml → Python types.py)

## Engineering Tradeoffs

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| Source of truth | Python types.py | User requirement. Directly usable at runtime. |
| Bootstrap | Hybrid codegen + manual polish (UAT-1) | gen_types.py generates draft; developer reviews and merges. Saves transcription, retains control. |
| Template engine | Jinja2 (dev-only dep) | Industry standard. StrictUndefined catches errors. |
| XML generation | xml.etree.ElementTree | Stdlib, no new dependency |
| SKILL.md split | Marker-based (markers required) (UAT-5) | gen_skills.py raises MarkerError if no markers found. No silent prepending. |
| ProcedureStep | Populated for supervisor+worker POC (UAT-6) | Proves the pattern end-to-end. Other roles deferred. |
| content_level typing | ContentLevel enum (from str) | Type safety; non-breaking (not Temporal-serialized) |
| Constraint→role mapping | Static dicts in Python → role-ref/phase-ref in XML (UAT-3) | Python is SoT; gen_schema.py exports structural attributes into schema.xml |
| Context injection types | ConstraintContext frozen dataclass (UAT-4) | Typed when+then fields, not bare strings. Strongly-typed throughout. |
| Generation diff output | gen_schema + gen_skills show diff (UAT-2) | User requirement: must see what changed on each generation run. |

### Temporal Compatibility

**No breaking changes to Temporal-serialized types.** The Temporal workflow (workflow.py) serializes:
- EpochState (contains PhaseId, RoleId, VoteType, SeverityLevel)
- TransitionRecord (contains PhaseId)
- EpochInput, EpochResult, PhaseAdvanceSignal, ReviewVoteSignal

None of these types are modified. New types (RoleSpec, CommandSpec, ConstraintContext, etc.) are NOT used by Temporal — they're for code generation and context injection only.

**HandoffSpec.content_level str→ContentLevel change:** This is safe because HandoffSpec is NOT serialized by Temporal. It's only used in constraints.py for validation and in types.py as a static definition.

### context_injection.py Integration Points

context_injection.py is a pure lookup module — no side effects, no Temporal dependency:
- Reads from PHASE_SPECS, CONSTRAINT_SPECS, HANDOFF_SPECS (existing), ROLE_SPECS, COMMAND_SPECS, LABEL_SPECS (new)
- Called at skill invocation time (not from Temporal workflow)
- Called at phase transition time for prompt enrichment (not from Temporal workflow)
- Static mappings for constraint→role and constraint→phase (Python is SoT; gen_schema.py exports as role-ref/phase-ref into schema.xml)
- Returns frozen RoleContext / PhaseContext dataclasses with ConstraintContext (typed when+then)

## Problem Space

**Axes:** code generation (schema → code, code → schema), drift elimination (38 SKILL.md files × 1 schema.xml), runtime context injection (role-level + phase-level), source-of-truth inversion (schema.xml → Python types.py)

## Engineering Tradeoffs

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| Source of truth | Python types.py | User requirement. Directly usable at runtime. |
| Bootstrap | Hybrid codegen + manual polish (UAT-1) | gen_types.py generates draft; developer reviews and merges. Saves transcription, retains control. |
| Template engine | Jinja2 (dev-only dep) | Industry standard. StrictUndefined catches errors. |
| XML generation | xml.etree.ElementTree | Stdlib, no new dependency |
| SKILL.md split | Marker-based (markers required) (UAT-5) | gen_skills.py raises MarkerError if no markers found. No silent prepending. |
| ProcedureStep | Populated for supervisor+worker POC (UAT-6) | Proves the pattern end-to-end. Other roles deferred. |
| content_level typing | ContentLevel enum (from str) | Type safety; non-breaking (not Temporal-serialized) |
| Constraint→role mapping | Static dicts in Python → role-ref/phase-ref in XML (UAT-3) | Python is SoT; gen_schema.py exports structural attributes into schema.xml |
| Context injection types | ConstraintContext frozen dataclass (UAT-4) | Typed when+then fields, not bare strings. Strongly-typed throughout. |
| Generation diff output | gen_schema + gen_skills show diff (UAT-2) | User requirement: must see what changed on each generation run. |

The existing test_schema_types_sync.py at lines 294-308 (TestConstraintSpecsMatchSchema.test_constraint_given_when_then_match_schema) already demonstrates the correct pattern: iterate schema elements, look up the Python spec by ID, and assert each field individually (given, when, then). This is the exact model for AC3.

The proposal names specific fields per entity type in AC3: ConstraintSpec.given/when/then/should_not, HandoffSpec.required_fields, SubstepSpec.startup_sequence. These are concrete anchors that prevent count-only assertions. The test_gen_schema round-trip direction is: types.py → gen_schema → parse_schema → field-level comparison, which is a true integration test of two new modules working together. The prior Round 2 review B (aura-plugins-qt1p) correctly identified that AC3 should cover should_not (missing from the existing test_schema_types_sync.py pattern) — and the proposal now includes it explicitly.

ASSESSMENT: ADEQUATE. The model is demonstrated in the existing codebase and the proposal correctly extends it.

### 4. Absence Testing

AC5a names concrete constraint IDs: C-worker-gates must NOT appear in get_role_context(SUPERVISOR); C-supervisor-no-impl must NOT appear in get_role_context(WORKER). AC6a: C-severity-eager must NOT appear in get_phase_context(P4_REVIEW); C-review-consensus must NOT appear in get_phase_context(P9_SLICE).

These are precise, falsifiable assertions against specific string identifiers. They test the SUT's output (the returned frozenset), not internal state. They follow the project's convention of asserting observable outcomes. The validation checklist has two dedicated entries ("get_role_context does NOT include irrelevant constraints", "get_phase_context does NOT include irrelevant constraints").

One observation: these absence tests rely on the static _ROLE_CONSTRAINTS and _PHASE_CONSTRAINTS dicts in context_injection.py being correctly populated. Since these dicts are hand-authored (not derived from schema.xml structurally), the tests need to be robust enough that they catch errors in that hand-authored data. The named constraint IDs (C-worker-gates, C-supervisor-no-impl) provide exactly the right anchors.

ASSESSMENT: ADEQUATE.

### 5. Regression Safety

AC7 states "all 554 existing tests pass" and AC11 (Temporal Isolation) states "all sandbox tests pass unchanged" with an explicit enumeration of the 6 Temporal-serialized types that must NOT be modified (EpochState, TransitionRecord, EpochInput, EpochResult, PhaseAdvanceSignal, ReviewVoteSignal). The "unchanged" files list explicitly includes state_machine.py, constraints.py, workflow.py, interfaces.py — all of which have comprehensive existing tests (test_state_machine.py ~120, test_constraints.py ~180, test_workflow.py ~60, test_interfaces.py ~40).

The HandoffSpec.content_level str→ContentLevel change (the one non-additive modification) is correctly called out in the proposal as requiring test_schema_types_sync.py to update (line 346 comparison `spec.content_level == h.get("content-level")` will need to compare the enum value string, not the enum itself).

One specific gap: the proposal does not explicitly call out that test_schema_types_sync.py's TestHandoffSpecsMatchSchema.test_handoff_roles_match_schema will need updating for the content_level field after the str→ContentLevel change. This is a valid implementation concern but it is traceable from the validation checklist ("test_schema_types_sync.py covers all new canonical dicts") and the "modified files" table (test_schema_types_sync.py listed as modified). A worker reading both sections can connect the dots.

ASSESSMENT: ADEQUATE. The regression strategy is sound. The one gap (content_level comparison update) is traceable from proposal text.

### 6. Integration Test Coverage

AC10 specifies the end-to-end pipeline test: parse_schema → populate types → gen_schema → validate_schema → gen_skills. This exercises all 4 new modules in sequence plus the existing validate_schema.py. This is a true integration test — not a mock-based test — because it runs the actual parsing, generation, and validation logic. It follows the project's convention (test_validate_schema.py already tests validate_schema.py via both the library API and subprocess CLI).

The prior Round 2 Review B (aura-plugins-qt1p) noted the "pipeline direction ambiguity" in AC10 (bootstrap vs. steady-state) as an IMPORTANT finding. PROPOSAL-3 does not resolve this ambiguity — AC10 still reads "parse_schema → populate types → gen_schema → validate_schema → gen_skills" which mixes bootstrap (schema→Python) and steady-state (Python→schema) steps. The validation checklist uses the slightly different phrasing "parse → gen_schema → validate → gen_skills" which omits "populate types".

This is the same IMPORTANT finding from Round 2 — not a new BLOCKER. Workers can resolve it by reading both documents together, and the checklist phrasing is the more actionable guide. Both pipeline directions are valid to test.

ASSESSMENT: ADEQUATE for a plan-review vote. The ambiguity is pre-existing, documented, and not a blocker.

### 7. Existing Test Pattern Alignment

Reading conftest.py and test_schema_types_sync.py reveals the following conventions:
- Class-per-concern grouping (TestPhaseIdMatchesSchema, TestConstraintSpecsMatchSchema, etc.)
- Module-scoped fixtures for expensive resources (schema_root fixture with scope="module")

All 7 review focus areas are satisfied. The test strategy is comprehensive, well-anchored in named failure inputs and named constraint IDs, field-level comparison is modelled on existing code, regression safety is explicitly scoped, and integration coverage exercises all 4 new modules end-to-end. ## Reviewer C (Elegance and Complexity Matching) — PROPOSAL-3, Round 1

---

## What Changed from PROPOSAL-2 (previously 3/3 ACCEPT)

PROPOSAL-3 adds to the already-ratified PROPOSAL-2:
1. Existing Foundation inventory (full v1+followup accounting)
2. Integration architecture diagram (explicit module-to-existing-code mapping)
3. Temporal compatibility analysis (no breaking changes to serialized types)
4. Modified vs new files delineation (clear ownership per file)
5. Gap analysis findings from 4 explore agents (SubstepSpec, DelegateSpec, 6 missing enums)
6. AC11: Temporal Isolation (new, explicit, machine-verifiable AC)
7. content_level str→ContentLevel enum fix (non-breaking type-safety improvement)

None of these additions introduce new modules, new abstractions, or new complexity. They are documentation improvements and a minor type-safety fix. The underlying architecture is unchanged.

---

## Sub-Axis Analysis

### 1. Complexity Proportionality

The added elements are proportionate:
- Gap analysis → 2 additional dataclasses (SubstepSpec, DelegateSpec) and 6 missing enums found by explore agents. These are discoveries, not invented complexity. Schema.xml has these entities; the types should represent them.
- AC11 (Temporal Isolation) is a zero-implementation-cost AC — the existing Temporal types are unchanged; the test just verifies the sandbox tests still pass. This is pure guard rail.
- content_level enum change: one field type corrected. Non-breaking because HandoffSpec is not Temporal-serialized. The proposal documents this reasoning explicitly.

### 2. Module Decomposition — Unchanged, Still Clean

4 new modules: schema_parser, gen_schema, gen_skills, context_injection. Each has single responsibility. Dependency graph remains a tree: generators and context_injection import types.py only, never each other. No circular dependencies possible. The integration architecture diagram confirms this explicitly.

### 3. context_injection.py Static Dict Approach — Adequate

The static dict approach for constraint→role and constraint→phase mappings is justified: the proposal correctly notes that this mapping is NOT structurally encoded in schema.xml (it's in the 'given:' text of constraints). The two options are (a) static dict or (b) parse free-text given: clauses at runtime. Option (b) would add fragility (free-text parsing) for no gain. Option (a) is correct. The approach matches the existing pattern in constraints.py where _REVIEW_PHASES, _SEVERITY_TREE_PHASES, and _HANDOFF_REQUIRED_TRANSITIONS are all static frozensets.

### 4. API Design Quality

The proposed interfaces are usable and consistent with the existing codebase:

- parse_schema(path: Path) -> SchemaSpec: one input, typed output, raises SchemaParseError. Clean.
- get_role_context(role: RoleId) -> RoleContext: strongly-typed enum input, frozen dataclass output. Matches existing pattern (constraints.py takes RoleId, PhaseId, etc.).
- get_phase_context(phase: PhaseId) -> PhaseContext: same pattern.
- SchemaSpec fields: all typed dicts keyed by str or PhaseId/RoleId. No bare dicts of Any.
- RoleContext and PhaseContext: frozen dataclasses using frozenset and tuple (immutable, consistent with PhaseSpec, ConstraintSpec, HandoffSpec).

The API surface is minimal and directly addresses the two use cases: bootstrap extraction and runtime context injection. No unused methods. No framework creep.

### 5. Source-of-Truth Clarity

Bootstrap → Steady-state distinction is clearly articulated:
- BOOTSTRAP: schema.xml → schema_parser.py → SchemaSpec → verify → expanded types.py (one-time)
- STEADY STATE: types.py (SoT) → gen_schema.py / gen_skills.py / context_injection.py (ongoing)

The integration architecture diagram makes this unambiguous. schema_parser.py's ongoing role (verification/round-trip) is cleanly separated from its bootstrap role (initial extraction). The transition point is explicit: after SLICE-1 completes and types.py is expanded, schema_parser.py becomes a verification tool rather than a migration tool.

### 6. Vertical Slice Decomposition — Correct Granularity

4 slices is the right count:
- SLICE-1: Foundation (types expansion + schema_parser). Must finish first. Cannot parallelize with anything.
- SLICE-2: gen_schema.py. Depends only on SLICE-1. Can parallelize with SLICE-3 and SLICE-4.
- SLICE-3: gen_skills.py. Depends only on SLICE-1. Can parallelize with SLICE-2 and SLICE-4.
- SLICE-4: context_injection.py. Depends only on SLICE-1. Can parallelize with SLICE-2 and SLICE-3.

Merging SLICE-2+SLICE-3 would create a slice with two unrelated output formats (XML and Markdown). Merging any of SLICE-2/3/4 with SLICE-4 would conflate code generation with runtime injection — two orthogonal concerns. The 4-slice decomposition correctly follows the C-vertical-slices constraint. Each slice owns exactly one production code path.

### 7. Existing Codebase Consistency

Verified against types.py, constraints.py, interfaces.py:

- Frozen dataclasses: types.py uses @dataclass(frozen=True) throughout. New types (RoleSpec, SubstepSpec, etc.) will follow the same pattern. ACCEPT.
- Enum-heavy approach: PhaseId, Domain, RoleId, VoteType, SeverityLevel all use class X(str, Enum). New enums ExecutionMode, ContentLevel will follow. The str subclassing enables JSON/Temporal serialization compatibility. ACCEPT.
- Canonical dicts: PHASE_SPECS, CONSTRAINT_SPECS, HANDOFF_SPECS use dict[PhaseId/str, XSpec] pattern. New dicts ROLE_SPECS, COMMAND_SPECS, etc. follow the same pattern. ACCEPT.
- frozenset for unordered membership, tuple for ordered sequences: PhaseSpec.owner_roles uses frozenset[RoleId]; PhaseSpec.transitions uses tuple[Transition, ...]. New types use the same discipline (RoleContext.phases uses frozenset[PhaseId]; RoleContext.commands uses tuple[str, ...]). ACCEPT.
- Module-level constants in ALL_CAPS: _REVIEW_PHASES, _SEVERITY_TREE_PHASES in constraints.py. Private static dicts _ROLE_CONSTRAINTS, _PHASE_CONSTRAINTS in context_injection.py follow the same underscore-prefix convention. ACCEPT.

The proposal's style is fully consistent with the existing codebase.

### 8. One Observation (Not a Concern)

The proposal lists 8 new dataclasses: SubstepSpec, RoleSpec, DelegateSpec, CommandSpec, LabelSpec, ReviewAxisSpec, TitleConvention, ProcedureStep. SubstepSpec and DelegateSpec are new additions from the gap analysis (not in PROPOSAL-2). This is correct — the explore agents found these entity types in schema.xml. The count is accurate. Their addition is appropriate, not inflated.

### 9. URD Coverage (Elegance Lens)

| Req | Status | Elegance Note |
|-----|--------|---------------|
| R1 | Clean | SchemaSpec mirrors all 7 schema.xml entity types |
| R2 | Clean | SoT inversion clearly articulated with bootstrap/steady-state diagram |
| R3 | Clean | All new types are frozen dataclasses, consistent with existing |
| R4 | Clean | Marker-based split remains minimal and safe |
| R5 | Deferred (type defined, dict empty) | Correct boundary, unchanged from PROPOSAL-2 |
| R6 | Clean | Two-function injection, static dict, no framework |
| R7 | Clean | gen_schema.py → validate_schema.py round-trip |

---

## Conclusion

PROPOSAL-3 is an additive clarification of PROPOSAL-2. It resolves no new BLOCKERs (there were none) and introduces no new concerns. The gap analysis discoveries (SubstepSpec, DelegateSpec, 6 missing enums) are correct additions — they reflect what schema.xml actually contains. The integration architecture and Temporal compatibility notes reduce implementation risk without adding architectural complexity. The content_level typing fix is a correct, non-breaking improvement. All prior elegance criteria remain satisfied.

{"id":"aura-plugins-myk7","title":"SLICE-4-REVIEW-C-1-F12: _build_constraint_contexts silently skips unknown constraint IDs — violates C-actionable-errors","description":"Axis-C finding (Elegance/Error Handling — violates C-actionable-errors).

context_injection.py _build_constraint_contexts() (lines 317-330) has this comment:
  'Unknown constraint IDs are skipped silently (should not occur with hand-authored dicts).'

Then the code does:
  spec = CONSTRAINT_SPECS.get(cid)
  if spec is not None:
      contexts.add(ConstraintContext(...))
  # else: silently skipped

This violates C-actionable-errors. If a constraint ID in _ROLE_CONSTRAINTS or _PHASE_CONSTRAINTS does not exist in CONSTRAINT_SPECS (e.g., due to a typo or stale mapping after a constraint rename), the function silently drops it. The caller receives a ConstraintContext set with fewer entries than expected, with no indication anything went wrong.

The rationale 'should not occur' is insufficient — that is true of most bugs. Silent drops make debugging extremely difficult: get_role_context(SUPERVISOR) returns silently missing constraints, but no error is raised, no count mismatch is surfaced.

Fix: Change the None branch to raise a ValueError (or KeyError) with an actionable message:
  raise KeyError(
      f'Constraint ID {cid!r} in _ROLE_CONSTRAINTS/{_PHASE_CONSTRAINTS} '
      f'not found in CONSTRAINT_SPECS. '
      f'Fix: update _ROLE_CONSTRAINTS/_PHASE_CONSTRAINTS to use a valid constraint ID.'
  )
This turns a silent correctness issue into an immediate, actionable error.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"dayvidpham@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-02-23T04:25:21Z","created_by":"David Huu Pham","updated_at":"2026-02-23T04:25:21Z"}

The signature of generate_schema() (gen_schema.py line 1600) is:

Both gen_schema.py (lines 49-99) and context_injection.py (lines 140-311) define:
  - _ROLE_CONSTRAINTS: dict[RoleId|str, ...]
  - _PHASE_CONSTRAINTS: dict[PhaseId|str, ...]

These two dicts represent the same domain knowledge: which constraints apply to which roles and phases. They exist in two different modules for two different purposes:
  - gen_schema.py uses them to emit role-ref/phase-ref attributes in schema.xml (str-keyed)
  - context_injection.py uses them to build ConstraintContext objects at runtime (PhaseId/RoleId-keyed)

The proposal docstring in context_injection.py (line 28-29) even acknowledges: 'gen_schema.py (SLICE-2) reads _ROLE_CONSTRAINTS and _PHASE_CONSTRAINTS to emit role-ref and phase-ref attributes into schema.xml (UAT-3).'

But gen_schema.py defines its own separate copies\! If someone adds a new constraint in types.py and updates context_injection.py's mappings, they must also update gen_schema.py's mappings, or schema.xml will be out of sync with the runtime context.

Fix: Consolidate. context_injection.py should be the single definition of these mappings. gen_schema.py should import _ROLE_CONSTRAINTS and _PHASE_CONSTRAINTS from context_injection.py, or both should be moved to a shared types.py location. @pytest.fixture(scope='module')
def aura_release_mod():
    '''Import aura-release once per module. Cleans sys.modules at module teardown.'''
    loader = SourceFileLoader('aura_release', str(BIN_PATH / 'aura-release'))
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_loader('aura_release', loader)
    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules['aura_release'] = mod  # must register before exec
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    yield mod
    sys.modules.pop('aura_release', None)

@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _clear_caches(aura_release_mod):
    '''Clear lru_cache on repo_root between tests (prevents cwd leakage).'''
    yield
    aura_release_mod.repo_root.cache_clear()

## PluginRegistry.find_plugin()
```python
def find_plugin(self, name: str | None, cwd: Path) -> tuple[PluginEntry, MarketplaceEntry] | None:
    resolved_cwd = cwd.resolve()

        for plugin in marketplace.plugins:
            if name:
                if plugin.name == name: return plugin, marketplace
            else:
                if plugin.path.resolve() == resolved_cwd: return plugin, marketplace
    return None

## Types (bin/aura-release)

```python
def _registry_path() -> Path:
    return Path.home() / '.local' / 'config' / 'aura' / 'plugins' / 'claude-plugin-registry.json'

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PluginEntry:
    name: str
    path: Path        # absolute
    remote: str | None

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MarketplaceEntry:
    path: Path
    plugins: tuple[PluginEntry, ...]

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PluginRegistry:
    marketplaces: tuple[MarketplaceEntry, ...]
    # Methods: load(), save(), find_plugin(), with_plugin_added(), with_plugin_removed()
```

## PluginRegistry.load() Validation Rules
- File absent → return None (no error)
- Invalid JSON → print error + sys.exit(2)
- Missing 'marketplaces' key → print error + sys.exit(2)
- marketplace.path does not exist → warn + skip
- plugin entry missing name/path → warn + skip

## PluginRegistry.find_plugin()
```python
def find_plugin(self, name: str | None, cwd: Path) -> tuple[PluginEntry, MarketplaceEntry] | None:
    resolved_cwd = cwd.resolve()
    for marketplace in self.marketplaces:
        for plugin in marketplace.plugins:
            if name:
                if plugin.name == name: return plugin, marketplace
            else:
                if plugin.path.resolve() == resolved_cwd: return plugin, marketplace
    return None
```

### Dataclasses (Path fields throughout)

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PluginEntry:
    name: str
    path: Path        # absolute local path to plugin repo
    remote: str | None

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MarketplaceEntry:
    path: Path                        # absolute path to marketplace.json
    plugins: tuple[PluginEntry, ...]

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PluginRegistry:
    marketplaces: tuple[MarketplaceEntry, ...]

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, registry_path: Path | None = None) -> PluginRegistry | None:
        """Load and validate registry. Returns None if absent.

        Validation:
        - File absent → return None (no error)
        - Invalid JSON → print error + sys.exit(2)
        - Missing "marketplaces" key → print error + sys.exit(2)
        - marketplace.path does not exist → warn + skip (continue loading)
        - plugin entry missing name or path → warn + skip (continue loading)
        """
        path = registry_path or _registry_path()
        if not path.exists():
            return None
        try:
            data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
            print(f"Error: registry at {path} is malformed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(2)
        if "marketplaces" not in data:
            print(f"Error: registry at {path} missing marketplaces key", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(2)
        marketplaces = []
        for m in data["marketplaces"]:
            mp_path = Path(m.get("path", "")).expanduser().resolve()
            if not mp_path.exists():
                print(f"Warning: marketplace not found: {mp_path}", file=sys.stderr)
                continue
            plugins = []
            for p in m.get("plugins", []):
                if "name" not in p or "path" not in p:
                    print(f"Warning: skipping malformed plugin entry: {p}", file=sys.stderr)
                    continue
                plugins.append(PluginEntry(
                    name=p["name"],
                    path=Path(p["path"]).expanduser().resolve(),
                    remote=p.get("remote"),
                ))
            marketplaces.append(MarketplaceEntry(
                path=mp_path,
                plugins=tuple(plugins),
            ))
        return cls(marketplaces=tuple(marketplaces))

    def save(self, registry_path: Path | None = None, *, dry_run: bool = False) -> None:
        """Serialise registry to JSON. Creates parent dirs if needed."""
        ...

    def find_plugin(
        self, name: str | None, cwd: Path
    ) -> tuple[PluginEntry, MarketplaceEntry] | None:
        """Find by explicit name, or auto-detect by matching entry.path to cwd.resolve()."""
        resolved_cwd = cwd.resolve()
        for marketplace in self.marketplaces:
            for plugin in marketplace.plugins:
                if name:
                    if plugin.name == name:
                        return plugin, marketplace
                else:
                    if plugin.path.resolve() == resolved_cwd:
                        return plugin, marketplace
        return None

    def with_plugin_added(...) -> PluginRegistry: ...
    def with_plugin_removed(...) -> PluginRegistry: ...

```python
# ── After commit and tag ───────────────────────────────────────────
registry = PluginRegistry.load()
if registry:
    match = registry.find_plugin(getattr(args, "plugin", None), root)
    if match:
        plugin_entry, marketplace_entry = match

**Why after commit:** The registry marketplace write is the last side-effect. If it fails, the release is already committed and tagged locally; the user can manually fix the external marketplace file. This avoids rollback complexity entirely.

**Double-bump guard:** `resolved_mp not in {vf.path.resolve() for vf in files}` — if `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` was already discovered and bumped by `_SCAN_SPECS`, the guard prevents a second write to the same file.

### FIX-1 (A-1 MUST FIX): Simplify PhaseInput — remove PhaseSpec

PROPOSAL-6 passed `PhaseInput(phase_spec=PhaseSpec)` across workflow boundaries. PhaseSpec.owner_roles is `frozenset[RoleId]` which is **not JSON-serializable** by Temporal's default data converter — this would raise TypeError at serialize time.

**Fix:** PhaseInput carries only the StrEnum-typed phase_id. Child workflows reconstruct PhaseSpec from the canonical PHASE_SPECS registry (already available at import time, no I/O needed).

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PhaseInput:
    epoch_id: str
    phase_id: PhaseId
    # NO phase_spec — reconstructed from PHASE_SPECS in child workflow

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PhaseResult:
    phase_id: PhaseId
    success: bool
    blocker_count: int = 0
    vote_result: VoteType | None = None
```

**Why this is safe:** PHASE_SPECS is a module-level constant built from canonical Python types. Every worker process loads the same dict at import time — no network I/O, no side effects. Child workflows call `PHASE_SPECS[phase_input.phase_id]` immediately after receiving PhaseInput.

**Rule:** EpochState (mutable runtime state) NEVER crosses workflow boundaries. PhaseInput/PhaseResult carry only primitives and StrEnums.

---

### FIX-2 (B-1 MUST FIX): Structural enforcement of AuditTrail.query_events

PROPOSAL-6 marked `query_events` as ACTIVITY-ONLY via docstring only. Temporal's non-determinism detector won't catch a direct call from workflow context — it will corrupt the audit log silently.

**Fix:** Add a dedicated registered activity:

```python
# scripts/aura_protocol/audit_activities.py

@activity.defn
async def query_audit_events(
    trail: AuditTrail,
    epoch_id: str,
    phase_id: PhaseId | None = None,
) -> list[AuditEvent]:
    """Registered activity — the ONLY way workflows may read audit events."""
    return await trail.query_events(epoch_id=epoch_id, phase_id=phase_id)
```

`AuditTrail.query_events()` remains on the Protocol interface for direct use in non-workflow contexts (scripts, tests, adapters). Workflows MUST call `query_audit_events` via `workflow.execute_activity(query_audit_events, ...)`.

**Linting enforcement:** A comment in AuditTrail.query_events warns that direct calls in workflow context are forbidden. A future ast-grep rule can enforce this statically.

### FIX-3 (B-1 MUST FIX): Document child workflow join semantics

```python
# EpochWorkflow (parent):

    PhaseInput(epoch_id=self._epoch_id, phase_id=PhaseId.P4_REVIEW),

# Child independently:
#   1. Registers signal handlers for PhaseAdvanceSignal + ReviewVoteSignal
#   2. Drains its signal queue via workflow.wait_condition()
#   3. Returns PhaseResult when complete

Join semantics: `workflow.execute_child_workflow()` is an awaitable that resolves only when the child workflow completes and returns. The parent does not poll — it suspends at the await point.

## FIX-1 (A-1 + B-1 MUST FIX): Class-based AuditActivities with dependency injection

### Problem
PROPOSAL-7 proposed `query_audit_events(trail: AuditTrail, ...)` as a free function activity. Temporal serializes ALL activity arguments via JSON DataConverter. `AuditTrail` is a `@runtime_checkable Protocol` — it has no JSON representation and cannot be deserialized on the worker side. Confirmed via Temporal SDK `worker/_activity.py` lines 551-564 and `converter.py value_to_type`.

ActivityEnvironment (used in tests) bypasses serialization — this bug would not be caught by existing test infrastructure.

### Fix
Use the standard Temporal DI pattern: class-based activity with the dependency injected via `__init__`. Only serializable types (str, StrEnum, None) cross the serialization boundary.

```python
# scripts/aura_protocol/audit_activities.py

class AuditActivities:
    """Class-based Temporal activity holder for AuditTrail operations.

    The AuditTrail implementation is injected at worker startup via __init__.
    Only serializable arguments (epoch_id, phase_id) flow through Temporal's
    DataConverter — the trail instance never crosses the serialization boundary.
    """

    def __init__(self, trail: AuditTrail) -> None:
        self._trail = trail

    @activity.defn
    async def query_audit_events(
        self,
        epoch_id: str,
        phase_id: PhaseId | None = None,
    ) -> list[AuditEvent]:
        """Query audit events for an epoch. ACTIVITY-ONLY — do not call from workflow context."""
        return await self._trail.query_events(epoch_id=epoch_id, phase_id=phase_id)
```

Worker registration:
```python
audit = AuditActivities(trail=InMemoryAuditTrail())
worker = Worker(client, task_queue='aura', activities=[audit.query_audit_events])
```

Workflow call:
```python
result = await workflow.execute_activity(
    AuditActivities.query_audit_events,
    args=[self._epoch_id, PhaseId.P4_REVIEW],
    schedule_to_close_timeout=timedelta(seconds=30),
)
```

## FIX-3 (B-1 MUST FIX): ChildWorkflowHandle retained for signal routing

### Problem
PROPOSAL-7 routed signals to child workflows via `workflow.get_external_workflow_handle(child_id).signal()`. This raises `WorkflowNotFoundError` if the child has already completed — a race condition that would fail the parent workflow silently.

### Fix
Retain the `ChildWorkflowHandle` from `start_child_workflow`. This handle knows the child's completion state and provides typed signal routing without re-lookup:

```python
# In EpochWorkflow.run():
child_handle: ChildWorkflowHandle[PhaseResult] = await workflow.start_child_workflow(
    ReviewPhaseWorkflow.run,
    PhaseInput(epoch_id=self._epoch_id, phase_id=PhaseId.P4_REVIEW),
    id=f'{self._epoch_id}-p4',
)

# Route a vote signal to the child:
await child_handle.signal(ReviewPhaseWorkflow.submit_vote, vote_signal)

# Await completion (blocking join — parent suspends until child returns PhaseResult):
result: PhaseResult = await child_handle
```

**Child workflow join semantics (explicit):**
- `start_child_workflow` registers the child and returns a handle immediately (non-blocking).
- `await child_handle` is the blocking join — parent suspends here until child workflow completes and returns `PhaseResult`.
- Child independently registers signal handlers (via class-level `@workflow.signal` decorators — see FIX-4) and awaits via `wait_condition` predicate.
- Signaling a completed child raises `ChildWorkflowError` from the handle; wrap in try/except if votes can arrive after child completes.

## FIX-4 (A-1 SHOULD FIX): Class-level @workflow.signal for signal buffering

Child workflows (ReviewPhaseWorkflow, SliceWorkflow) MUST use class-level `@workflow.signal` decorators — NOT imperative handler registration inside `run()`.

```python
class ReviewPhaseWorkflow:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._votes: dict[str, VoteType] = {}

    @workflow.signal
    def submit_vote(self, signal: ReviewVoteSignal) -> None:
        self._votes[signal.axis] = signal.vote

    @workflow.run
    async def run(self, input: PhaseInput) -> PhaseResult:
        # wait_condition: predicate gate — NOT a queue drain
        await workflow.wait_condition(
            lambda: all(ax in self._votes for ax in ('A', 'B', 'C'))
        )
        vote_result = VoteType.ACCEPT if all(
            v == VoteType.ACCEPT for v in self._votes.values()
        ) else VoteType.REVISE
        ...
```

Rationale: Temporal buffers signals sent before the first workflow task executes, but ONLY if the handler is registered at class definition time (via decorator). Imperative handlers miss signals that arrive during startup latency.

## FIX-1 (A-1 MUST FIX): workflow.execute_activity_method() for typed dispatch

### Problem
PROPOSAL-8 used `workflow.execute_activity(AuditActivities.query_audit_events, ...)`. The Temporal Python SDK has a distinct, typed API for class-method activities: `workflow.execute_activity_method()`. Using the untyped form violates the project guideline to prefer strongly-typed APIs over stringly-typed dispatch.

Note: B-1 confirmed via SDK source that both forms resolve the activity name correctly (from_callable handles bound methods). This is a type-safety fix, not a correctness fix — but the typed API is the right choice per project conventions.

### Fix
```python
result = await workflow.execute_activity_method(
    AuditActivities.query_audit_events,
    args=[epoch_id, phase_id],
    start_to_close_timeout=timedelta(seconds=30),
)
```

## FIX-2 (A-1 + B-1 MUST FIX): try/except around child_handle.signal()

### Problem
`ChildWorkflowHandle.signal()` raises `ApplicationError` (via `FailureError`) if the child workflow has already completed. Confirmed by B-1 via SDK trace: `_apply_resolve_signal_external_workflow` calls `fut.set_exception()` when the server returns a failure for a closed workflow. PROPOSAL-8 showed no error handling.

### Fix
```python
try:
    await child_handle.signal(ReviewPhaseWorkflow.submit_vote, vote_signal)
except temporalio.exceptions.ApplicationError:
    pass  # child already completed — vote signal not needed
```

This covers the timing race: child completes (all votes received + wait_condition fires) between when the parent decided to re-signal and when the signal is processed.

## FIX-3 (B-1 MUST FIX): Prohibit asyncio.gather for parallel child workflows

### Problem
PROPOSAL-8 mentioned P9_SLICE executes slices in parallel but did not specify the concurrency primitive. Any implementation using `asyncio.gather` is INCORRECT in Temporal workflow code — `asyncio.gather` uses a non-deterministic scheduler order that differs between original execution and replay, causing nondeterminism errors. The Temporal sandbox does not replace or intercept `asyncio.gather`.

### Fix
Parallel child workflows MUST use `workflow.wait()` or `workflow.as_completed()` — the SDK-provided deterministic replacements.

Correct pattern for parallel P9_SLICE execution:
```python
# Start all slice child workflows
handles = [
    await workflow.start_child_workflow(
        SliceWorkflow.run,
        SliceInput(epoch_id=self._epoch_id, slice_id=s.id),
        id=f'{self._epoch_id}-{s.id}',
    )
    for s in slices
]

# Await all completions deterministically
done, _ = await workflow.wait(set(handles))
results: list[SliceResult] = [h.result() for h in done]
```

DO NOT use: ~~`asyncio.gather(*handles)`~~ — non-deterministic replay.

## FIX-4 (A-1 + B-1 MUST FIX): ReviewAxis(StrEnum) for vote tracking

### Problem
PROPOSAL-8 showed:
```python
_votes: dict[str, VoteType] = {}
await workflow.wait_condition(lambda: all(ax in self._votes for ax in ('A', 'B', 'C')))
```

Raw string literals violate the project's strongly-typed enum guideline. If axes change or expand, the predicate silently becomes wrong. Also, `ReviewVoteSignal.axis: str` is stringly-typed at the signal boundary.

### Fix
Introduce `ReviewAxis(StrEnum)` (or confirm it already exists in types.py — check and use if present):

```python
class ReviewAxis(StrEnum):
    A = 'A'  # End-user alignment
    B = 'B'  # Temporal concurrency
    C = 'C'  # Interface design

class ReviewVoteSignal:
    axis: ReviewAxis  # was: str

class ReviewPhaseWorkflow:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._votes: dict[ReviewAxis, VoteType] = {}

    @workflow.signal
    def submit_vote(self, signal: ReviewVoteSignal) -> None:
        self._votes[signal.axis] = signal.vote

    @workflow.run
    async def run(self, input: PhaseInput) -> PhaseResult:
        # Predicate: all 3 axes have voted — exhaustive, enum-safe
        await workflow.wait_condition(
            lambda: all(ax in self._votes for ax in ReviewAxis)
        )
```

This is exhaustive (iterates over all enum members), self-documenting, and correct when axes are added.

### Problem

```python
# state_machine.py
_CONSENSUS_GATED: frozenset[tuple[PhaseId, PhaseId]] = frozenset({...})
_BLOCKER_GATED: frozenset[tuple[PhaseId, PhaseId]] = frozenset({...})

`AuditActivities.query_audit_events` error handling:

- **Permanent failures** (epoch not found, invalid query, schema mismatch): raise `ApplicationError('reason', non_retryable=True)` inside the activity. This immediately marks the activity as failed without retrying.

```python
from temporalio.exceptions import ApplicationError

async def query_audit_events(self, epoch_id: str, phase: PhaseId | None = None) -> list[AuditEvent]:
    try:
        return await self._trail.query_events(epoch_id=epoch_id, phase=phase)

PROPOSAL-9 FIX-7 proposed `tool_call_id: str = ''`. Empty string is semantically ambiguous: in MCP protocol, tool_call_id is a mandatory correlation identifier.     tool_call_id: str | None = None         # new in v3; None for v2-origin records

## FIX-3 (C-1 SHOULD FIX): AuditTrail.query_events epoch_id optionality — documented design decision

### Problem
`AuditTrail.query_events` makes `epoch_id: str | None = None` (optional), but the `query_audit_events` activity wrapper makes `epoch_id: str` required (non-optional). A consumer using the Protocol directly can issue cross-epoch queries that the activity disallows. This optionality mismatch is a learnable API confusion.

### Decision
Keep `epoch_id` optional in the Protocol to allow cross-epoch queries as an advanced use case (scripts, admin tooling, tests). The activity wrapper makes it required because workflows always have an epoch_id — they should never issue unbounded cross-epoch queries in a running workflow.

Document this intent explicitly in the Protocol:

```python
async def query_events(
    self,
    *,
    epoch_id: str | None = None,
    phase: PhaseId | None = None,
    role: RoleId | None = None,
) -> list[AuditEvent]:
    """Query recorded audit events with optional filters.

    Args:
        epoch_id: Optional epoch filter. None = cross-epoch (advanced/admin use only).
                  Workflows MUST always provide epoch_id via the query_audit_events activity.
        phase:    Optional phase filter.
        role:     Optional role filter.
    """
```

**Topology:** Hybrid — sequential phases as activities in EpochWorkflow; P4_REVIEW, P9_SLICE, P10_CODE_REVIEW as child workflows.

    to_phase: PhaseId
    condition: str
    action: str | None = None

@dataclass(frozen=True)

    id: PhaseId; number: int; domain: Domain; name: str

    epoch_id: str

    phase_id: PhaseId
    success: bool
    blocker_count: int = 0
    vote_result: VoteType | None = None

    return await _AUDIT_TRAIL.query_events(epoch_id=epoch_id, phase=phase)

## Gap
In audit_activities.py:
- Activity signature is: query_audit_events(epoch_id: str, phase: PhaseId | None = None)
- Missing: role: RoleId | None = None parameter
- The delegation call: await _AUDIT_TRAIL.query_events(epoch_id=epoch_id, phase=phase)
- Missing: role=role kwarg

The AuditTrail Protocol defines:
  async def query_events(self, *, epoch_id: str | None = None, phase: PhaseId | None = None, role: RoleId | None = None) -> list[AuditEvent]

## Fix Required
1. Add role: RoleId | None = None to query_audit_events signature
2. Forward role=role in the _AUDIT_TRAIL.query_events() call
3. Update any callers and tests accordingly

## Rationale
Without the role filter, queries that scope to a specific agent role (e.g. 'show only SUPERVISOR audit events for this epoch') silently return unfiltered results. This is a silent correctness failure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- query_audit_events activity accepts role: RoleId | None = None
- Delegation call passes role=role to _AUDIT_TRAIL.query_events()
- Test: query_audit_events with role filter returns only role-matching events
- No regressions in existing tests","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"dayvidpham@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-02-26T20:53:36Z","created_by":"David Huu Pham","updated_at":"2026-02-26T20:53:36Z"}

## Critical Gap
workflow.py contains only EpochWorkflow. The following child workflow classes are entirely absent:

### SliceWorkflow
- @workflow.defn class
- Accepts SliceInput (dataclass with epoch_id, slice_id, phase_spec: SerializablePhaseSpec)
- Executes slice activities (or stubs with R12 docstrings for now)
- Returns SliceResult (or PhaseResult)
- Fail-fast: EpochWorkflow must use workflow.wait(slice_handles, return_when=FIRST_EXCEPTION)
  and cancel remaining handles on first exception

### ReviewPhaseWorkflow
- @workflow.defn class
- Accepts ReviewInput (dataclass)
- @workflow.signal handler for ReviewVoteSignal (axis: ReviewAxis)
- wait_condition until all 3 ReviewAxis members have voted (using ReviewAxis enum members)
- try/except ApplicationError around child_handle.signal() calls (race protection)
- Returns PhaseResult with vote_result

### EpochWorkflow Integration
- P9_SLICE: start N SliceWorkflow children, then workflow.wait(handles, return_when=FIRST_EXCEPTION)
  On first exception: cancel pending handles, propagate
- P10_CODE_REVIEW: start ReviewPhaseWorkflow children; wait for completion

## Acceptance Criteria
- SliceWorkflow class exists with @workflow.defn
- ReviewPhaseWorkflow class exists with @workflow.defn + @workflow.signal for ReviewVoteSignal
- EpochWorkflow.p9_slice_phase() uses workflow.wait(FIRST_EXCEPTION) + cancel-on-failure
- EpochWorkflow.p10_review_phase() starts ReviewPhaseWorkflow child(ren) and waits
- asyncio.gather NEVER used — only workflow.wait()
- Tests: fail-fast behavior verified; signal routing verified
- No regressions in existing tests","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"dayvidpham@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-02-26T20:53:52Z","created_by":"David Huu Pham","updated_at":"2026-02-26T20:53:52Z"}

## Finding

TestP9SliceFailFastPattern (test_workflow.py:1160) tests the raw asyncio.wait(FIRST_EXCEPTION) semantic directly using plain asyncio coroutines:

```python
class TestP9SliceFailFastPattern:
    """Tests the asyncio pattern that the P9 supervisor uses to run parallel slices
    and cancel remaining slices on first failure. This tests the PATTERN — not an
    actual P9 Temporal workflow..."""

    async def test_first_exception_returns_on_first_failure(self) -> None:
        async def fast_fail() -> None:
            raise RuntimeError("Slice 0 failed with BLOCKER")

        async def long_slice() -> None:
            await asyncio.sleep(100)

        tasks = [
            asyncio.create_task(fast_fail(), name="fast-fail"),
            asyncio.create_task(long_slice(), name="long-slice"),
        ]
        done, pending = await asyncio.wait(tasks, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_EXCEPTION)
        ...
```

The test class docstring explicitly acknowledges it tests the "PATTERN — not an actual P9 Temporal workflow".

The production method EpochWorkflow._run_p9_slices() (workflow.py:454) wraps child workflow handles, not plain asyncio.Tasks. While ChildWorkflowHandle is awaitable, the actual integration (start_child_workflow, then asyncio.wait on handles) is untested.

## Why It Matters

The fail-fast semantic is a correctness requirement from the URD (aura-plugins-cz2t description: "asyncio.gather NEVER used — only workflow.wait()"). Testing only the raw pattern misses a production code path: that start_child_workflow handles behave as asyncio-awaitable tasks when passed to asyncio.wait. A subtle Temporal SDK behavior change could break this without test failure.

The existing sandbox tests (TestWorkflowEnvironmentSandbox) are skipped because they require a running Temporal server (4 skipped). There is no path that exercises _run_p9_slices() end-to-end in CI.

## What Would Be Better

A structural test that calls _run_p9_slices() with SliceInput lists and verifies the fail-fast pattern via the actual method, using a DI-friendly stub for SliceWorkflow (per R12 docstring pattern), without requiring a Temporal server.

Alternatively, the existing pattern tests are acceptable as a first-pass and the gap is documented. The tests that do exist (structural invariants, signal logic) are well-written.

## Not a Blocker Because

- The asyncio pattern tests verify the control-flow semantics
- This is a test coverage gap, not a correctness failure","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"dayvidpham@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-02-26T23:47:15Z","created_by":"David Huu Pham","updated_at":"2026-02-26T23:47:15Z"}

{"id":"aura-plugins-cz2t","title":"IMPLEMENT: SliceWorkflow + ReviewPhaseWorkflow child workflow classes (fail-fast P9_SLICE)","description":"The supervisor implemented EpochWorkflow correctly but did not implement the two child workflow classes required by the ratified PROPOSAL-11 design.

## Critical Gap
workflow.py contains only EpochWorkflow. The following child workflow classes are entirely absent:
- SliceWorkflow: Represents a single P9_SLICE; runs concurrently with other SliceWorkflows
- ReviewPhaseWorkflow: Represents P10_CODE_REVIEW for a slice; receives ReviewAxis votes via signals

## Requirements (from PROPOSAL-11 / HANDOFF aura-plugins-6zro)

### SliceWorkflow
- @workflow.defn class
- Accepts SliceInput (dataclass with epoch_id, slice_id, phase_spec: SerializablePhaseSpec)
- Executes slice activities (or stubs with R12 docstrings for now)
- Returns SliceResult (or PhaseResult)
- Fail-fast: EpochWorkflow must use workflow.wait(slice_handles, return_when=FIRST_EXCEPTION)
  and cancel remaining handles on first exception

### ReviewPhaseWorkflow
- @workflow.defn class
- Accepts ReviewInput (dataclass)
- @workflow.signal handler for ReviewVoteSignal (axis: ReviewAxis)
- wait_condition until all 3 ReviewAxis members have voted (using ReviewAxis enum members)
- try/except ApplicationError around child_handle.signal() calls (race protection)
- Returns PhaseResult with vote_result

### EpochWorkflow Integration
- P9_SLICE: start N SliceWorkflow children, then workflow.wait(handles, return_when=FIRST_EXCEPTION)
  On first exception: cancel pending handles, propagate
- P10_CODE_REVIEW: start ReviewPhaseWorkflow children; wait for completion

## Acceptance Criteria
- SliceWorkflow class exists with @workflow.defn
- ReviewPhaseWorkflow class exists with @workflow.defn + @workflow.signal for ReviewVoteSignal
- EpochWorkflow.p9_slice_phase() uses workflow.wait(FIRST_EXCEPTION) + cancel-on-failure
- EpochWorkflow.p10_review_phase() starts ReviewPhaseWorkflow child(ren) and waits
- asyncio.gather NEVER used — only workflow.wait()
- Tests: fail-fast behavior verified; signal routing verified
- No regressions in existing tests","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"dayvidpham@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-02-26T20:53:52Z","created_by":"David Huu Pham","updated_at":"2026-02-26T23:39:16Z"}

{"id":"aura-plugins-oyxw","title":"FIX: query_audit_events drops role filter — add role: RoleId | None to activity","description":"The query_audit_events activity (audit_activities.py) does not forward the role parameter to AuditTrail.query_events even though the Protocol interface supports it.

## Gap
In audit_activities.py:
- Activity signature is: query_audit_events(epoch_id: str, phase: PhaseId | None = None)
- Missing: role: RoleId | None = None parameter
- The delegation call: await _AUDIT_TRAIL.query_events(epoch_id=epoch_id, phase=phase)
- Missing: role=role kwarg

The AuditTrail Protocol defines:
  async def query_events(self, *, epoch_id: str | None = None, phase: PhaseId | None = None, role: RoleId | None = None) -> list[AuditEvent]

## Fix Required
1. Add role: RoleId | None = None to query_audit_events signature
2. Forward role=role in the _AUDIT_TRAIL.query_events() call
3. Update any callers and tests accordingly

## Rationale
Without the role filter, queries that scope to a specific agent role (e.g. 'show only SUPERVISOR audit events for this epoch') silently return unfiltered results. This is a silent correctness failure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- query_audit_events activity accepts role: RoleId | None = None
- Delegation call passes role=role to _AUDIT_TRAIL.query_events()
- Test: query_audit_events with role filter returns only role-matching events
- No regressions in existing tests","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"dayvidpham@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-02-26T20:53:36Z","created_by":"David Huu Pham","updated_at":"2026-02-26T23:39:16Z"}

  @dataclass

      ...
      review_votes: dict[str, VoteType] = field(default_factory=dict)

Should be:
  review_votes: dict[ReviewAxis, VoteType] = field(default_factory=dict)

## Why This Matters
PROPOSAL-9 introduced ReviewAxis(StrEnum) specifically to replace raw str keys in vote tracking.
PROPOSAL-10 fixed ReviewVoteSignal.axis: str → ReviewAxis.

Because ReviewAxis is a StrEnum, dict[ReviewAxis, VoteType] is backward-compatible at runtime
(StrEnum values are strings), but mypy/pyright will catch misuse at development time.

2. Update all dict assignments: self._state.review_votes[signal.axis] = signal.vote

3. Update tests to use ReviewAxis.CORRECTNESS etc. as keys

- All assignments use ReviewAxis enum members as keys

## Review Axis: A (Correctness), Round 2

### Methodology

Reviewed PROPOSAL-2 (aura-plugins-fl5p) against:
1. Actual RuntimeConstraintChecker method signatures in constraints.py (all 20 check_*() methods)
2. Actual ConstraintViolationTestCase dataclass in fixture_loader.py (line 114-147)
3. Actual test dispatch logic in test_protocol_combinatorial.py (lines 515-539)
4. Actual EpochState / TransitionRecord definitions in state_machine.py (lines 36-74)
5. Actual check_audit_trail method (lines 652-719) and check_blocker_gate (lines 626-650)
6. Every proposed violation_args dict against its corresponding method parameter names and types

---

### Round 1 Finding Resolution

#### BLOCKER (A+B): C-blocker-dual-parent kwarg fixed

Round 1 found: violation_args used followup_slice_id but method signature has slice_id.

PROPOSAL-2 YAML:
  violation_args: { blocker_task_id: "leaf-1", severity_group_id: "", slice_id: "slice-1" }

Actual signature (constraints.py:782-786):
  def check_blocker_dual_parent(self, blocker_task_id: str, severity_group_id: str, slice_id: str)

**VERIFIED CORRECT.** All three kwargs match. Empty severity_group_id triggers the expected violation.

#### Structural (C): Removed _coerce_violation_args

Replaced with single inline coercion in fixture loader:
  if "phase" in raw_args and isinstance(raw_args["phase"], str):
      raw_args["phase"] = PhaseId(raw_args["phase"])

**VERIFIED CORRECT.** See PhaseId coercion sufficiency analysis below.

#### Structural (C): Removed _factory — audit constraints use violation_state with transition_history

C-audit-never-delete and C-audit-dep-chain now use violation_state YAML (the existing code path), extended with optional transition_history list. No separate _factory dispatch mechanism.

**VERIFIED CORRECT.** See detailed analysis below.

---

### Verification 1: All 20 violation_method + violation_args Match Method Signatures

Each entry verified against actual method signatures in constraints.py.

**15 structural constraints:**

1. C-review-binary: check_review_binary(vote="MAYBE")
   Signature: (self, vote: str) — CORRECT

2. C-dep-direction: check_dep_direction(parent_id="", child_id="child-abc")
   Signature: (self, parent_id: str, child_id: str) — CORRECT

3. C-blocker-dual-parent: check_blocker_dual_parent(blocker_task_id="leaf-1", severity_group_id="", slice_id="slice-1")
   Signature: (self, blocker_task_id: str, severity_group_id: str, slice_id: str) — CORRECT

4. C-followup-timing: check_followup_timing(has_important_or_minor=true, followup_created=false)
   Signature: (self, has_important_or_minor: bool, followup_created: bool) — CORRECT

5. C-vertical-slices: check_vertical_slices(production_code_path="src/module.py", owner_ids=["worker-1", "worker-2"])
   Signature: (self, production_code_path: str, owner_ids: list[str]) — CORRECT

**Result: All 20 violation_method + violation_args entries match their method signatures exactly. Zero kwarg mismatches.**

---

### Verification 2: Audit Constraint transition_history Extension

**C-audit-never-delete:**
YAML: violation_state with current_phase: p2, no transition_history key.
Fixture loader: transition_history defaults to empty list in EpochState (default_factory=list).
check_audit_trail (line 664-668): state.current_phase != P1_REQUEST and not state.transition_history -> fires C-audit-never-delete.
**CORRECT.** P2 with empty history fires the expected violation.

**C-audit-dep-chain:**
YAML: violation_state with current_phase: p2, transition_history containing one record with triggered_by: "".
Fixture loader: constructs TransitionRecord(from_phase=PhaseId("p1"), to_phase=PhaseId("p2"), triggered_by="", condition_met="classification confirmed", timestamp=datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc)).
TransitionRecord dataclass (state_machine.py:56-74): has fields from_phase, to_phase, timestamp, triggered_by, condition_met, success=True. All provided. success defaults to True (correct for a valid transition).
check_audit_trail (line 685-701): iterates records, checks if not record.triggered_by — empty string is falsy, fires C-audit-dep-chain.
Isolation: transition_history is non-empty (one record), so C-audit-never-delete does NOT co-fire.
**CORRECT.** Both constraints independently testable without co-firing.

The post-construction approach state.transition_history.extend(transition_history) is correct because EpochState.transition_history uses field(default_factory=list) — a mutable list.

---

### Verification 3: PhaseId Coercion Sufficiency

The single inline coercion handles phase: str -> PhaseId. Scanning all 20 violation_args entries:

- C-supervisor-cartographers: phase="p8" -> PhaseId.P8_IMPL_PLAN — NEEDS coercion, COVERED
- All other entries: str, bool, int, list[str] only — natively handled by YAML parsing

No other violation_method takes PhaseId in its args. (check_state and check_transition take PhaseId but route through different dispatch paths, not violation_method.)

**CORRECT.** PhaseId coercion for check_supervisor_cartographers is the only needed coercion.

---

### NOTE: C-worker-gates Duplicate Key Concern

The proposal lists C-worker-gates in the "15 constraints — use check_structural as violation_method" group. However, C-worker-gates is NOT one of the 21 skipped constraints — it is one of the 5 existing RUNNABLE constraints (protocol.yaml line 704-712, uses violation_state with blocker_count: 1 at p10, testing check_blocker_gate).

If the implementer adds a second C-worker-gates entry with violation_method: check_worker_gates, YAML will silently overwrite the first — losing the blocker_count state-based test. The correct count for the structural group should be 14, not 15. The proposal's validation checklist claims "5 existing runnable constraint tests still pass" but including C-worker-gates in the new entries would replace one of those 5.

This is NOT a BLOCKER because:
- Both check_blocker_gate and check_worker_gates emit constraint_id="C-worker-gates", so the test assertion still passes
- The blocker_count behavior is tested elsewhere (transition tests, check_transition)
- The implementer will likely notice the YAML duplicate during implementation

However, for the proposal to be internally consistent: the structural group should list 14 entries (removing C-worker-gates), and the total new entries should be 2 audit + 14 structural + 4 naming = 20 (matching the 20 un-skipped from 21).

---

### End-User Alignment

1. **End-users:** Developers running the test suite
2. **What they want:** All tests pass, no false skips, reliable CI
3. **Impact:** 20 formerly-skipped tests become passing, 2 new state-based audit tests pass, 1 remains documented skipped
4. **Implementation gaps:** C-worker-gates duplicate key is discoverable during implementation
5. **MVP scope:** Appropriate — test infrastructure only, no production code changes
6. **Validation checklist:** Complete and verifiable, with the C-worker-gates counting note above

---

## VOTE: ACCEPT

All four correctness verification items pass:

1. C-blocker-dual-parent kwarg fix: slice_id matches method signature exactly — VERIFIED
2. All 20 violation_method + violation_args entries: zero kwarg mismatches against actual method signatures — VERIFIED
3. transition_history extension for audit constraints: correctly triggers expected violations without co-firing — VERIFIED
4. PhaseId coercion: only needed for check_supervisor_cartographers(phase="p8"), correctly implemented — VERIFIED

The C-worker-gates counting note is an implementation-time discovery, not a design correctness issue. The Round 1 BLOCKER is resolved. The proposal is correct."}

## Specification

Extend gen_schema.py to emit new XML sections from types.py canonical dicts, and extend schema_parser.py to parse them back into typed Python objects. Full XML round-trip for all new entities.

### gen_schema.py Changes

#### New child elements under existing sections:
- <example> children under <constraint> with CDATA content (id, lang, label, also-illustrates attrs)
- <example> children under <step> (procedure steps) with CDATA content
- <introduction> child under <role> (text content)
- <ownership-narrative> child under <role> (text content)
- <behaviors>/<behavior> children under <role> (id, given, when, then, should-not attrs)
- command attribute on <constraint> elements (where applicable)

#### New top-level sections:
- <checklists>/<checklist> (role-ref, gate attrs) → <item> children (id, required, text)
- <coordination-commands>/<coord-cmd> (id, action, template, role-ref?, shared? attrs)
- <workflows>/<workflow> (id, name, role-ref, description) → <stage> children → <action> + <exit-condition> children

### schema_parser.py Changes

#### New parse functions:
- _parse_examples(parent_elem) → tuple[CodeExample, ...]
- _parse_behaviors(role_elem) → tuple[BehaviorSpec, ...]
- _parse_checklists(root) → dict[str, Checklist]
- _parse_coordination_commands(root) → dict[str, CoordinationCommand]
- _parse_workflows(root) → dict[str, Workflow]

#### SchemaSpec extensions:
- Add fields: checklists, coordination_commands, workflows
- Extend _parse_roles to extract introduction, ownership_narrative, behaviors
- Extend _parse_constraints to extract command, examples
- Extend _parse_procedure_steps to extract examples

### Key patterns from Cartographer A findings:
- gen_schema.py: _build_* functions take root ET.Element, read canonical dicts, emit via ET.SubElement
- schema_parser.py: _parse_* functions take root + path, extract attrs via _require(), return typed objects
- CDATA for code examples (DocBook pattern) — use xml.etree CDATA handling
- Follow existing function naming: _build_kebab_case() / _parse_kebab_case()

## Files Owned
- scripts/aura_protocol/gen_schema.py
- scripts/aura_protocol/schema_parser.py

## Acceptance Criteria
Given types.py with new canonical dicts when running gen_schema then schema.xml contains new sections (checklists, coordination-commands, workflows) and child elements (example, introduction, ownership-narrative, behaviors) should never break existing schema.xml structure

Given schema.xml with new elements when running schema_parser then SchemaSpec contains parsed checklists, coordination_commands, workflows, and extended roles/constraints/steps should never lose any existing parsed data

Given code examples in CDATA when parsing then raw code content preserved without XML escaping should never mangle code content

- [ ] gen_schema.py emits <workflows> top-level section
