# FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-1 — Native Codex distribution from Pasture

## Outcome

Pasture becomes the single compiler and artifact owner for Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex. It emits an installable Codex plugin containing namespaced skills, native Codex instructions, UI metadata, and one canonical, hash-addressed native-agent bundle. The existing Pasture CLI performs explicit transactional agent installation. Aura publishes the aggregate Codex marketplace entry and may opt into Home Manager ownership of those exact agent files.

The product claim remains deliberately precise: installing the plugin installs skills; invoking the explicit setup workflow or enabling Home Manager installs native custom agents. Codex currently has no supported plugin agent component.

## Problem shape

- Parallelism: the feature has four implementation slices after an interface-first foundation. Generated-artifact and release work share contracts and must be sequenced; Aura consumption follows the Pasture artifact contract.
- Distribution: two repositories and two independent Codex loaders. Plugins load skills; project/user TOML files load agents.
- Integrity: generated developer instructions are privileged workflow code. Namespace collisions, mutable Git references, partial writes, or stale agents can cause unintended behavior.
- Compatibility: canonical bodies currently encode Claude operations and models in every spec family. A manifest-only target would install but behave incorrectly.
- Lifecycle: companion, Home Manager, and future project installation cannot safely co-own the same agent names.
- Cost/frequency: generation occurs during development and release; agent install/status/uninstall are user operations. Determinism and actionable failure matter more than micro-optimization.

## Architecture

### A. Explicit generation roots

Adopt and resolve aura-plugins-oj7we rather than duplicating it:

    type GenerationRoots struct {
        SourceRoot string
        OutputRoot string
    }

Verbatim/canonical inputs always resolve beneath SourceRoot. Every generated write is proven beneath OutputRoot. The CLI keeps repository-root defaults and supports isolated output for tests, plugin smoke, and downstream consumers. Attempts to escape either root fail with what/why/where/when/impact/fix diagnostics.

### B. Typed runtime compiler

TargetHarness gains a RuntimeDialect. Runtime-sensitive canonical prose uses opaque typed references rather than raw harness syntax:

    type SkillKey string
    type SurfaceKind uint8
    type WorkTier uint8
    type AgentPurpose uint8
    type AgentLifetime uint8
    type DeliveryKind uint8
    type InputShape uint8

    type RuntimeContext struct {
        Harness HarnessName
        Surface SurfaceKind
        OwnerSkill SkillKey
        OwnerRole protocol.RoleId
        Location string
    }

    type RuntimeDialect interface {
        Render(RuntimeRef, RuntimeContext) (string, error)
    }

    func RT(parts ...any) string
    func CompileRuntimeText(text string, dialect RuntimeDialect, ctx RuntimeContext) (string, error)

RuntimeRef has private variants and typed constructors for:
- skill activation and invocation;
- agent spawn with purpose, lifetime, fan-out, and work tier;
- initial assignment, follow-up work, and notification;
- wait/barrier behavior;
- user input with callable-tool and direct-question fallback;
- instruction source, commit attribution, and repository capability.

A stable 31-entry SkillKey registry is the only runtime skill identity. CommandSpec.Name stays protocol/human metadata and cannot be transliterated into an invocation address.

A canonical visitor compiles every rendered string owner: SkillBody, ConstraintSpecs, WorkflowSpecs, ProcedureSteps, SharedFragmentSpecs, CommandSpec fields, and RoleSpec introductions/behaviors. Unknown references, invalid context combinations, raw forbidden operations, and uncompiled tokens fail generation with the canonical field location.

Dialect behavior:
- ClaudeDialect proves existing committed output byte-identical.
- OpenCode uses the seam but preserves its accepted output in this feature unless a shared correctness fix is separately demonstrated.
- CodexDialect emits namespaced $pasture:<skill> activation, collaboration primitives with the correct lifecycle semantics, mode-aware user input, inherited work-tier policy, Codex instruction paths, and neutral attribution.
- Self activation in an already active skill/agent is elided instead of becoming recursion.
- Initial TeamCreate plus assignment collapses into spawn_agent; fixes sent to an idle persistent worker use followup_task; notifications use send_message.
- swarm is not falsely translated. It remains an explicit compatibility skill that says it starts the Claude-backed aura-swarm; implicit invocation is disabled.

This is a compiler migration, not a raw replacement pass. Claude byte-stability is established before Codex generation is accepted.

### C. Codex TargetHarness and plugin

Add HarnessCodex to the existing static registry and EmitHarness pipeline.

Committed Pasture layout:

    plugins/pasture/
      .codex-plugin/plugin.json
      skills/
        <31 catalog-derived canonical skills>/
          SKILL.md
          agents/openai.yaml
          <required protocol/reference assets>
        install-codex-agents/
          SKILL.md
          agents/openai.yaml
          assets/agent-bundle/
            manifest.json
            agents/
              pasture-epoch.toml
              pasture-architect.toml
              pasture-supervisor.toml
              pasture-worker.toml
              pasture-reviewer.toml

There are 32 plugin skills: the registry-derived canonical set plus one Codex-only setup skill. Tests derive expected inventory from the registry rather than embedding a magic count as the source of truth.

SKILL.md frontmatter contains only unqualified name and description. Plugin namespace pasture yields effective $pasture:<skill> names. Every agents/openai.yaml entry has curated display_name, a 25–64 character short_description, exact default_prompt coverage of its effective name, and an invocation policy. install-codex-agents and swarm have allow_implicit_invocation=false. Protocol references and schema assets are recursively packaged and link-checked.

The rich plugin manifest is the common subset accepted by current Codex and the pinned plugin-creator validator. It includes version, author, skills, and interface metadata but no invented agents field, install hook, MCP server, or app.

### D. Canonical native-agent bundle

The five TOMLs are generated from RoleSpec plus the shared frontmatter-free, dialect-compiled role body. Target-local projection defines only:
- public names pasture_epoch, pasture_architect, pasture_supervisor, pasture_worker, pasture_reviewer;
- description;
- developer_instructions.

Optional model, model_reasoning_effort, sandbox_mode, MCP, and skills.config are omitted so the live parent policy remains authoritative. In particular, the reviewer must update Beads, so read-only is not a valid blanket default.

Each developer instruction starts with a plugin prerequisite: if required $pasture:* skills are unavailable, stop and report how to install/enable them. No agent uses a built-in name such as worker or explorer.

manifest.json includes:
- schema version;
- plugin/bundle full semver;
- minimum tested Codex version;
- canonical role ID and public name;
- safe relative filename;
- SHA-256 of exact TOML bytes;
- explicit inherited policy projection.

This skill-local asset bundle is the sole generated agent source. Home Manager consumes it directly; tests materialize it via the installer. There is no duplicate top-level .codex/agents tree.

### E. Transactional Pasture CLI lifecycle

Add:

    pasture codex agents plan --bundle <manifest>
    pasture codex agents install --bundle <manifest>
    pasture codex agents status
    pasture codex agents uninstall

Paths:
- target: CODEX_HOME/agents, default ~/.codex/agents;
- state: CODEX_HOME/pasture/agent-install.json;
- lock: CODEX_HOME/pasture/agent-install.lock;
- recoverable journal/staging: CODEX_HOME/pasture, never under the recursively scanned TOML tree.

Common preflight:
1. Resolve CODEX_HOME and every destination without traversal.
2. Parse the manifest and enforce supported schema/semver/minimum Codex.
3. Verify filenames, hashes, TOML syntax, role/public-name uniqueness, and exact bundle membership.
4. Recursively parse existing user/project agent TOMLs and detect duplicate public names, including alternate filenames.
5. Reject symlink targets/parents, unowned destination collisions, Home Manager ownership, mixed project/personal same-name layers, locally modified managed files, tampering, and implicit downgrade.
6. Produce an exact plan before any mutation.

plan performs zero writes, including no lock/ledger creation. install takes an exclusive lock, writes staged files on the same filesystem, atomically replaces the whole managed set with a recoverable journal/rollback strategy, writes the ledger last, and leaves the prior valid set recoverable on every injected failure point. An identical install is a true no-op that preserves bytes and mtimes. Explicit downgrade authorization is required.

The ledger records authority, schema, installed bundle version, role/public name, relative path, installed hash, and journal generation. status reports healthy, missing, modified, stale, unsupported, ownership conflict, plugin/agent version drift, and recoverable interrupted transaction. uninstall removes only ledger-owned files whose current hashes still match; modified and unowned files survive. It remains available after plugin removal because the implementation lives in the Pasture CLI.

All errors follow the actionable-error contract and identify operation, path/command, failure cause, caller impact, and concrete repair.

The setup skill has no implicit invocation. It resolves assets relative to its own directory, never constructs plugin-cache paths, checks pasture and codex, routes to $pasture:install-cli if Pasture is absent, runs and displays plan, requests scoped permission for the user-home mutation, invokes install, shows status, and tells the user to start a fresh Codex thread.

### F. Exclusive owner contract

For a given Codex home and generated role names:

    companion | home-manager | project

Exactly one may own the files.
- Companion owns regular files plus its ledger.
- Home Manager owns Nix symlinks and cleanup.
- Project mode would own repo .codex/agents and is outside MVP.
- Companion refuses Home Manager symlinks and project/personal same-name conflicts.
- Home Manager is opt-in, never force-overwrites, asserts the companion ledger/files are absent, and requires uninstall before switching.
- Aura does not sync Codex skills directly. Direct user skills would be unnamespaced duplicates of plugin skills and would break generated cross-skill addresses.
- Home Manager support is accepted only after a current Codex smoke proves loading and removal through symlinked TOMLs.

### G. Distribution, version, and drift ownership

Pasture owns plugins/pasture and the CLI. Aura owns the aggregate .agents/plugins/marketplace.json. The marketplace Pasture entry uses Git git-subdir for plugins/pasture and pins an immutable commit SHA or release tag; it never follows main and carries no invented version field.

The base release version remains canonical in Pasture's existing release metadata. Codegen derives both plugin.json version and bundle manifest version from it. pasture-release discovers/synchronizes both. Committed generated files contain no development cachebuster.

The feature branch is based on commit 8b4e04f from Pasture PR #35. Extend that existing CI design: make generate emits claude-code,opencode,codex and the existing dirty-tree check covers all committed targets. Do not add a duplicate drift job.

## Implementation decomposition

Foundation — generation roots and runtime compiler
- Owner: shared codegen contracts.
- Adopt aura-plugins-oj7we.
- Files: internal/codegen/harness.go and tests; tools/codegen/main.go; new runtime catalog/compiler/dialects/guards; canonical specs_data*.go migration; shared agent body renderer; docs/codegen.md and CONTRIBUTING.md.
- Exit: source/output isolation, compiler exhaustiveness, Claude byte stability, targeted Codex hotspot goldens, canonical lexical guard.

Slice 1 — Codex plugin and canonical skills
- Depends on Foundation.
- Owner: Codex TargetHarness, plugin manifest, skill templates, UI registry, recursive assets.
- Outputs 31 canonical skill trees and manifest.
- Exit: exact registry bijection, valid frontmatter/UI, all relative assets resolve, creator validation, isolated plugin install/list/invoke smoke.

Slice 2 — agent bundle, CLI lifecycle, and setup skill
- Depends on Foundation and extends Slice 1 UI registry.
- Owner: Codex TOML renderer, manifest/hashes, pasture codex agents commands, transactional filesystem core, setup skill.
- Outputs the canonical bundle and 32nd skill.
- Exit: full lifecycle/fault-injection suite, five namespaced agent load smoke, no built-in override, plugin install alone creates no agents.

Slice 3 — release sync and generate-all
- Depends on Slices 1–2 artifact/version contracts.
- Owner: internal/release, pasture-release tests/docs, Makefile generation aggregation, PR #35 drift integration.
- Exit: version parity, double-generation idempotence, no untracked output, all Pasture gates.

Slice 4 — Aura marketplace and Home Manager consumption
- Depends on the committed Pasture bundle contract.
- Owner: Aura .agents/plugins/marketplace.json, nix/hm-module.nix, module tests, README, Pasture submodule/flake lock pin.
- Installs only opt-in native agents from exact bundle files; publishes immutable plugin source.
- Exit: module eval and live isolated Codex symlink smoke, all Aura Nix gates.

No implementation worker may edit another slice's owned files without supervisor reassignment and an audit comment.

## Horizontal integration points

| Contract | Owner | Consumers | Merge timing |
|---|---|---|---|
| GenerationRoots | Foundation | every emitter, CLI, tests | first |
| SkillKey/RuntimeRef/RuntimeDialect | Foundation | plugin skills, agent bodies, guards | first |
| shared agent body | Foundation | Claude, OpenCode, Codex bundle | before Slice 2 |
| Codex UI registry | Slice 1 | all canonical skills, setup extension | Slice 1 then Slice 2 |
| canonical bundle manifest/bytes | Slice 2 | CLI, Home Manager, smoke tests | before Aura |
| full semver projection | Slice 3 | plugin and bundle | after artifact shapes settle |
| generate-all | Slice 3 | existing PR #35 drift gate | before Pasture PR |
| immutable Pasture revision | Pasture PR | Aura marketplace/submodule/flake input | before Aura PR |

## Validation and clean-review exit

Architecture and each implementation slice receive independent correctness, test-quality, and elegance/maintainability reviews. Any severity produces a revised proposal or implementation plus a new review round. Exit requires a fix-free round with zero BLOCKER, zero IMPORTANT, and zero MINOR across all three reviewers. Review effort is unlimited per the user's terminal directive.

Foundation/compiler tests:
- every ref kind × dialect × surface/render form;
- enum and catalog exhaustiveness/bijection;
- every generated directory maps to one SkillKey;
- self-invocation elision;
- spawn/follow-up/notification/barrier lifecycle goldens;
- callable input and direct-question fallback;
- full Claude output byte stability;
- Codex hotspot goldens for epoch, supervisor, architect-handoff, supervisor-spawn-worker, architect-request-review, user-request, user-elicit, and user-uat;
- all five agent TOML goldens;
- canonical and generated lexical guards with narrow fixture/compatibility allowlists;
- actionable location for unknown or uncompiled refs.

Plugin/bundle tests:
- creator validators run in a declared environment;
- exact, duplicate-free metadata registry;
- no double namespace or unsupported manifest agents field;
- all links/assets resolve;
- immutable version agreement;
- isolated current-Codex marketplace/plugin add/list/remove and skill discovery.

Installer tests:
- plan has zero writes;
- fresh install writes exactly five agents plus ledger outside agents;
- identical reinstall preserves mtimes;
- CODEX_HOME override leaves default home untouched;
- every collision, duplicate name, symlink, tamper, traversal, malformed TOML, modified file, ownership conflict, or downgrade refuses before mutation;
- injected failure at every mutation boundary restores/reports a recoverable prior state;
- upgrade and explicit downgrade;
- status drift;
- uninstall after plugin removal;
- uninstall preserves modified/unowned files;
- remaining agents fail actionably without plugin skills.

Pasture gates:
- make generate twice;
- make fmt;
- make lint;
- make test-race;
- make build;
- plugin-creator validation;
- skill-creator validation for every generated skill;
- isolated current-Codex smoke;
- intended git diff only.

Aura gates:
- focused Home Manager evaluation;
- isolated Codex symlink enable/load/disable/removal smoke;
- nix flake check --no-build;
- nix build .#aura-swarm --no-link;
- nix run .#aura-swarm -- --help;
- intended git diff only.

## BDD acceptance

1. Given canonical protocol specs, when all-target codegen runs twice, then Claude remains byte-identical, OpenCode remains accepted, Codex is native, and the second run is clean.
2. Given the generated plugin, when installed from Aura's immutable marketplace entry, then exactly the expected namespaced skills load and no native agent file is created.
3. Given the setup skill, when invoked with permission, then it displays a zero-write plan and transactionally installs the five namespaced agents from its verified bundle.
4. Given any preflight or injected mutation failure, when install runs, then no partial unusable agent set becomes authoritative and the diagnostic explains recovery.
5. Given an identical installed bundle, when install repeats, then no bytes or mtimes change.
6. Given user modifications or unowned files, when upgrade/uninstall runs, then those files are preserved and the operation reports the exact conflict.
7. Given companion ownership, when Home Manager is enabled, then evaluation fails actionably until companion uninstall; the inverse conflict is also refused.
8. Given Home Manager ownership, when enabled then disabled, then current Codex loads then removes all five symlinked roles without duplicate skills.
9. Given plugin removal while agents remain, when an agent starts, then it stops with an actionable missing-plugin prerequisite; pasture CLI uninstall still works.
10. Given a release change, when pasture-release and codegen run, then plugin and bundle full semver agree and no cachebuster enters committed output.
11. Given a review finding at any severity, when the loop runs, then it is fixed and a new fix-free 0/0/0 round is required before progression.
12. Given all gates and clean reviews, when delivery runs, then Pasture and Aura commits are pushed and evidence-backed pull requests are open.

## Tradeoffs

- Typed runtime tokens instead of Markdown AST: preserves existing canonical prose while making runtime-sensitive operations exhaustive and auditable.
- No raw post-render rewrite: topology, self-activation, and user-input semantics are context-dependent.
- One skill-local bundle instead of duplicate trees: eliminates byte/version drift and works inside plugin caching without depending on cache layout.
- Go CLI instead of model-directed copies or plugin Python: cross-platform, testable, recoverable, and available after plugin removal.
- Inherited agent policy instead of hardcoded model/sandbox: avoids stale model IDs and preserves Beads writes; live parent permissions remain explicit.
- Aura agents-only Home Manager support: avoids unnamespaced duplicate skills while retaining declarative lifecycle.
- Explicit Claude-backed swarm compatibility instead of omission: preserves a useful existing capability without falsely calling it Codex-native.
- Stacked immutable PR delivery: Pasture feature PR may target PR #35 while it remains open, then retarget main; Aura pins the published feature commit and declares Pasture-before-Aura merge order.

## Out of scope

- Invented plugin-native custom agent registration.
- Automatic SessionStart copying or uninstall hooks.
- Project-local agent export.
- A Codex backend for aura-swarm.
- Direct Aura Home Manager skill sync.
- Vercel skills CLI, oh-my-codex, npm packaging, ChatGPT-web native-agent claims.

# FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-2 — Native Codex distribution from Pasture

Supersedes Proposal 1. This revision incorporates every Round 1 finding: target-owned protocol/install assets, a default-depth root-orchestrated topology, versioned CLI bootstrap, a precise recoverable-directory transaction, personal-scope ownership, deterministic loader observables, one catalog/version writer, executable Home Manager activation checks, complete artifact inventories, and collision-free file ownership. URD Amendments 1 and 2 are normative.

## Product boundary

Pasture owns one compiler and every generated artifact. Its Codex plugin installs namespaced skills and carries a verified native-agent bundle. Codex does not currently install native custom agents from a plugin manifest, so users explicitly choose either the Pasture companion CLI or Aura Home Manager for personal agents.

Native agents are optional depth-1 leaf specializations. The plugin-only workflow is complete: the root thread runs Pasture role skills and may spawn built-in leaves whose self-contained prompts activate the exact `$pasture:<skill>`. No hidden home mutation or raised Codex delegation depth is required.

## 1. Roots and one skill catalog

Adopt `aura-plugins-oj7we` with `GenerationRoots{SourceRoot, OutputRoot}` and containment checks on every read/write. Replace `roleSkillDirs`, `commandSkillDirs`, `TargetHarness.Verbatim`, and mirrored inventories with one ordered `SkillDescriptor{Key, Directory, SourceKind, RoleID, CommandID}` catalog. All paths, runtime addresses, inventories, and target metadata project from it. Codex adds exactly one target support descriptor, `install-codex-agents`; its complete UI overlay is owned in one file. `ProtocolCommandName` and actionable `SkillInvocation` are separate typed values.

## 2. Structural runtime compiler and complete render graph

Use a closed structural value, never `...any` or opaque string reparsing:

```go
type RuntimeText struct { parts []RuntimePart }
type RuntimePart interface { runtimePart() }
type Literal struct { Text string }
type Ref struct { Value RuntimeRef }
func Text(parts ...RuntimePart) RuntimeText
func Lit(string) RuntimePart
func Runtime(RuntimeRef) RuntimePart
```

Private `RuntimeRef` variants cover skill activation/self-activation, agent purpose/delivery/lifetime/fan-out/work tier, initial/follow-up/notification/barrier, context/fork policy, user input fallback, commit policy, instruction source, and prerequisites. `RuntimeContext` carries harness, surface, owner descriptor/role, canonical location, and delivery capability.

Every production-template string owner is typed or explicitly classified: constraints, workflows, transitions, procedures, checklists, review axes, fragments, command and role fields, recipes/examples, figures, schema attributes, and normative external assets. A sentinel coverage test proves every field is visited. Unknown combinations, raw forbidden operations, and uncompiled parts fail with all six actionable-error fields.

Claude remains byte-identical except a separately golden-reviewed install capability addition. OpenCode keeps its exact path/byte inventory. Codex emits native operations and registry-derived `$pasture:<directory>` addresses. Every actionable archive address must resolve to one descriptor.

## 3. Target-owned protocol and installer skills

`protocol` and `install-cli` are not recursive Codex verbatim copies. Put the normative protocol source set behind the dialect-aware asset emitter: `SKILL.md`, `PROCESS.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CONSTRAINTS.md`, `SKILLS.md`, `README.md`, a harness-specific runtime document, and target-local `schema.xml`. Claude keeps existing names/bytes. Historical or Claude-specific examples remain in the Claude distribution and outside Codex active instruction links; any comparative Codex artifact needs a file/line/reason golden.

`InstallCLISpec` captures shared platform/binary/source semantics. Codex install-cli accepts the exact bundle release tag, never substitutes `latest`, downloads the published checksum manifest, verifies SHA-256 before activation, and labels immutable Go/Nix source-revision paths as development fallbacks.

Scan every Markdown, XML, YAML, JSON, and TOML file in the final plugin and link-walk the installed cache. Known `PROCESS.md`, install-cli, and schema hotspots are direct assertions; there is no blanket protocol exemption.

## 4. Default-depth orchestration and agent projection

Current Codex defaults `agents.max_depth=1`; Pasture keeps that recommended default. The root invokes `$pasture:epoch`, owns all phase transitions/consensus/waits/follow-ups, and directly spawns explorers, reviewers, and workers as depth-1 leaves. Architect and supervisor coordination runs as root role skills. A child `pasture_architect` or `pasture_supervisor` may produce a bounded artifact but never recursively spawns. `pasture_epoch` is a leaf analysis/status helper whose description directs full orchestration to the root skill; it is not advertised as a nested master.

`AgentDelivery` has two paths:

- plugin-only: built-in default/worker/explorer leaf plus a first-line exact Pasture skill directive;
- installed: healthy `pasture_*` leaf when the spawn surface exposes it, with redundant activation elided.

Unavailable custom types fall back to plugin-only. Self-contained Beads handoffs use no inherited conversation fork and list all task IDs. Follow-up work reuses the persistent leaf. Fan-out batches or serializes when `max_threads` is small.

The five target-local agent modes are honest: epoch analysis/root guidance; architect bounded requirements/proposal/handoff artifact; supervisor bounded implementation-plan/progress artifact; worker implementation/fix; reviewer review. Names are `pasture_epoch`, `pasture_architect`, `pasture_supervisor`, `pasture_worker`, and `pasture_reviewer`. Optional model/reasoning/sandbox/MCP/skill config is omitted so live parent policy wins.

## 5. Plugin and canonical bundle

Pasture emits `plugins/pasture/.codex-plugin/plugin.json` plus 31 catalog skills and `install-codex-agents`. Every skill has unqualified name/description frontmatter and exhaustive `agents/openai.yaml`; installed addresses are namespaced. `install-codex-agents` and the explicitly Claude-backed `swarm` set `allow_implicit_invocation=false`. The plugin manifest includes only the documented compatible skills/interface surface—never an agents field or install hook.

The setup skill owns one bundle at `assets/agent-bundle/{manifest.json,agents/pasture-*.toml}`. Its manifest carries bundle schema, installer protocol, plugin/bundle semver, exact compatible Pasture CLI release tag/semver, minimum/tested Codex versions, checksum artifact name, and each role/public-name/path/SHA-256/execution-policy projection. A committed file cannot contain its own commit SHA, so production bootstrap uses the release tag/checksums; development smoke injects a separately labeled source revision.

## 6. Public CLI and bootstrap contract

```text
pasture codex agents capabilities --format=json
pasture codex agents plan --bundle M [--project-root P|--no-project-check] --format=text|json
pasture codex agents install --bundle M --plan-digest D [--allow-downgrade] [project flags] --format=text|json
pasture codex agents status [--bundle M] [project flags] --format=text|json
pasture codex agents uninstall --format=text|json
```

`capabilities` reports CLI version, installer/bundle protocols, supported OS guarantees, and features. Bundle-less status reports local ledger/disk/interruption health; `--bundle` adds desired version/hash comparison. Optional plugin observation is explicitly unknown when unavailable and never reads cache paths. Stable JSON schemas and exit categories are black-box tested through the built Cobra binary.

`plan` is a zero-write snapshot. Its digest binds bundle, root identity, ledger/current generation, collisions, and options. `install` locks, recovers, reruns authoritative validation, and rejects a stale digest so the setup workflow can redisplay and ask again. Downgrade is an explicit audited flag.

The setup skill resolves its own bundle, verifies Codex and the exact Pasture installer capability, probes `bd`/Git/conditional repository commit policy and optional `aura-swarm`, invokes install-cli with the exact release when needed, shows plan, obtains scoped permission, installs, checks status, and requires a fresh thread. It never changes Git config or installs hooks. Landing uses `git agent-commit` when repository policy requires it and stops actionably if that required alias/command is absent; ordinary commit is allowed only by the active repository policy.

## 7. Recoverable managed-directory transaction

Threat model: untrusted bundle input, accidental corruption, crashes, and concurrent Pasture commands—not a privileged/malicious same-UID process continuously racing path replacement.

```text
CODEX_HOME/agents/pasture-managed/       complete loader-visible generation
CODEX_HOME/pasture/agent-install.json    committed ledger
CODEX_HOME/pasture/agent-install.lock    OS advisory lock
CODEX_HOME/pasture/transactions/<id>/    durable journal, staged new, old backup
```

Every mutation takes the same OS-released lock, recovers an old journal, and revalidates path components with lstat before each rename. The state machine stages/fsyncs a complete generation, journals `PREPARED`, renames the prior managed directory to a control-area backup and journals `OLD_MOVED`, renames the complete new directory into the loader tree and journals `NEW_ACTIVE`, atomically writes/fsyncs the generation ledger and journals `COMMITTED`, then cleans. Uninstall uses the same journal and moves the whole managed directory out before ledger removal.

The truthful guarantee is crash-recoverable quiescent installation: a concurrent Codex start may see the complete old set, a brief absence, or the complete new set, but never a mixed Pasture generation. Start a fresh thread only after healthy status. If recursive subdirectory loading or Linux/macOS rename semantics do not pass the pinned test, narrow the claim before shipping.

Identical install is a true no-op preserving mtimes. Modified managed content is never silently overwritten/deleted. Tests SIGKILL a real subprocess after every durable boundary, then recover; also cover two-process contention, persistent unheld lock file, stale consent, concurrent upgrade/uninstall/read, symlink/path swap, permissions, injected short write/ENOSPC, cleanup failure, first install, upgrade, explicit downgrade, no-op, and uninstall after plugin removal.

## 8. Enforceable ownership and Home Manager

Exclusive personal authority is companion XOR Home Manager for `CODEX_HOME/agents/pasture-managed`. Arbitrary project `.codex/agents` are higher-precedence Codex layers outside that algebra. `--project-root` scans only the explicitly resolved active project and reports/refuses same-name overrides; `--no-project-check` records the skipped check. No global project discovery is claimed.

Aura adds `CUSTOM.programs.aura-config-sync.codex.agents.enable = false` and no Codex skill sync. Nix evaluation parses the canonical bundle manifest, validates schema/version/safe unique paths/names and SHA-256, and derives file mappings without `roleNames`. A named `home.activation` step before link generation uses lstat to reject a companion ledger or regular managed directory with exact uninstall remediation. Companion symmetrically rejects Home Manager symlinks.

A pinned Home Manager fixture tests pure defaults/malformed manifests, then temporary-HOME activation for enable, repeat enable, conflict with zero mutation, upgrade, disable/removal, stale ledger, and preservation. Pinned Codex proves the symlink types load and disappear. Aura owns only default `~/.codex`; another `CODEX_HOME` is an independent companion target.

## 9. Version, inventories, and marketplace policy

`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` is the sole canonical version writer. Codegen derives Codex plugin/bundle values. `pasture-release` updates the canonical version then invokes/validates generation; it never independently rewrites generated siblings. This feature bumps the release minor and publishes SHA-256 binary checksums.

`make generate` emits `claude-code,opencode,codex` and extends PR #35's drift job. Empty-root generation compares exact recursive paths/bytes against every committed target. In-place generation records owned outputs and removes only previously recorded stale generated paths or fails actionably; a seeded stale path must be caught.

Aura appends Pasture after existing marketplace entries with name `pasture`, `git-subdir`, HTTPS Pasture URL, path `plugins/pasture`, and immutable 40-hex revision. Category is `Productivity`; authentication is `ON_INSTALL` per schema although no credential is required; products are omitted. Installation is `NOT_AVAILABLE` during stacked review and becomes `AVAILABLE` only after the matching checksummed release is reachable and the entry is repinned to its immutable release commit. Never use `INSTALLED_BY_DEFAULT` or mutable `main`.

## 10. Validation layers

Mandatory hermetic tests cover roots, the sole catalog, structural runtime parts and full visitor, dialects/invocations, manifests/TOML/hashes, whole-archive leakage/link walk, transaction/CLI black boxes, inventories/version/stale outputs, Home Manager evaluation/activation, and all six actionable-error fields.

A pinned Codex CLI compatibility test uses isolated `CODEX_HOME`, fresh processes, app-server `skills/list` and plugin list/read, plus a debug prompt/config observable for exact agent types. It proves plugin add creates zero agents, companion/HM expose five namespaced leaves without shadowing built-ins, and removal is exact. Network/model UAT is separate and demonstrates the default-depth root path, plugin-only fallback, installed selection, missing-plugin prerequisite, and setup permissions.

Repository Go validators are mandatory. Ambient skill-creator/plugin-creator scripts provide compatibility evidence with recorded hashes/versions; CI never depends on a contributor home.

## 11. Collision-free ownership and sequence

1. Foundation owns `GenerationRoots`, the catalog replacement, structural compiler/dialects, full canonical projection, target-aware protocol/install semantics, shared agent body, TargetHarness integration, and docs. No later slice edits these files.
2. Bundle-contract leaf freezes `pkg/codexbundle` serialization.
3. Codex distribution owns only `codex_*` files/tests/templates, the complete UI overlay, plugin/agent/bundle emitters, and generated plugin tree.
4. Agent CLI owns `internal/codexagents`, `cmd/pasture/codex_agents*`, and recovery/black-box tests while consuming the frozen bundle contract.
5. Release integration owns release packages/tests, Makefile, CI comments, checksum workflow/docs; it consumes emitters.
6. Aura owns marketplace, Home Manager module/fixture, README, input/lock, and Pasture gitlink; it consumes the frozen bundle.

One root implementor executes sequentially; exploration/review agents do not edit. Any newly shared file is reassigned in Beads before editing. Order: roots/catalog/runtime → bundle contract → Codex emitter and CLI → release/generate → immutable Pasture revision → Aura. PR #35 remains the base until merge. Pasture merges/releases before Aura becomes AVAILABLE.

## BDD acceptance

1. Default `max_depth=1` completes the epoch path through review, workers, and code review using only depth-1 leaves.
2. Healthy custom agents may be selected without duplicate activation; missing types fall back to built-ins.
3. All-target empty generation and in-place rerun match exact path/byte inventories with no stale output.
4. Every normative plugin file/link is valid, every actionable name resolves, and no unapproved Claude operation remains.
5. Fresh setup obtains/verifies the exact compatible CLI, reports prerequisites, shows a zero-write plan, binds consent to its digest, and never uses latest.
6. Crash at every durable boundary recovers to a complete generation or precise interrupted state; no mixed generation is reported healthy.
7. Concurrency, stale consent, collision, symlink, tamper, malformed TOML, modification, or unauthorized downgrade fails before commit with repair guidance.
8. Identical install preserves bytes and mtimes.
9. Home Manager conflict fails before link mutation; after companion uninstall, enable/load/disable/removal succeeds.
10. Project precedence is checked only for an explicit root or explicitly skipped; no global exclusivity claim remains.
11. Plugin removal leaves CLI status/uninstall functional and remaining agents stop actionably without skills.
12. One canonical release version regenerates equal plugin/bundle versions and checksums; Aura stays unavailable until release.
13. Any review finding causes a fix and new round; progression requires a fix-free three-axis 0/0/0 round.
14. After all clean gates, Pasture and Aura branches are pushed and evidence-backed PRs open with Pasture-before-Aura order.

## Out of scope

- Plugin-native agents or automatic install hooks.
- Raised-depth/nested Codex orchestration.
- Global arbitrary-project ownership or project export.
- Codex backend for aura-swarm.
- Aura Codex skill sync.
- Hook installation or Git configuration mutation.
- Vercel skills CLI, oh-my-codex, npm packaging, and ChatGPT-web local-agent claims.

Direct assertions cover known protocol, schema, and installer hotspots; there is no blanket support-skill exemption. Exact empty-root and in-place output manifests detect missing and stale owned paths.

## 3. Default-depth orchestration

The supported entry path is the root Codex thread invoking `$pasture:epoch` or another Pasture role skill. With Codex's recommended default `agents.max_depth=1`, the root owns phase transitions, consensus, fan-out, worker/reviewer dispatch, waits, follow-ups, and consolidation. Architect/supervisor coordination executes as root skills when coordination is required. All spawned explorers, workers, and reviewers are depth-1 leaves.

Native agent projections are bounded leaves, not a nested hierarchy:

- `pasture_epoch`: analysis/status/root guidance; directs full orchestration to the root skill.
- `pasture_architect`: bounded requirements/proposal/handoff artifact.
- `pasture_supervisor`: bounded implementation-plan/progress artifact.
- `pasture_worker`: implementation or review-fix work.
- `pasture_reviewer`: plan or code review with required Beads writes.

Plugin-only delivery uses a current built-in/default leaf with a self-contained prompt whose first directive activates the exact namespaced skill. Healthy installed delivery may select `pasture_*` and elide redundant activation. Unavailable custom types fall back to plugin-only. Self-contained Beads handoffs inherit no conversation; follow-ups target the persistent leaf. Fan-out batches or serializes when thread capacity is small. Model, reasoning, sandbox, MCP, and skill overrides are omitted so live parent policy wins.

## 4. Plugin, skill metadata, and canonical agent bundle

Pasture emits `plugins/pasture/.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, all 31 canonical skills, and `skills/install-codex-agents`. Skill frontmatter uses unqualified name/description; installed invocations are namespaced. Every skill has exhaustive `agents/openai.yaml` with compatible display name, 25–64 character short description, and a default prompt naming its skill. `install-codex-agents` and the explicitly Claude-backed `swarm` set `allow_implicit_invocation=false`.

The rich compatible plugin manifest includes documented identity/interface/skills only—no agents field, install hook, unbacked app, or MCP declaration. Plugin add installs skills and zero native agents.

The setup skill owns exactly one bundle:

```text
skills/install-codex-agents/assets/agent-bundle/
  manifest.json
  agents/pasture_epoch.toml
  agents/pasture_architect.toml
  agents/pasture_supervisor.toml
  agents/pasture_worker.toml
  agents/pasture_reviewer.toml
```

The manifest freezes bundle schema and installer protocol; plugin/bundle semver; exact compatible CLI release tag and semver; minimum/tested Codex versions; checksum artifact name; supported OS/architecture matrix; and each canonical role ID, public name, safe relative path, SHA-256, and execution-policy projection. Both installer and Home Manager consume these exact bytes. The Go wire implementation is private `internal/codexbundle`; the JSON schema is the shared contract.

## 5. Exact CLI and setup contract

```text
pasture codex agents capabilities --format=json
pasture codex agents plan --bundle M [--project-root P|--no-project-check] --format=text|json
pasture codex agents install --bundle M --plan-digest D [--allow-downgrade] [project flags] --format=text|json
pasture codex agents status [--bundle M] [project flags] --format=text|json
pasture codex agents recover --format=text|json
pasture codex agents uninstall --format=text|json
```

Stable JSON schemas and exit categories are black-box tested through the built Cobra binary. `capabilities` is a static zero-write report of CLI release tag/semver, protocols, supported platforms, and features. Bundle-less status reports only ledger/disk/journal integrity; `--bundle` adds desired version/hash comparison. Optional plugin observation is labeled unknown when unavailable and never constructs cache paths.

`plan` and `status` acquire the installer lock without writing, wait for active mutations, and inspect one coherent ledger/generation/journal snapshot. An interrupted journal is reported, never repaired. Plan is explicitly non-authoritative and writes zero bytes. Its digest binds the canonical bundle bytes, resolved Codex home identity, ledger/current generation, journal state, collisions, explicit project decision, and options.

`recover`, `install`, and `uninstall` are authorized mutators and take the exclusive lock. Install reruns all validation. If it first recovers an interrupted transaction, the old digest is stale and activation stops until the user sees and approves a fresh plan. Downgrade requires an audited flag.

The setup skill resolves its own bundle without cache-path inference, checks exact CLI capability, Codex compatibility, `bd`, Git, conditional repository commit policy, and optional `aura-swarm`. If CLI bootstrap is needed it invokes `$pasture:install-cli` with the bundle's exact tag. It displays plan, obtains scoped permission, installs with the bound digest, verifies status, and requires a fresh thread. It never changes Git config or hooks. Landing uses `git agent-commit` only when repository policy requires it and stops actionably when required but unavailable.

## 6. Recoverable managed-generation transaction

Threat model: untrusted bundle input, accidental corruption, crashes, concurrent Pasture commands, and path replacement—not a continuously racing privileged or malicious same-UID process.

```text
CODEX_HOME/agents/pasture-managed/       complete companion generation
CODEX_HOME/pasture/agent-install.json    committed ledger
CODEX_HOME/pasture/agent-install.lock    persistent advisory-lock path
CODEX_HOME/pasture/transactions/<id>/    journal, staged new, old backup
```

Before a mutation, lstat every path component and recursively compare the complete managed generation against the ledger. Expected regular files, hashes, and relevant modes must match; expected directories must be present; unknown, missing, modified, or type-changed entries and all symlinks are TAMPERED. They stop with zero mutation and preservation/repair guidance.

The mutator stages and fsyncs a complete same-filesystem generation, journals `PREPARED`, moves the validated prior directory to the control-area backup and journals `OLD_MOVED`, renames the staged directory into the loader tree and journals `NEW_ACTIVE`, atomically writes/fsyncs the ledger and journals `COMMITTED`, then removes only transaction-owned content whose recorded identity still matches. Uninstall uses the same state machine. Recovery restores or completes the only unambiguous journal state; if loader-visible or backup content changed after journaling, it preserves every candidate and stops rather than guessing.

The honest guarantee is crash-recoverable quiescent installation: a concurrent Codex start can see the complete old set, a brief absence, or the complete new set, never a mixed Pasture generation. A fresh thread begins only after healthy status. Identical install is a true no-op preserving mtimes. No option in this feature adopts, overwrites, or deletes unknown/modified content.

Real subprocess tests SIGKILL after every durable boundary, then invoke explicit recovery. They cover first install, no-op, upgrade, explicit downgrade, uninstall, every journal state, read/write contention, two mutators, persistent unheld lock file, stale consent, symlink/path swap, short write/ENOSPC, permissions, cleanup failure, tampered backups, and supported Linux/macOS directory semantics.

`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` stores the canonical bare semver. `pasture-release` is its sole mutating writer; codegen reads it and deterministically emits equal Codex plugin and bundle versions. The manifest freezes bundle schema and installer protocol; plugin/bundle semver; exact compatible CLI release tag and semver; minimum/tested Codex versions; checksum artifact name; supported OS/architecture matrix; and each canonical role ID, public name, safe relative path, SHA-256, and execution-policy projection. Both installer and Home Manager consume these exact bytes. The Go wire implementation is private `internal/codexbundle`; the JSON schema is the shared contract.

## 5. Exact CLI and setup contract

```text
pasture codex agents capabilities --format=json
pasture codex agents plan --bundle M [--project-root P|--no-project-check] --format=text|json
pasture codex agents install --bundle M --plan-digest D [--allow-downgrade] [project flags] --format=text|json
pasture codex agents status [--bundle M] [project flags] --format=text|json
pasture codex agents recover --format=text|json
pasture codex agents uninstall --format=text|json
```

Stable JSON schemas and exit categories are black-box tested through the built Cobra binary. `capabilities` is a static zero-write report of CLI release tag/semver, protocols, supported platforms, and features. Bundle-less status reports only ledger/disk/journal integrity; `--bundle` adds desired version/hash comparison. Optional plugin observation is labeled unknown when unavailable and never constructs cache paths.

The persistent lock is an empty regular mode-0600 file created only by an authorized mutator. A mutator may create the secure control directory and atomically create the lock with O_EXCL as its first owned file, then uses no-follow lstat/fstat identity checks and takes the exclusive advisory lock before any ledger, journal, transaction, or managed-generation mutation. A race loser coordinates on the same inode. A crash after directory creation but before lock creation is BOOTSTRAP_INTERRUPTED; explicit recovery finishes bootstrap only if that directory is securely owned and empty and all other installer paths are absent.

When a valid lock exists, `plan` and `status` open it read-only with no-follow, verify regular type, identity, owner, link count, and restrictive mode, take a shared lock, wait for a mutator, and inspect one coherent snapshot without changing bytes or mtimes. When the lock is absent, they read two complete snapshots of lock identity, exact control entries, ledger, transactions, and managed generation. Stable all-absent snapshots are pristine and linearize before a later mutation; lock appearance or any identity change retries through the locked path; stable non-pristine state without a lock is BOOTSTRAP_INTERRUPTED/TAMPERED. Bounded retry exhaustion is CONCURRENT_CHANGE. An interrupted journal is reported, never repaired. Plan is non-authoritative and writes zero bytes. Its digest binds canonical bundle bytes, resolved Codex-home identity, ledger/current generation, journal state, collisions, explicit project decision, and options.

`recover`, `install`, and `uninstall` are authorized mutators and take the exclusive lock. Install reruns all validation. If it first recovers an interrupted transaction, the old digest is stale and activation stops until the user sees and approves a fresh plan. Downgrade requires an audited flag.

The setup skill resolves its own bundle without cache-path inference, checks exact CLI capability, Codex compatibility, `bd`, Git, conditional repository commit policy, and optional `aura-swarm`. If CLI bootstrap is needed it invokes `$pasture:install-cli` with the bundle's exact tag. It displays plan, obtains scoped permission, installs with the bound digest, verifies status, and requires a fresh thread. It never changes Git config or hooks. Landing uses `git agent-commit` only when repository policy requires it and stops actionably when required but unavailable.

## 6. Recoverable managed-generation transaction

Threat model: untrusted bundle input, accidental corruption, crashes, concurrent Pasture commands, and path replacement—not a continuously racing privileged or malicious same-UID process.

```text
CODEX_HOME/agents/pasture-managed/       complete companion generation
CODEX_HOME/pasture/agent-install.json    committed ledger
CODEX_HOME/pasture/agent-install.lock    persistent advisory-lock path
CODEX_HOME/pasture/transactions/<id>/    journal, staged new, old backup
```

With no journal, lstat every path component and recursively compare the complete managed generation against the committed ledger. Expected regular files, hashes, and relevant modes must match; expected directories must be present; unknown, missing, modified, or type-changed entries and all symlinks are TAMPERED. They stop with zero mutation and preservation/repair guidance. During an interrupted transaction, the journal—not the old ledger alone—is the identity authority.

Before any rename, the durable journal records operation/schema/transaction ID, contained candidate paths, prior generation and ledger identity `P` (or ABSENT), desired generation and ledger identity `N` (or ABSENT), and complete staged-tree identity. Identities cover recursive membership, types, hashes, and relevant modes. The exact recovery table is:

| Journal | Loader-visible active | Backup | Stage | Ledger | Recovery |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| none/healthy | committed | absent | absent | same committed identity | no recovery |
| PREPARED | P | absent | N | P | roll back stage |
| PREPARED successor | absent | P | N | P | restore P, remove exact stage |
| OLD_MOVED | absent | P | N | P | restore P, remove exact stage |
| OLD_MOVED successor | N | P | absent | P | roll forward N |
| NEW_ACTIVE | N | P | absent | P | commit N ledger |
| NEW_ACTIVE successor | N | P | absent | N | mark committed |
| COMMITTED | N | P until cleanup | absent | N | clean recorded P/journal |

ABSENT covers first install and uninstall. The three successor rows are the identity-equivalent result of a rename/ledger commit that completed before its next journal checkpoint. Directory and ledger renames are fsynced before the next checkpoint. Recovery accepts only the named checkpoint or its single exact successor. Malformed/unknown fields, path escape, duplicate candidate, impossible operation/state pair, corrupt/forged digest, changed backup, unexpected ledger temp, or any unknown transaction member preserves every candidate and stops. Cleanup removes only transaction-owned content whose recorded identity still matches.

The honest guarantee is crash-recoverable quiescent installation: a concurrent Codex start can see the complete old set, a brief absence, or the complete new set, never a mixed Pasture generation. A fresh thread begins only after healthy status. Identical install is a true no-op preserving mtimes. No option in this feature adopts, overwrites, or deletes unknown/modified content.

Real subprocess tests SIGKILL after every durable boundary, then invoke explicit recovery. They cover first install, no-op, upgrade, explicit downgrade, uninstall, every baseline and successor journal shape, every corrupt/forged/tampered variant, fresh observer at every mkdir/O_EXCL/flock boundary, two first mutators, persistent unheld lock, read/write contention, stale consent, symlink/path swap, short write/ENOSPC, permissions, cleanup failure, and supported Linux/macOS directory semantics. Fresh `plan`/`status` tests compare complete bytes and mtimes before/after.

## 7. Ownership scope and Home Manager

Exclusive authority applies only to one personal `CODEX_HOME/agents/pasture-managed`: companion XOR Home Manager. When a valid lock exists, `plan` and `status` open it read-only with no-follow, verify regular type, identity, owner, link count, and restrictive mode, take a shared lock, wait for a mutator, and inspect one coherent snapshot without changing bytes or mtimes. When the lock is absent, they read two complete snapshots of lock identity, exact control entries, ledger, transactions, and managed generation. Stable all-absent snapshots are pristine and linearize before a later mutation; lock appearance or any identity change retries through the locked path; stable non-pristine state without a lock is BOOTSTRAP_INTERRUPTED/TAMPERED. Bounded retry exhaustion is CONCURRENT_CHANGE. An interrupted journal is reported, never repaired. Plan is non-authoritative and writes zero bytes. Its digest binds canonical bundle bytes, resolved Codex-home identity, ledger/current generation, journal state, collisions, explicit project decision, and options.

The lock inode is coordination metadata, not semantic installer state: absent pristine and a valid unheld lock with no ledger/journal/generation normalize to the same PRISTINE plan state. `recover`, `install`, and `uninstall` take the exclusive lock. Install reruns all validation; concurrent first installs with the same digest serialize, the winner proceeds, and later contenders reject stale consent after the committed semantic state changes. Transaction recovery invalidates consent and requires a fresh plan. Downgrade requires an audited flag.

The setup skill resolves its own bundle without cache-path inference, checks exact CLI capability, Codex compatibility, `bd`, Git, conditional repository commit policy, and optional `aura-swarm`. If CLI bootstrap is needed it invokes `$pasture:install-cli` with the bundle's exact tag. It displays plan, obtains scoped permission, installs with the bound digest, verifies status, and requires a fresh thread. It never changes Git config or hooks. Landing uses `git agent-commit` only when repository policy requires it and stops actionably when required but unavailable.

## 6. Recoverable managed-generation transaction

Threat model: untrusted bundle input, accidental corruption, crashes, concurrent Pasture commands, and path replacement—not a continuously racing privileged or malicious same-UID process.

```text
CODEX_HOME/agents/pasture-managed/       complete companion generation
CODEX_HOME/pasture/agent-install.json    committed ledger
CODEX_HOME/pasture/agent-install.lock    persistent advisory-lock path
CODEX_HOME/pasture/transactions/<id>/    journal, staged new, old backup
```

With no journal, lstat every path component and recursively compare the complete managed generation against the committed ledger. Expected regular files, hashes, and relevant modes must match; expected directories must be present; unknown, missing, modified, or type-changed entries and all symlinks are TAMPERED. They stop with zero mutation and preservation/repair guidance. During an interrupted transaction, the journal—not the old ledger alone—is the identity authority.

Before staging, the durable journal records operation/schema/transaction ID, contained candidate paths, prior generation+ledger identity `P` (or ABSENT), desired generation+ledger identity `N` (or ABSENT), and complete recursive identities. It is a framed append-only hash chain: magic/schema, bounded length, canonical payload, monotonic sequence, previous-record hash, and SHA-256. Appends and directory changes are fsynced; there is no journal-replacement temp.

Install/upgrade/downgrade uses this write-ahead automaton (`P` optional, `N` present):

| Journal state | Allowed physical shape(s) | Recovery direction |
|---|---|---|
| CREATED/STAGING | active+ledger=P; only declared staging candidates may be partial | rollback |
| PREPARED | active+ledger=P; generation-stage=N; next-ledger=N; backup absent | rollback |
| MOVE_OLD_INTENT, only P present | before: active=P/backup absent; after: active absent/backup=P; both stages=N, ledger=P | rollback both |
| OLD_MOVED, only P present | active absent; backup=P; both stages=N; ledger=P | rollback |
| ACTIVATE_NEW_INTENT | before: active absent/generation-stage=N; after: active=N/stage absent; backup=P if any; ledger=P; next-ledger=N | roll forward both |
| NEW_ACTIVE | active=N; backup=P if any; generation-stage absent; ledger=P; next-ledger=N | roll forward |
| COMMIT_LEDGER_INTENT | before: ledger=P/next-ledger=N; after: ledger=N/next-ledger absent; active=N | roll forward both |
| COMMITTED/CLEANUP | active+ledger=N; only recorded prior/cleanup suffix remains | ordered cleanup |

First install has `P=ABSENT` and skips MOVE_OLD_INTENT/OLD_MOVED. `next-ledger.json` is generated, hashed, fsynced, and journaled before PREPARED, then atomically renamed over the control ledger at COMMIT_LEDGER_INTENT.

Uninstall uses a separate automaton (`P` present, `N` absent):

| Journal state | Allowed physical shape(s) | Recovery direction |
|---|---|---|
| CREATED/PREPARED | active+ledger=P | rollback |
| MOVE_OLD_INTENT | before: active=P/backup absent; after: active absent/backup=P | rollback both |
| OLD_MOVED | active absent; backup=P; ledger=P | rollback |
| COMMIT_LEDGER_INTENT | before: ledger=P/retired-ledger absent; after: ledger absent/retired-ledger=P; active absent | roll forward both |
| COMMITTED/CLEANUP | active+ledger absent; exact backup/retired-ledger cleanup suffix | ordered cleanup |

Uninstall has no ACTIVATE_NEW_INTENT or NEW_ACTIVE. It atomically renames the validated control ledger to journaled `retired-ledger.json` rather than unlinking it. Thus journal state always selects one direction; generic `N=ABSENT` inference is forbidden.

Recovery uses the last complete hash-chained record. A partial tail may be truncated only when it is a prefix of the one canonical next record permitted by the observed physical state; otherwise all candidates are preserved. A transaction with no complete first record is STAGING_INCOMPLETE and removable only when empty. After COMMITTED, cleanup follows a fixed journaled order. CLEANUP checkpoints accept only the recorded remaining suffix or its exact one-deletion successor, always continuing cleanup. The journal remains until all other candidates are gone; after journal unlink, only an empty secure well-formed transaction-ID directory may be removed. Any malformed field, path escape, duplicate/impossible candidate, changed hash/type, non-prefix cleanup set, or unknown content is TAMPERED and preserved.

The honest guarantee is crash-recoverable quiescent installation: a concurrent Codex start can see the complete old set, a brief absence, or the complete new set, never a mixed Pasture generation. A fresh thread begins only after healthy status. Identical install is a true no-op preserving mtimes. No option in this feature adopts, overwrites, or deletes unknown/modified content.

Real subprocess tests SIGKILL/short-write after candidate creation, file fsync, every intent append, rename, directory fsync, ledger replacement/retirement, every cleanup deletion/checkpoint, journal unlink, rmdir, and parent fsync. They cover first install, no-op, upgrade, explicit downgrade, uninstall, both pre/post shapes for every intent, partial journal tails, all corrupt/forged/tampered candidates, two and three first mutators scheduled at mkdir/O_EXCL/open/flock/validation/commit, persistent unheld lock, read/write contention, stale consent, symlink/path swap, permissions, cleanup failure, and supported Linux/macOS semantics. Fresh `plan`/`status` tests compare complete bytes and mtimes before/after.

## 7. Ownership scope and Home Manager

Exclusive authority applies only to one personal `CODEX_HOME/agents/pasture-managed`: companion XOR Home Manager. Project `.codex/agents` directories are independent higher-precedence layers. `--project-root` checks exactly the resolved named project for same-name overrides; `--no-project-check` records the explicit skip. No global discovery or project ownership is claimed.

Aura adds only `CUSTOM.programs.aura-config-sync.codex.agents.enable = false`; it does not sync Codex skills. Nix evaluation parses the canonical bundle manifest and derives the five mappings after schema/version/path/name/hash validation—there is no second role list.

When enabled, Home Manager owns one symlink at default `~/.codex/agents/pasture-managed` to an immutable generated store directory containing the exact TOMLs and an ownership manifest. A pre-link activation guard rejects a companion ledger, a regular managed directory, an arbitrary symlink, or malformed/modified ownership manifest before link mutation. It accepts absent state or a previous Home Manager-owned immutable target with exact membership, enabling repeat activation and upgrade. Companion symmetrically rejects the managed symlink. Disable removes only the Home Manager-owned link. A non-default `CODEX_HOME` is a separate companion target.

A pinned Home Manager fixture tests default, malformed bundle, enable, repeat enable, upgrade, companion/stale-ledger conflict with zero mutation, disable/removal, modified or arbitrary links, and preservation. Pinned Codex proves directory-symlinked TOMLs load and disappear.

## 8. One version, strict checksums, and release readiness

`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` stores the canonical bare semver. `pasture-release` is its sole mutating writer; codegen reads it and deterministically emits equal Codex plugin and bundle versions. Change `cmd/pasture/root.go` from `const version` to linker-injectable `var version = "dev"`. Release builds inject canonical `vX.Y.Z`; one parser exposes both tag and bare semver. CLI `--version`, capabilities, bundle constraint, generated versions, release tag, and release verification must agree.

Supported release tuples are exactly linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, and darwin/arm64. A release publishes `pasture`, `pastured`, and `pasture-release` for each tuple plus `SHA256SUMS`: exactly 12 lexicographically sorted, newline-terminated lines of `<64 lowercase hex><two spaces><basename>`, with no path separators. Bootstrap rejects missing, duplicate, extra, malformed, unsupported, version/tag-mismatched, untrusted redirect, and mismatched artifacts. It verifies the exact current-platform `pasture` in a private same-filesystem stage before rename or execution, then fsyncs and activates.

Fake-release tests exercise every negative case. After publish, a gate fetches the immutable actual tag/checksum roster and runs `pasture codex agents capabilities` for all four tuples on declared native/emulated runners. Aura cannot mark the entry AVAILABLE until this passes. `make generate` emits `claude-code,opencode,codex` and extends PR #35's drift gate. Release invokes generation; it does not rewrite generated sibling versions independently.

Aura creates/updates its repo Codex marketplace at `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` and appends Pasture after existing entries. The entry is frozen as:

## 10. Deterministic validation and clean-machine coverage

Mandatory hermetic tests cover roots/containment, the sole catalog, structural parts and full visitor, dialects/invocations, complete plugin/assets/link graph, manifest/TOML/schema/hash validation, transaction and CLI black boxes, exact target inventories/stale output, version parity, and Home Manager evaluation/activation. Its `agent_type` schema is a plain string; the test parses the deterministic `Available roles:` entries in its description and asserts exact five custom names/descriptions/order, built-in preservation, and exact absence after removal. Clean-machine fixtures vary isolated PATH/repository state for absent/incompatible/compatible Codex and Pasture, absent/present `bd` and Git, required present/missing `git agent-commit`, optional swarm, no repository, and fully provisioned setup. They assert fallback or exact failure plus no changes to hooks, Git configuration, default home, unrelated task DB, or cache.

Repo-owned Go/Nix checks are mandatory. Skill/plugin creator validators are recorded compatibility evidence with exact script hashes and interpreter dependencies, never ambient-home CI dependencies.

## 11. Buildable ownership and implementation sequence

One root implementor executes sequentially; exploration and adversarial reviewers do not edit.

1. Foundation owns `GenerationRoots`, the one catalog, structural runtime semantics/compiler, canonical assets/projections, and their tests. It does not register Codex or own target renderers.

5. Release integration alone owns `cmd/pasture/root.go`, release packages/tests, Makefile, checksum workflow/docs, all-target generation wiring, and version parity.
6. Aura owns `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, Home Manager module/fixture, README/inputs/lock, and the Pasture gitlink; it consumes the frozen bundle.

Any newly shared file is reassigned in Beads before editing. Sequence is roots/catalog/runtime → bundle schema → Codex emitter/integration → CLI/lifecycle → release/generate → immutable Pasture commit → Aura consumer. PR #35 stays the base until merged. Pasture merges/releases before a later Aura AVAILABLE change.

## BDD acceptance

1. Default `max_depth=1` reaches plan review, worker implementation, and code review with only root-to-leaf delegation.
2. The plugin-only path is complete; healthy custom types may be selected without duplicate activation and missing types fall back.
3. Empty and in-place all-target generation match exact paths/bytes and report stale owned outputs.
4. The final plugin contains 32 valid namespaced skills, all links/assets resolve, and no unapproved Claude operation remains.
5. Plugin add creates zero custom agents; explicit companion or Home Manager delivery exposes exactly five namespaced types without shadowing built-ins.
6. `capabilities`, `plan`, and `status` write zero bytes in healthy, pristine, bootstrap-interrupted, and transaction-interrupted states; the absent-lock double snapshot and existing-lock read path are race-safe.
7. Consent is bound to exact state. Recovery, collision, project decision, or any state change invalidates the digest before activation.
8. SIGKILL at every durable boundary matches one operation-specific write-ahead state whose pre/post shapes share a recovery direction; otherwise every candidate is preserved with a precise TAMPERED/INTERRUPTED report.
9. Unknown, modified, missing, symlinked, malformed, downgraded, or unowned content is never silently moved, overwritten, adopted, or deleted.
10. Identical install preserves bytes and mtimes; uninstall removes only an exact owned generation.
11. Home Manager conflict fails before mutation; enable/repeat/upgrade/load/disable/removal succeeds from the canonical bundle.
12. A fake provider observes exact custom-role prose in `agent_type.description` and deterministically calls each installed/removed role; real model UAT separately demonstrates selection.
13. Strict checksum/bootstrap negatives fail before verified binary activation; the actual-release gate is required before marketplace availability.
14. One canonical version projects equal plugin/bundle/CLI/tag/checksum values, and release generation stays clean.
15. The exact Aura marketplace object is immutable and NOT_AVAILABLE in the stacked feature PR.
16. Any review finding causes a revised proposal or implementation and another three-axis round; progression requires a fix-free 0/0/0 wave.
17. After clean gates and user implementation UAT, evidence-backed Pasture and Aura PRs open in Pasture-before-Aura order.

## Out of scope

- Plugin-native custom agents or automatic install hooks.
- Raised-depth or nested Codex orchestration.
- Global project discovery, project ownership/export, or a project Home Manager mode.
- Codex backend for `aura-swarm`.
- Aura Codex skill sync.
- Git hook installation or Git configuration mutation.
- Silent adoption/deletion of tampered managed content.
- Vercel skills CLI, oh-my-codex, npm packaging, and ChatGPT-web local-agent claims.
