# FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-8 — Unified multi-harness installation

Supersedes Proposal 7 in response to Plan UAT feedback. URD Amendments 1–8 are normative, with the newest amendment governing conflicts. Proposal 7's source/output isolation, single structural runtime compiler, complete render graph, default-depth Codex orchestration, canonical role projections, version/checksum discipline, fault-injected journal semantics, clean-machine tests, and clean-review exit remain part of this proposal unless explicitly replaced below.

The revision fixes two product-boundary errors. First, Aura Home Manager already installs Pasture-generated Claude Code and OpenCode skills; the missing capability was a common component-selection surface and Codex skill delivery, not skills in general. Second, an agents-only Codex helper is too narrow. Pasture will ship one kickstart-style installer that asks which harnesses and which independently selectable components the user wants.

## 1. Product boundary and user experience

The primary command is `pasture install`, with `kickstart` as a Cobra alias. With no selectors and an interactive terminal it opens a Bubble Tea wizard inspired by Peasant's kickstart interaction grammar. Explicit selectors or an input document bypass the TUI. An incomplete noninteractive invocation fails actionably and never waits for input.

The central page is a real harness-by-component matrix:

| Harness | Skills | Agents | Hooks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | generated native skills | generated native agents | separately delivered Claude lifecycle hook plugin |
| OpenCode | generated native skills | generated native agents | generated target-native OpenCode plugin |
| Codex | generated `pasture` plugin | generated standalone TOML agents | separate generated `pasture-hooks` plugin |

Each cell is independently selectable and reports one of available, selected, installed, no-op, disabled, degraded, conflicting, or externally managed. Row and column toggles affect only selectable cells. Disabled and degraded cells retain visible what/why/impact/remediation text. Back-navigation preserves answers. Terminal resize, search/help, cancel, and an explicit final confirmation follow the proven Peasant state-machine pattern, but the summary page renders the real immutable install plan rather than descriptive prose.

The wizard initially selects only cells already owned by the same authority or explicitly chosen in the current session. It may visually suggest detected harnesses, but detection never silently opts into new components. Hooks are always initially unselected. Selecting a hook shows its harness lifecycle events and consent consequence before the plan page. The term hook never means `.git/hooks`, `core.hooksPath`, or a Beads hook; those remain prohibited without separate explicit user approval.

## 2. One typed catalog, no parallel inventories

Pasture adds a closed delivery model alongside the canonical role/command/skill semantics:

```go
type HarnessName string       // claude-code, opencode, codex
type ComponentName string     // skills, agents, hooks
type SupportState string      // supported, degraded, unavailable
type DeliveryAuthority string // companion, home-manager
type DeliveryStrategy string  // direct-files, native-plugin, external-cli

type Capability struct {
    Harness       HarnessName
    Component     ComponentName
    State         SupportState
    Reason        ActionableReason
    Strategy      DeliveryStrategy
    Scope         Scope
    Prerequisites []Prerequisite
    Unit          OwnershipUnit
}

type Artifact struct {
    Harness       HarnessName
    Component     ComponentName
    RelativePath  SafePath
    Mode          fs.FileMode
    SHA256        Digest
    PayloadKey    PayloadKey
}
```

`SkillDescriptor`, canonical role descriptors, structural `RuntimeText`, and lifecycle-hook semantics remain the semantic sources. `TargetHarness` projects them into artifacts tagged with harness/component. A deterministic delivery catalog is derived from those artifacts; it is not manually repeated in the TUI, Cobra layer, Aura Nix, setup skills, docs, or tests. A compile-time/exhaustive test requires exactly one capability record for each of the nine cells and exactly one owner for every emitted artifact. New harnesses or components make switches and fixtures fail until classified.

`GeneratedFile` gains mode, component, hash, and payload identity. The final immutable `BundleManifest` freezes schema version, Pasture version, target harness version constraints, every payload byte/hash/mode/path, capability status/reason, strategy, ownership key, supported platform tuple, and external adapter contract. Development codegen still emits complete harness distributions. Install planning selects manifest members; it never regenerates protocol text in a user's home.

Proposal 7's structural runtime compiler remains mandatory for Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex. OpenCode may no longer reuse Claude operation prose verbatim where harness operations differ. Every rendered actionable skill address and lifecycle action must resolve under its target's real syntax.

## 3. Exact delivery units

Component independence is a physical invariant. No selected cell may activate an unselected component.

### Claude Code

- Skills are direct, owned directory trees under `~/.claude/skills/<skill>/`.
- Agents are direct, owned files under `~/.claude/agents/<role>.md`.
- Hooks are a separately generated hook-only Claude plugin, installed through a pinned supported Claude plugin adapter and verified by plugin ID/version/source. The existing all-in-one repository plugin remains a development/marketplace compatibility surface, but the new installer never uses it to satisfy an independent cell.

### OpenCode

- Skills are direct, owned directory trees under `~/.config/opencode/skills/<skill>/`.
- Agents are direct, owned files under `~/.config/opencode/agent/<role>.md`.
- Hooks are one generated, owned target-native plugin under `~/.config/opencode/plugins/`. It uses only pinned OpenCode plugin events. It must not contain Claude event names, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`, or Claude tool payload assumptions.

The OpenCode hook projection supplies Pasture system/session context through `experimental.chat.system.transform`, compaction context through `experimental.session.compacting`, and pre-shell discipline through `tool.execute.before`, or the exact pinned successor APIs proven by conformance tests. Worker-only policy runs only when supported session/agent data proves worker identity. Unknown identity is degraded coverage, not a block on unrelated agents.

### Codex

- Skills are the complete namespaced `pasture` Codex plugin installed from a private pinned local marketplace with the supported `codex plugin add` workflow.
- Agents are the five native standalone TOMLs under the supported personal custom-agent tree. The plugin carries their canonical bundle only as inert installer assets; its manifest never claims plugin-native agents.
- Hooks are a separate `pasture-hooks` Codex plugin. Installing skills alone activates no hook definition.

Both Codex plugins have valid `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` manifests and their own exact IDs/versions/sources. The primary plugin contains the canonical skills plus required metadata/assets; the hook plugin contains only lifecycle-hook material and metadata needed to execute it. No code writes Codex private plugin cache paths. Plugin state changes use the supported CLI adapter, then verify exact installed identity and effective enablement. Any creator-validator drift is documented as compatibility evidence; the pinned live Codex CLI ingestion test is authoritative for currently documented fields.

## 4. Command and machine contract

The root command supports a guided convenience path and explicit lifecycle subcommands:

```text
pasture install                                      # TTY wizard, plan, confirm, apply
pasture kickstart                                    # exact alias
pasture install --harness codex,opencode \
  --component skills,agents --authority companion    # plan; require --yes to apply
pasture install --request request.json [--yes]

pasture install capabilities --format text|json
pasture install plan --request request.json --format text|json
pasture install apply --plan plan.json --plan-digest D [--allow-hooks]
pasture install status [--request request.json] --format text|json
pasture install recover [--unit U] --format text|json
pasture install uninstall --request request.json [--yes] [--allow-hooks]
```

`InstallRequest`, `InstallPlan`, `PlanAction`, `ApplyResult`, `StatusReport`, and error envelopes have versioned canonical JSON. A request identifies authority, home/scope, exact selected cells, optional role filters, hook consent, and downgrade policy. It cannot contain output paths or raw commands. The planner resolves those exclusively from the signed/embedded catalog.

`capabilities`, `plan`, and `status` are zero-write observers. `apply`, `recover`, and `uninstall` are explicit mutators. The guided convenience form performs the same plan and apply calls in-process; it has no alternate mutation path. Explicit selectors never launch Bubble Tea. A non-TTY without a complete request names the missing dimensions and exact corrective flags. Unsupported selections fail with the same structured reason shown in the matrix.

TUI messages, flags, and JSON fixtures expressing the same selection produce byte-identical canonical plans and digests. `--yes` is required to mutate outside the interactive confirmation. Any noninteractive request containing hooks additionally requires `--allow-hooks`; merely placing hooks in a file is not sufficient consent. Home Manager hook consent is the explicit presence of `hooks` in its declared component list and is echoed in activation output.

The TUI package owns presentation only. `cmd/pasture/install.go` owns Cobra/TTY wiring; `internal/handlers/install.go` owns command-independent orchestration; `internal/delivery` owns catalog, requests, pure planning, ownership, adapters, transactions, and errors; `internal/tui/kickstart` maps Bubble Tea messages to the same typed request. The UI never reads codegen globals, invokes a harness CLI, or mutates files directly.

Adopt Bubble Tea, Bubbles, and Lip Gloss at versions pinned in `go.mod`/`go.sum`, matching Peasant's stack where compatible. Because they are new production dependencies, the Phase 8 supervisor records explicit repository dependency approval before the first module edit; Plan UAT acceptance approves the requested TUI architecture but does not bypass repository policy.

## 5. Home Manager is the declarative adapter for the same matrix

Aura changes `CUSTOM.programs.aura-config-sync` to expose:

```nix
targets = {
  "claude-code".components = [ "skills" "agents" ];
  opencode.components = [ "skills" "agents" ];
  codex.components = [ ];
};
```

The list is unique and restricted to `skills`, `agents`, and `hooks`; an empty list disables that harness. Defaults preserve current behavior exactly: Claude Code skills+agents enabled, OpenCode skills+agents enabled, Codex disabled, all hooks disabled. Existing `commands.enable`, `agents.enable`, `opencode.skills.enable`, and `opencode.agents.enable` remain compatibility inputs for one release cycle with precise deprecation warnings. Equivalent old/new declarations normalize to one intent; conflicting declarations fail Nix evaluation with both option locations and the migration fix. The current shared role filter remains shared unless a later UAT explicitly changes it.

Pasture codegen emits a versioned `InstallIntent`/catalog projection for Nix. Aura consumes the pinned Pasture output and never recreates skill names, roles, paths, hashes, plugin IDs, or support states. Home Manager direct-file cells link exact immutable store payloads and ownership manifests. The OpenCode hook plugin is likewise a direct immutable artifact. Deactivation removes only links whose manifest and target prove Home Manager ownership.

Claude hook and Codex plugin cells use activation adapters around their supported idempotent plugin CLI operations because plugin registration includes harness-owned state. Aura stages the exact pinned local plugin/marketplace bytes, invokes the shared Pasture installer with `authority=home-manager`, and verifies postconditions. It does not write a private plugin cache or describe these cells as pure `home.file` mappings.

Before any Codex mutation the plan preflights `~/.codex/config.toml`. A symlinked, read-only, or independently Home-Manager-owned file is an actionable conflict naming the option/owner and choices: let the adapter own supported plugin registration, disable that cell, or select a future standalone skill dialect. The implementation never bypasses the conflict. A generated standalone `$pasture-*` direct-skill dialect remains deferred and cannot be silently substituted.

Ownership is exclusive per resolved `(home, scope, harness, component)`, not per entire home. Companion and Home Manager may coexist only on disjoint cells. Every plan includes current authority, desired authority, generation, exact destinations, and conflict state for all selected cells. Unselected cells are read only for collision detection and otherwise untouched.

Aura currently publishes packages only for Linux. Either the implementation adds the corresponding Darwin package/module evaluation coverage before claiming macOS support or it rejects unsupported systems at evaluation with an actionable message. It may not advertise a target that cannot supply the pinned installer and bundle.

## 6. Release-complete payload and setup skill

The release-installed `pasture` binary embeds the immutable manifest and all payload bytes for every supported cell, including support documents, agent bodies, hook code/scripts, plugin manifests, local marketplace metadata, and ownership schemas. A released installer works after binary acquisition without a source checkout or network. An alternate adjacent signed data archive is acceptable only if every release platform installs it atomically with the binary and the CLI verifies its exact digest before planning; implementation must choose one path and freeze it in fixtures.

`make generate` emits Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex main plugin, Codex hook plugin, Claude hook plugin, and the delivery bundle from the same inputs. Empty-root and in-place generation compare exact path/byte/mode manifests and identify stale owned outputs. Proposal 7's single canonical version, four release tuples, strict `SHA256SUMS`, bootstrap rejection cases, and actual-release readiness gate remain mandatory. The feature remains based on upstream codegen-drift PR #35 until it merges.

The generated setup skill becomes a thin conversational adapter to the same CLI. It can explain capabilities, gather a matrix request, call zero-write plan, display exact actions, request scoped consent, call apply with the bound digest, verify status, and require a fresh harness session where needed. It does not implement a second installer, infer cache paths, mutate Git config/hooks, or install unsupported cells.

## 7. Recoverable multi-unit execution

Proposal 7's secure path validation, persistent no-follow lock, canonical-byte payload oracle, append-only hash-chained journal, PREPARED commit point, explicit install/upgrade/uninstall state machines, flattened atomic cleanup, fsync ordering, zero-write observers, stale-consent rejection, tamper preservation, and fault-injection matrix are generalized from one Codex-agent generation to each direct-file ownership unit.

Each resolved cell is one ownership unit with its own ledger, lock, generation, and transaction journal under a Pasture control namespace outside harness-managed content. A plan digest binds bundle bytes, request, hook consent, home/scope identity, all selected cell states and authorities, exact paths/actions/modes/hashes, collisions, external registry observations, journal states, platform, adapter versions, and options. Identical apply is a true no-op preserving content and mtimes.

Before the first unit reaches PREPARED, global preflight validates every selected unit, prerequisite, collision, Home Manager conflict, and external adapter availability. Units then execute in deterministic `(home, scope, harness, component)` order. Direct-file units use the journaled generation transaction. External CLI units append a canonical intent before invoking only a pinned idempotent supported command; after success, error, timeout, or process death, recovery re-observes exact plugin ID/version/source/effective state and classifies the outcome before retrying. It never guesses success from an exit code alone.

The multi-unit operation is resumable, not falsely atomic. A failure report distinguishes already committed/no-op units, the interrupted unit, and untouched units, and prints the exact `recover`/resume command. It never claims that an external plugin mutation was rolled back when it was not. Recovery completes or safely aborts the current unit according to its journal and then requires a fresh plan digest for remaining units. Uninstall removes only exact owned state. Modified, missing, unknown, symlinked, downgraded, or foreign content is preserved and surfaced.

Every error satisfies the actionable-error contract: what failed; why; exact unit/path/module/function; operation and time/journal state; caller impact including partial commits; and a concrete fix/recovery command.

## 8. Validation architecture

Tests use YAML fixtures for table-driven domain cases per repository policy. The minimum hermetic suite covers:

1. The complete 3×3 capability catalog, exhaustive enum handling, unique artifact ownership, and exact component isolation.
2. Structural runtime rendering for all three harnesses and exhaustive active-link/address scanning over every final Markdown/XML/YAML/JSON/TOML/JS artifact.
3. TUI model messages for row/column toggles, disabled/degraded/conflict cells, existing selections, back, cancel, confirmation, help/search, resize, narrow terminals, progress, failure, and recovery presentation.
4. Byte-identical request/plan/digest output for equivalent TUI, flags, JSON, and Home Manager intent fixtures; incomplete non-TTY and unsupported-selector errors.
5. Hook consent in interactive, noninteractive, and Home Manager paths; proof that skills-only and agents-only activate zero hooks; proof that no path or subprocess touches Git hooks, Git config, or Beads hooks.
6. Direct-file first install, no-op, upgrade, downgrade, uninstall, cross-authority conflict, disable, tamper, symlink/path-swap, concurrent first mutators, stale consent, and every Proposal 7 journal/syscall fault point.
7. External CLI adapter success, no-op, missing/incompatible CLI, rejected plugin, unknown timeout/outcome, process death, recovery, partial multi-unit apply, exact postcondition mismatch, and foreign registration preservation.
8. Release-installed binary operation from an empty source-less/networkless fixture for all supported platform tuples, plus exact archive/binary manifest parity.
9. Home Manager default preservation, legacy normalization/warnings, old/new conflict, explicit hooks, enable/repeat/upgrade/disable, per-cell coexistence/conflict, immutable Codex config preflight, Linux/Darwin gating, and exact Pasture-source provenance.
10. Pinned black-box harness smoke tests: selected skills list/load and unselected skills are absent; selected custom agents list/spawn and unselected agents are absent; selected lifecycle hooks fire only at their declared events; all removals disappear in fresh processes.

Pinned target versions are Codex 0.144.1 and the current verified Claude Code/OpenCode versions recorded by generated fixtures; upgrades require fixture review. Codex tests prove plugins install skills but not custom agents, five TOMLs load as native agent types, and each plugin's hook isolation. OpenCode tests compile/load the generated plugin against its pinned type package and exercise the three chosen events. Claude tests use isolated homes and the supported plugin command/status surface. Network/model UAT is separately labeled and cannot replace deterministic fake-provider/CLI tests.

Mandatory repository gates remain `go test -race ./...` in Pasture and Aura's `nix flake check --no-build`, `nix build .#aura-swarm --no-link`, and `nix run .#aura-swarm -- --help`. Generated-tree drift, `git diff --check`, and clean worktree/submodule status are part of landing evidence.

## 9. Implementation plan and ownership

One root implementor performs implementation sequentially; subagents are limited to scoped exploration and adversarial review and do not edit. Phase 8 decomposes leaf work but the root executes it directly. Integration points are explicit:

1. **Catalog/runtime foundation (Pasture):** owns `GenerationRoots`, descriptors, structural runtime compiler, typed harness/component catalog, artifact metadata, actionable reasons, and fixtures. It exports immutable capability/artifact APIs to all later slices.
2. **Bundle and planner contract (Pasture):** owns manifest/payload embedding, versioned requests/plans/status/errors, canonical JSON/digests, pure planner, authority/unit keys, and fixture schemas. It consumes only foundation exports and becomes frozen before adapters/UI.
3. **Harness projections (Pasture):** owns Codex main/hook plugins, Claude hook-only plugin, OpenCode native hook plugin, target skill/agent emitters, metadata, link scanners, and exact generated trees. It exports catalog-tagged bytes to the bundle.
4. **Direct/external adapters (Pasture):** owns generalized Proposal 7 transaction engine, direct-file adapter, Claude/Codex plugin CLI adapters, OpenCode direct adapter, recovery/uninstall/status, and fault tests. It consumes the frozen planner and bundle contracts.
5. **Cobra/TUI/setup (Pasture):** owns the root command, alias, handlers, Bubble Tea model/views, flag/JSON parity, setup skill, documentation, and black-box command tests. It cannot bypass planner/executor interfaces.
6. **Release integration (Pasture):** owns version injection, payload embedding/adjacent archive decision, all-platform artifacts, checksums, generate/drift workflows, clean-machine harness conformance, and the final Pasture commit.
7. **Home Manager/Aura:** owns typed target options, legacy migration, generated intent, activation/preflight, Nix fixtures, docs, marketplace entries, and the immutable Pasture gitlink. It consumes the released/frozen catalog and contains no protocol inventory or Python engine.

Shared-file ownership is assigned in Beads before edits. Merge order follows the integration contracts above. Pasture commits and pushes before Aura pins the immutable Pasture commit. Marketplace availability stays NOT_AVAILABLE until matching released checksums/capabilities pass; the stacked Aura feature PR may reference an immutable feature commit but must describe that state honestly.

## 10. Alternatives and explicit tradeoffs

- **Agents-only companion:** rejected because it cannot answer the requested component × harness installation problem and misstates Home Manager's existing skill behavior.
- **One plugin containing skills and hooks:** rejected for Codex/Claude installer units because selecting skills would implicitly activate hooks.
- **Copy Codex plugin skills into `~/.codex/skills`:** rejected because it loses plugin namespacing and creates a second invocation dialect. A deliberately generated standalone dialect is deferred to a future UAT choice.
- **Write harness-private plugin caches/settings directly:** rejected in favor of supported CLI adapters and exact postcondition verification.
- **Make every cell a CLI plugin mutation:** rejected because Claude/OpenCode direct skill/agent paths and OpenCode plugin paths are declarative, work well with Home Manager, and avoid unnecessary external state.
- **Copy Peasant kickstart wholesale:** rejected. Its page/state interaction is useful, but Pasture requires noninteractive parity, a real immutable plan, per-cell ownership, and crash recovery.
- **Claim an all-or-nothing nine-cell transaction:** rejected because supported external plugin CLIs are independently committed systems. The truthful guarantee is complete preflight plus deterministic, journaled, resumable units with explicit partial-state reporting.

## BDD acceptance

1. On a TTY, `pasture install` displays all nine cells, exact support reasons, stable back-navigation, a real plan, one confirmation, and progress; `pasture kickstart` is behaviorally identical.
2. The same selection through TUI, flags, JSON, and Home Manager produces the same selected-unit set, artifact hashes, actions, and canonical plan digest where authority semantics match.
3. Defaults preserve Claude Code and OpenCode skills+agents in Home Manager, leave Codex disabled, and enable no hook.
4. Every cell is physically isolated: selecting or disabling one never activates, removes, or rewrites another.
5. Codex skill installation uses the namespaced plugin; Codex agents are exactly five standalone TOMLs; the hook plugin is separate; no surface claims plugin-native agents.
6. OpenCode hooks use pinned native events and unknown worker identity degrades safely. Claude/Codex hook plugins contain only their declared lifecycle component.
7. `capabilities`, `plan`, and `status` write zero bytes. Mutators require a bound digest and explicit consent; noninteractive hooks also require `--allow-hooks`.
8. No path, command, test fixture, or activation mutates `.git/hooks`, `core.hooksPath`, or Beads hooks.
9. A source-less released binary can plan/apply/status/recover/uninstall every supported selected cell offline after bundle acquisition.
10. Direct-file faults and external CLI unknown outcomes recover deterministically without deleting foreign/tampered state. Partial multi-unit outcomes are reported truthfully and resume safely.
11. Home Manager and companion coexist on disjoint cells, conflict before mutation on the same cell, and remove only exact owned state.
12. A symlinked/read-only/independently managed Codex config blocks Codex plugin activation before mutation with a concrete remediation; private caches are never written directly.
13. Pinned fresh-process smoke tests prove every selected component present and every unselected component absent for all three harnesses.
14. All generated outputs, plugins, bundle bytes, versions, hashes, checksums, release archives, setup metadata, and marketplace claims derive from one catalog and remain drift-clean.
15. Every plan and code review wave ends with three fix-free ACCEPT votes and 0 BLOCKER/IMPORTANT/MINOR before user UAT or landing.
16. After implementation UAT and clean mandatory gates, Pasture and Aura branches are pushed and PRs opened in Pasture-before-Aura order with exact validation evidence.

## Out of scope

- Git hook or Git configuration installation.
- Plugin-native Codex custom agents.
- A second standalone `$pasture-*` Codex skill dialect in this wave.
- Project-wide harness discovery or bulk mutation outside the explicitly resolved home/scope.
- A Codex backend for `aura-swarm`.
- New Python protocol-engine code in Aura.
- Silent adoption, overwrite, rollback claims, or deletion of foreign/tampered content.
- Marketplace AVAILABLE status before immutable release evidence exists.

# FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-9 — Unified multi-harness installation

Supersedes Proposal 8. Round 8 found 4 BLOCKER, 10 IMPORTANT, and 1 MINOR findings across the three axes. This revision resolves them by separating canonical content from physical packages and effective activation, defining sparse selection and authority-specific execution, narrowing scattered-file consistency truthfully, closing external-command/discovery/cancellation state machines, choosing an acyclic embedded release bundle, pinning every harness/toolchain, and adding an independent nine-cell acceptance oracle.

URD Amendments 1–8 remain normative. Proposal 8 remains normative where this revision does not replace it. Proposal 7's structural runtime compiler, Codex default-depth design, source/output isolation, secure journal primitives, checksum/version discipline, and clean-review requirements remain normative. Proposal 7's whole-generation visibility guarantee now applies only to delivery strategies with one proven loader-visible managed subtree; it is explicitly replaced for scattered Claude Code/OpenCode paths.

## 1. Frozen three-layer delivery model

Generation and installation use three distinct graphs:

```go
type ContentArtifact struct {
    ID               ArtifactID
    SemanticOwner    ComponentName
    RelativePath     SafePath
    Mode             fs.FileMode
    SHA256           Digest
    Bytes            PayloadKey
}

type PackageMember struct {
    Artifact ArtifactID
    Purpose  MemberPurpose // active, inert-installer-asset, runtime-support
}

type DeliveryPackage struct {
    ID       PackageID
    Harness  HarnessName
    Kind     PackageKind // direct-tree, native-plugin, release-bundle, legacy-external
    Members  []PackageMember
    Effects  []CellID
    Managed  bool
}

type ActivationUnit struct {
    Cell            CellID // exact harness + component
    Support         SupportState
    Reason          ActionableReason
    Packages        []PackageID
    Postconditions  []EffectiveStateCheck
    Executors       map[DeliveryAuthority]ExecutorProfile
    Prerequisites   []Prerequisite
}
```

`ContentArtifact` has one canonical semantic owner and exact bytes. `DeliveryPackage` is physical membership and may reference content owned by another component with an explicit inert/support purpose. `ActivationUnit` is the selectable cell and defines effective loader state. `ExecutorProfile` is resolved only after authority, scope, platform, and harness version are known. Tests require every content artifact to have one semantic owner, every package member to resolve once, every active package effect to be declared, and all nine cell IDs to have one activation unit.

The Codex skills plugin references native agent TOMLs as `inert-installer-asset`; its skills postcondition requires namespaced skills loaded and zero new native `pasture_*` agent types. The Codex agents unit references the same canonical TOMLs as active direct content. Thus unselected components are never activated or mutated, while inert package bytes remain auditable and are not falsely described as absent.

The existing all-in-one Claude repository plugin is represented as `legacy-external` with effects on Claude skills, agents, and hooks. The new installer never adopts or silently removes it. If it is active, any requested state that differs from all-three-active is `CONFLICT_LEGACY_COMPOSITE`; the plan offers preservation plus manual/plugin-supported removal guidance. If all three are desired it may remain `EXTERNALLY_MANAGED`, but Pasture still does not claim ownership. Migration/adoption is deferred.

Canonical protocol roles, commands, skill descriptors, runtime text, and lifecycle intents remain upstream of this graph. Packages are projections, never additional semantic inventories.

## 2. Exact nine-cell catalog and sparse request grammar

The ratified capability intent is:

| Cell | Support | Activation delivery | Consistency |
|---|---|---|---|
| claude-code:skills | supported | native direct skill trees | per-artifact atomic, cell resumable |

## 3. Direct-file physical topology and truthful visibility

There are two direct strategies.

### Dedicated-subtree strategy

Codex agents retain Proposal 7's managed generation layout because the pinned harness test must prove that one loader-visible directory/symlinked subtree exposes all five TOMLs. The active subtree changes with one directory rename or current-pointer switch under the exact tested topology. A fresh loader may see old, briefly absent, or new, never a mixed Pasture agent generation. If the pinned Codex conformance test fails, this cell is downgraded before release to the ordered-direct strategy and the manifest/UX state that weaker guarantee.

### Ordered-direct strategy

Claude skills/agents, OpenCode skills/agents, and the single OpenCode hook file occupy shared native roots. The plan does not claim one atomic visibility point. One cell transaction has one ledger/lock/journal and ordered artifacts, but each native artifact is independently published.

Before PREPARED, all new bytes and next-ledger bytes are staged with Proposal 7's exact prefix oracle; abort removes only transaction-local content. PREPARED is the roll-forward commit point. For each lexicographically ordered artifact `i`, the journal executes:

```text
MOVE_OLD_i_INTENT -> OLD_i_MOVED (when P exists)
PUBLISH_NEW_i_INTENT -> NEW_i_PUBLISHED (when N exists)
```

Each rename and parent fsync has before/after fault points. Removed artifacts have only the move-old transition; added artifacts have only publish-new. After all artifacts reach N, `COMMIT_LEDGER_INTENT` atomically publishes the N ledger, then the flattened cleanup engine disposes exact backups/staging. Uninstall is the same ordered move-old sequence with N absent. Recovery validates every per-index physical shape and resumes one direction after PREPARED.

At every instant, any visible regular artifact is exact P or exact N—never partial bytes—but a harness scan may observe a mixture of P/N artifacts or a brief per-artifact absence during publication and until recovery. `status` reports `RECOVERY_REQUIRED_MIXED` for an interrupted post-PREPARED cell and never calls it healthy. The TUI/CLI tells the user to close active harness processes before apply and to start a fresh process only after healthy status. This is a truthful per-artifact atomicity plus cell-level resumability guarantee, not Proposal 7 whole-generation atomicity.

All direct tests enumerate stage writes, every old/new rename, unlink/rmdir, parent fsync, ledger checkpoint, process kill, recovery kill, mixed vector, symlink/type swap, foreign path, and concurrent mutator. Pinned Linux/macOS harness tests explicitly observe allowed states.

- `HomeManagerDeclarativeLinks`: exact immutable store paths, native link actions, ownership manifest, activation guards, and Home Manager generation rollback; no Pasture transaction journal is invented.

Parity assertions compare the canonical selection plan when home/current-state fixtures match. Authority-specific execution plans have separate golden fixtures; they are not required to be byte-identical across authorities.

Home Manager direct cells link individual exact artifacts from an immutable Nix generation and therefore have the same per-artifact/mixed-cell visibility caveat. ## 6. Zero-write observation and authorized discovery

Pinned probes show that external status commands are not zero-write on pristine homes: Claude 2.1.207 `plugin list --json` created `.claude.json` and a backup, while Codex 0.144.1 `plugin list --json` created `.codex/tmp/arg0`. Therefore `capabilities`, `plan`, and `status` never invoke a harness CLI and retain literal zero-write behavior.

They read Pasture ledgers, lstat native paths, and inspect only documented user configuration. External effective state without a fresh exact observation is `UNKNOWN_DISCOVERY_REQUIRED`; a plugin mutation plan is refused rather than guessed. `status` labels recorded observations as last-observed, never live.

`pasture install discover --select <external-cell> --allow-harness-writes` is an explicit mutator. The TUI asks for this scoped permission before it can render an external-cell plan; declining leaves those cells disabled and changes nothing. Discovery runs the pinned supported CLI, snapshots and reports its exact allowed filesystem effects, and records a canonical observation: executable identity/version/hash, plugin and marketplace IDs/version/source/effective state, relevant documented config identities, command result, and observation digest. It never parses or writes a private cache directly.

Apply acquires the harness registry lock, reruns authorized discovery, and requires the observation digest to equal the plan-bound state before executing a plugin mutation. A difference aborts before plugin add/remove and requires a new zero-write plan. `status --refresh` is an alias for explicit discover followed by status and requires the same permission. Observer tests snapshot bytes, modes, mtimes, inode/type, and directory membership under HOME, harness homes, all XDG roots, TMPDIR, working directory, Pasture control state, and registries in pristine/installed/missing/incompatible/interrupted/tampered/concurrent cases. Zero-write commands permit no delta. Discovery fixtures permit only a versioned exact allowlist and preserve every unexpected change for diagnosis.

## 7. External-operation and cancellation automata

An external install or uninstall journal begins with a self-contained `EXT_CREATED` record containing adapter/schema, cell/package, authority, exact executable identity, P and N observations, marketplace/plugin identities, canonical argv and nonsecret environment policy, timeouts, postconditions, and recovery guidance. The closed states are:

```text
EXT_CREATED
COMMAND_INTENT
SPAWN_INTENT
CHILD_STARTED
EXIT_OBSERVED
POSTCHECK_INTENT
OBSERVED_PRIOR | OBSERVED_DESIRED | OBSERVED_FOREIGN | UNOBSERVABLE
COMMITTED | ABORTED | PRESERVED_UNKNOWN
```

Every record append/fsync is fault injected. `COMMAND_INTENT` is durable before any child. The parent holds the harness registry flock and passes an inherited lock descriptor to the child, so a parent SIGKILL cannot let recovery retry while the original CLI still runs. Recovery waits boundedly for that lock. Once released it performs authorized post-observation: desired-exact commits; prior-exact may abort or retry the same idempotent command; foreign or unobservable state is preserved and stops; no ambiguous state is deleted or automatically inverted. Install and uninstall have distinct P/N values and never masquerade rollback as success.

Tests kill before/after spawn, child-start acknowledgement, exec failure, exit, wait, timeout, every journal append/fsync, observation, and parent death. Fake CLIs cover successful/failed/partial writes, background-child rejection, stdout/stderr bounds, process-group behavior, and all four observed classifications. Real pinned CLIs run only in isolated homes. The recovery oracle never depends on the original plugin bundle after EXT_CREATED.

Cancellation is cooperative and stateful:

- Before execution: immediate zero-write cancel.
- Direct unit before PREPARED: record cancel, finish the current safe checkpoint, run journaled abort cleanup, return `CANCELED_CLEAN`.
- Direct unit at/after PREPARED: cancellation becomes stop-after-current; roll the unit forward to N, do not start another unit, return `CANCELED_AFTER_COMMIT` with the committed set.
- External unit before spawn: abort cleanly.
- External child in flight: record `CANCEL_REQUESTED`, signal the process group, wait boundedly, and classify only by post-observation. Timeout/parent death returns `CANCELED_UNKNOWN`/`BUSY_UNKNOWN` and requires recovery; it never reports rollback.

The TUI changes Escape from “instant cancel” to “cancellation requested” once a mutator starts and shows the exact state. Tests cover cancellation before PREPARED, after PREPARED, between every publish step, before/after spawn, timeout, desired/prior/foreign/unobservable outcomes, and the absence of any later-unit start.

## 8. Chosen release payload and acyclic build graph

The release mechanism is now frozen: every `pasture` binary embeds one deterministic ZIP containing the complete delivery manifest and all content/package bytes. ZIP order is canonical; timestamps/extras/platform metadata are normalized; file modes and hashes are in the manifest; the overall digest is generated and checked. No adjacent archive is supported in this wave.

The dependency graph is acyclic:

```text
canonical specs/templates + delivery schema
                  ↓
pure in-memory harness projections
                  ↓
deterministic package/bundle assembler
          ├── generated harness trees
          └── internal/deliverybundle/generated/bundle.zip
                              ↓ go:embed
                    released pasture binary
```

`internal/deliveryspec` owns schema/types and no generated payload. `internal/codegen` owns pure projections and imports only the schema. `tools/codegen` imports those two and writes target trees plus the deterministic ZIP. `internal/deliverybundle` embeds/parses only the checked-in generated ZIP and is imported by the installer/CLI, never by codegen. Thus codegen does not require an already embedded bundle. Bundle schema freezes before harness projections; payload finalization occurs after all projections.

`make generate` runs before build/release, and the drift gate regenerates into an empty root and in place. Nix/Aura consume the same generated manifest/tree from the pinned Pasture source and verify hashes against the embedded manifest. Release checksums include the resulting binary size/content. A source-less, networkless released binary installs every supported cell after acquisition.

# FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-10 — Unified multi-harness installation

Supersedes Proposal 9. Round 9 returned REVISE with 6 BLOCKER and 6 IMPORTANT findings. This revision closes the remaining placement, cross-authority coordination, legacy-discovery, multi-step external operation, payload-oracle, process-lifetime, empty-selection, semantic-digest, conformance, and legacy-provenance gaps. Proposal 9 remains normative except where replaced below; all earlier retained requirements remain in force.

## 1. Package placement is an edge, not content identity

Replace the first two Proposal 9 wire types with:

```go
type ContentArtifact struct {
    ID            ArtifactID
    SemanticOwner ComponentName
    SHA256        Digest
    Bytes          PayloadKey
}

type PackageMember struct {
    Artifact    ArtifactID
    PackagePath SafePath
    Mode        fs.FileMode
    Purpose     MemberPurpose // active, inert-installer-asset, runtime-support
}

type DestinationBinding struct {
    Package      PackageID
    PackagePath  SafePath
    Destination DestinationTemplate
}
```

Content identity is path-independent. `(package ID, package path)` is unique, contained, traversal-free, and resolves exactly one member. Each authority-resolved active destination is an explicit `DestinationBinding`; `(activation unit, resolved destination)` is unique and collision checked. Plugin/package assemblers and executors may not add paths outside these edges.

One `pasture_epoch.toml` content ID is therefore referenced at both `skills/install-codex-agents/assets/agent-bundle/agents/pasture_epoch.toml` in the Codex skills plugin with inert purpose and `pasture_epoch.toml` in the direct Codex-agent package with active purpose. The fixture proves byte/hash identity, two placements, one content record, one native destination, and no emitter-side path table. Mode is placement-specific. The independent YAML oracle and bundle manifest freeze every package path and active destination template.

## 2. One per-cell lease across both authorities

Coordination is independent of lifecycle/recovery authority. Every direct activation, upgrade, disable, uninstall, and rollback uses the same securely created/validated per-cell lease path keyed by resolved home, scope, harness, and component. Companion and Home Manager both acquire the exclusive lease before runtime revalidation and hold it through every native-path change and ownership-manifest publication or removal.

Aura does not delegate Pasture direct cells to ordinary `home.file`/`linkGeneration` steps that cannot hold this lease. Its activation invokes the shared Pasture `HomeManagerLinkReconciler` with immutable Nix-store package paths and the generated authority-specific plan. That reconciler remains journal-free: Home Manager generation state is its rollback authority, but it holds the shared lease, applies the prevalidated ordered link actions, and publishes the Home Manager ownership manifest before releasing. Companion executors acquire the same lease and reject that manifest. Disable/rollback similarly run under the lease.

Lease creation uses Proposal 7's O_EXCL/no-follow/flock identity algorithm; an absent pristine cell normalizes independent of the coordination inode. Apply reruns state/owner checks after acquiring it. Tests deterministically interleave first install, upgrade, rollback, disable, interruption, and recovery between companion and Home Manager at every guard/link/manifest point; exactly one authority commits and the loser reports the winning owner without mutation.

## 3. Complete sparse/empty request grammar

Repeated `--select harness:component` continues to express every nonempty subset. `--select-none` is an explicit, mutually exclusive empty selection. It produces a zero-action install plan; it does not mean uninstall or disable. Removal remains `pasture install uninstall` with explicit selected cells. On a TTY, no selector still launches the wizard; on a non-TTY, neither selector nor `--select-none` is incomplete and fails actionably.

Actual Cobra parsing—not a synthetic post-parse slice—is fixture-tested for all 512 subsets, ordering, duplicates, Cartesian sugar equivalence, malformed/unknown/degraded cells, mutual exclusion, hook consent, and empty no-op behavior across flags, JSON, TUI state, and matching Home Manager intent.

## 4. Legacy Claude observation is a prerequisite for every Claude plan

The legacy all-in-one Claude plugin can change the effective state of all three Claude cells, so its exact active/inactive state is a prerequisite for every nonempty request containing any Claude cell, including direct-only skills or agents. Literal zero-write plan reports `UNKNOWN_DISCOVERY_REQUIRED` until a fresh authorized Claude discovery exists. Declining discovery leaves the Claude cells unavailable and changes nothing.

Apply revalidates the legacy semantic digest under the harness registry lock before any direct or external Claude mutation. If the legacy composite is active, a request that is not exactly all three Claude cells is `CONFLICT_LEGACY_COMPOSITE`; hook consent cannot be satisfied by ignoring it. An exact all-three request is reported `EXTERNALLY_MANAGED` and schedules no duplicate direct/plugin units. Pasture neither adopts nor removes it. Tests cover unknown zero-write state, declined discovery, every Claude singleton/pair/sparse diagonal, exact all-three preservation, stale discovery, CLI absence, and a discovery/apply race.

## 5. Stable semantic discovery versus volatile evidence

Discovery produces two separate records:

```go
type EffectiveState struct {
    Schema              uint32
    Harness             HarnessIdentity // version + executable digest
    Cell                CellID
    Marketplace         MarketplaceSemanticState
    Plugin              PluginSemanticState
    LegacyComposite     LegacySemanticState
    RelevantConfigHash  Digest
}

type DiscoveryEvidence struct {
    ObservedAt          time.Time
    CommandExit         ExitEvidence
    StdoutHash          Digest
    StderrHash          Digest
    FilesystemDelta     []ObservedDelta
    VolatilePaths       []SafePath
    Admissible          bool
}
```

`EffectiveStateDigest` is canonical JSON of stable semantic fields only: schema, exact harness identity, cell, plugin installed/enabled/version/source-package digest, marketplace present/source digest, legacy composite effective cells, and relevant documented config content hash. It excludes timestamps, durations, PID, stdout/stderr, backup/temp names, inode/mtime, and discovery-created but semantically irrelevant files. `DiscoveryEvidence` is append-only audit material linked to the semantic digest. Any unexpected filesystem effect sets `Admissible=false` and blocks planning/apply while preserving evidence; it does not make equality nondeterministic.

The plan binds `EffectiveStateDigest`. Apply's authorized refresh may produce different evidence but must reproduce the same semantic digest. Tests run two discoveries with changed time, backup/temp names, inode/mtime, and output evidence and require equal semantic digests; each semantic field is then mutated individually and must change the digest. Discovery itself uses the durable runner in section 7 and is recoverable; harness-created initialization files are disclosed as persistent harness-owned side effects and are not falsely removed by Pasture uninstall.

## 6. Self-contained external package source

Every external activation unit materializes a persistent content-addressed package source under the Pasture control root. Its marketplace entry points to that stable source, not to a transient extraction, current binary, or Nix generation that may be garbage-collected.

The first complete `EXT_CREATED` record embeds one bounded deterministic package ZIP containing the exact plugin and one-entry marketplace bytes plus member paths, modes, sizes, and hashes. The record size limit is versioned and rejects oversized input before mutation. Journaled WRITE/PUBLISH intents use Proposal 7's prefix/no-follow/fsync oracle to materialize the transaction source and then the persistent source before the first registry command. Canonical external argv references only that persistent source.

Recovery after EXT_CREATED therefore succeeds with the original extraction removed and the running/embedded Pasture bundle replaced. Missing, tampered, oversized, or wrong-prefix transaction/persistent sources are preserved as TAMPERED. Install/upgrade retains the exact persistent source while the marketplace/plugin is owned. Uninstall removes plugin, removes marketplace, commits absence, then uses flattened cleanup for only the exact owned persistent source. Home Manager external cells use the same content-addressed source and journal; their Nix store is an input oracle before EXT_CREATED, not the long-lived registry target.

## 7. Ordered external steps and a Pasture-owned durable runner

An external operation contains a closed ordered `[]ExternalStep`; singular argv is removed. Initial Codex/Claude install is:

```text
0 MATERIALIZE_SOURCE
1 MARKETPLACE_ADD
2 PLUGIN_ADD
3 VERIFY_EFFECTIVE_STATE
```

Uninstall is `PLUGIN_REMOVE -> MARKETPLACE_REMOVE -> VERIFY_ABSENT -> CLEAN_SOURCE`; upgrade has an explicitly generated old/new step graph. Each step freezes its adapter operation, canonical arguments, exact prior vector, exact desired vector, timeout, and postcondition. The journal has `STEP_i_INTENT`, `STEP_i_CHILD_ARMED`, `STEP_i_CHILD_STARTED`, `STEP_i_EXIT`, `STEP_i_POSTCHECK`, and `STEP_i_COMPLETE`. Marketplace-only, plugin-removed/marketplace-present, and source-materialized states are known owned intermediates tied to a step index, never collapsed into foreign.

PREPARED, durably appended after package materialization and full plan revalidation, commits the external unit to its operation-specific direction. Cancellation before PREPARED aborts exact staging. At/after PREPARED it becomes stop-after-unit: the runner classifies the current child outcome and completes the remaining known steps to N before returning `CANCELED_AFTER_COMMIT`; it starts no later unit. Only a truly foreign/unobservable outcome can stop earlier as `CANCELED_RECOVERY_REQUIRED`, preserving all candidates for explicit recovery in the same direction. Every step/record/fsync/spawn/exit/observation/cancel boundary is fault injected for both commands and both harnesses.

The frontend never directly owns a harness child. It launches a hidden Pasture-owned delivery runner with only a validated transaction ID. The runner reopens the secure journal, acquires and holds the harness registry lock, owns journal appends, starts each harness command in a new process group, waits, performs post-observation, handles cancellation, and continues safely if the TUI/Home Manager/frontend process dies.

Before a harness command may execute, a start-gated child is spawned; the runner records and fsyncs the PID, platform process-start token, executable identity, step, and process group, then releases the gate for exec. Linux reads `/proc/<pid>/stat` start time; macOS uses the pinned `proc_pidinfo`/`sysctl` equivalent. Every Pasture operation under that harness lock scans incomplete external journals before mutation. If the runner itself dies, recovery distinguishes PID reuse, waits while the exact child is live, and never retries concurrently. When it exits, recovery observes the step vector and resumes. Cancellation records intent, signals the exact process group, waits boundedly, escalates, then classifies only by observation.

Pinned real commands must prove they do not daemonize mutation and do not return before descendant registry work completes. Fake tests cover daemon/background rejection. Tests kill frontend, runner, start-gated wrapper, and harness child at every boundary on Linux and macOS; live-child and reused-PID cases cannot start another mutation. The registry lock is still held by the healthy runner, but safety never depends on an arbitrary harness retaining an inherited descriptor.

Discovery is an external runner operation with no mutation steps beyond its supported observer command. Crash/recovery records or finishes evidence; it never retries a live child or cleans harness-owned observer side effects.

# FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-11 — Unified multi-harness installation

Supersedes Proposal 10. Proposal 10 remains normative except where this revision replaces it. Round 10 returned REVISE on intent-mode parity, the external commit boundary, start-gate and executable identity, exact lifecycle fixtures, Claude-row projection, the OpenCode commit pin, and role-filter provenance. This revision closes each finding without changing product scope.

## 1. Intent mode is part of the wire contract

```go
type IntentMode string

const (
    EnsureSelected IntentMode = "ensure-selected"
    ReconcileExact IntentMode = "reconcile-exact"
)

type InstallRequest struct {
    Schema       uint32
    Authority    DeliveryAuthority
    Mode         IntentMode
    Operation    InstallOperation
    Selected     []CellID
    EnabledRoles []RoleID
}
```

Companion TUI, flags, and JSON use `ENSURE_SELECTED`: selected cells are installed/upgraded and every unselected cell is out of scope. `--select-none` is therefore a literal no-op. Explicit companion uninstall remains a separate operation over selected cells.

Home Manager uses `RECONCILE_EXACT`: after legacy/default option normalization, its declaration is the complete desired set for Home-Manager-owned cells. Omitted Home Manager cells are removed; companion- or foreign-owned cells are conflicts, not implicit uninstall targets. An empty Home Manager declaration disables only Home-Manager-owned cells. Mode and authority are included in plan and consent digests.

Fixtures run two independent exhaustive suites: all 512 matrices through actual Cobra/TUI/JSON parsing under `ENSURE_SELECTED`, and all 512 normalized Home Manager matrices under `RECONCILE_EXACT`. There is no cross-mode plan-equality assertion. Each suite freezes create/update/remove/no-op actions, ownership effects, empty selection, and repeated clean application.

## 2. Role selection has one typed projection edge

```go
type SkillDescriptor struct {
    ID        SkillID
    Role      *RoleID // nil is a core skill and is always retained
    Artifacts map[HarnessName]ArtifactID
}

type ArtifactProjection struct {
    Artifact ArtifactID
    Skill    SkillID
    Role     *RoleID
}

type DeliveryPackage struct {
    ID          PackageID
    Harness     HarnessName
    Members     []PackageMember
    Effects     []CellID
    Granularity ProjectionGranularity // member-prunable or indivisible
}
```

The canonical `SkillDescriptor`/`RoleSpec` graph generates `ArtifactProjection`; emitters cannot author a second map. Aura reads this edge from the generated bundle manifest and removes filename-prefix filtering. A role filter affects role-scoped skills only; core skills remain selected and the agent component remains the complete five-agent set.

Claude Code and OpenCode direct skill packages are member-prunable. The Codex skills plugin is indivisible, so selecting Codex skills with any narrowed role set fails before mutation with `UNSUPPORTED_INDIVISIBLE_PROJECTION`, explaining that the plugin would expose the full skill set and how to select all roles or omit that cell. It never claims pruned parity. Fixtures cover all 32 role subsets, each single-role toggle, mixed direct/plugin matrices, manifest membership, active destinations, effect reporting, and Home Manager normalization without ID/path parsing.

## 3. Legacy Claude compares only the Claude row

Legacy discovery is required for a plan whose projected Claude row is nonempty (and for an exact-reconcile transition that touches an already owned Claude cell). It is never keyed to the whole nine-cell selection.

- Active legacy composite + all three Claude cells: those three cells are `EXTERNALLY_MANAGED`; any selected OpenCode/Codex cells still plan normally.
- Active legacy composite + a sparse Claude row: the Claude row is `CONFLICT_LEGACY_COMPOSITE`.
- Inactive legacy composite: modern direct/plugin units plan normally.
- Empty Claude row: no legacy observation prerequisite is introduced by other harnesses.
- Unknown, declined, stale, unavailable-CLI, and apply-race evidence retain Proposal 10's zero-write/discovery rules.

Tests cross all seven nonempty Claude-row subsets with all 64 subsets of the other six cells under active, inactive, unknown, declined, stale, unavailable-CLI, and apply-time-changed observations. They assert that an all-three Claude row is recognized regardless of other-harness selections and that non-Claude action shapes are unchanged by the projection.

## 4. Staging is pre-commit; persistent publication is post-commit

`EXT_CREATED` still embeds the bounded deterministic package ZIP. Before `PREPARED`, `STAGE_SOURCE` expands and fsyncs only a transaction-local source under the Pasture control root, and `STAGE_EXECUTABLE` creates the exact private harness snapshot described below. Both remain abortable transaction state. Full plan/state/lease revalidation runs after staging; only then is `PREPARED` appended and fsynced.

The first post-`PREPARED` external step is `PUBLISH_PERSISTENT_SOURCE`. It atomically promotes the staged source on the same filesystem into the cell- and digest-qualified persistent path, fsyncs the destination and parents, and records its postcondition. Existing-exact is an explicit no-op. Absent, exact stage-only, exact destination-only, published-but-unrecorded, prefix/partial, wrong digest, symlink, and foreign/tampered states are distinct fixtures. No persistent marketplace source exists before `PREPARED`; after it, recovery only rolls forward. Missing or altered committed staging is tampered and preserved, never silently reconstructed from a different binary.

Install begins `PUBLISH_N`; upgrade/downgrade publish N while retaining P until N is verified; uninstall has no publish step. `MATERIALIZE_SOURCE` is removed from the post-commit graph and from all prior fixtures.

## 5. Fail-closed gate and immutable executable object

The runner resolves the pinned CLI through a bounded no-follow path walk, opens the final regular native executable, and copies bytes from that descriptor into a private transaction-owned executable snapshot. It rejects scripts/wrappers, validates the exact pinned release digest and native format, fsyncs file and parent, makes the snapshot non-writable, and records digest/device/inode. This snapshot—not PATH, the original symlink, or a mutable Nix profile—is the operation's executable object. Linux uses descriptor execution where available; Darwin executes the private immutable snapshot path under the still-held transaction/registry authority. The snapshot remains until the unit and recovery are complete.

For each CLI step the runner creates two private channels: an expected-token descriptor preloaded before spawn and a release pipe whose write end exists only in the runner. The wrapper inherits the expected-token read end, release read end, and executable descriptor, but never a release writer. The runner spawns it in a new process group, obtains PID/platform start token, and appends and fsyncs:

```text
STEP_i_CHILD_ARMED { pid, start_token, pgid, executable_digest, device, inode, token_hash }
```

Only after that fsync succeeds does the runner issue one fixed authenticated frame, bounded by `PIPE_BUF`, in one write. The wrapper performs an exact constant-time comparison. EOF, zero/short/extra/invalid frame, timeout, runner death, closed expected-token descriptor, or any executable identity mismatch exits with a dedicated no-exec result and closes the executable descriptor. A full release write can race runner death only after `CHILD_ARMED` is durable; recovery then waits for/classifies the exact PID/start token and never retries concurrently. The wrapper closes both gates before exec and creates no shell or daemon child.

Fault tests kill frontend, runner, wrapper, and harness around create/spawn, PID observation, journal append/fsync, release write, exec, exit, and postcheck. They prove zero-child and exactly-one-child shapes, fail-closed EOF, bounded orphan exit, PID/PGID reuse, and recovery after a released child. Path, symlink, inode, executable-content, and Nix-generation swaps before and after `PREPARED` either reject before commit or execute the exact transaction snapshot; they can never switch the exec object.

## 6. Exact external lifecycle graphs and argv

Each external cell has digest-qualified marketplace name `M_<digest>`, persistent source `S_<digest>`, and selector `Q_<digest>=plugin@marketplace`. Old and desired states are P and N. The checked-in YAML oracle freezes these vectors:

| Adapter operation | Claude Code 2.1.207 argv | Codex 0.144.1 argv |
|---|---|---|
| `MARKETPLACE_ADD_N` | `plugin marketplace add --scope user S_N` | `plugin marketplace add --json S_N` |
| `MARKETPLACE_LIST` | `plugin marketplace list --json` | `plugin marketplace list --json` |
| `PLUGIN_ADD_N` | `plugin install --scope user Q_N` | `plugin add --json Q_N` |
| `PLUGIN_REMOVE_P` | `plugin uninstall --scope user Q_P` | `plugin remove --json Q_P` |
| `PLUGIN_LIST` | `plugin list --available --json` | `plugin list --available --json` |
| `MARKETPLACE_REMOVE_P` | `plugin marketplace remove --scope user M_P` | `plugin marketplace remove --json M_P` |

No adapter uses `plugin update`: neither command binds an explicit immutable local desired source. The operation graphs are:

```text
INSTALL:
  PUBLISH_N -> MARKETPLACE_ADD_N -> MARKETPLACE_LIST_N ->
  PLUGIN_ADD_N -> PLUGIN_LIST_N -> ASSERT_N

UPGRADE / authorized DOWNGRADE:
  PUBLISH_N -> MARKETPLACE_ADD_N -> MARKETPLACE_LIST_PN ->
  PLUGIN_REMOVE_P -> PLUGIN_LIST_NOT_P ->
  PLUGIN_ADD_N -> PLUGIN_LIST_N ->
  MARKETPLACE_REMOVE_P -> MARKETPLACE_LIST_N ->
  CLEAN_P -> ASSERT_N

UNINSTALL:
  PLUGIN_REMOVE_P -> PLUGIN_LIST_ABSENT ->
  MARKETPLACE_REMOVE_P -> MARKETPLACE_LIST_ABSENT ->
  CLEAN_P -> ASSERT_ABSENT
```

Every list is its own journaled observer child, not an opaque postcheck spawn. Pure `ASSERT_*` steps compare the exact observed source/marketplace/plugin vector. Each graph has independent Claude and Codex fixtures for clean install, upgrade, downgrade, uninstall, already-satisfied no-op, crash recovery, cancellation, and P/N/both/absent/foreign/tampered states. The full fault matrix covers source promotion, every step record/fsync/gate/spawn/exit/observation, and exact authorized cleanup. Known intermediates roll forward; additional identities remain foreign and are never removed.

# FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-11 — Unified multi-harness installation

Supersedes Proposal 10. Proposal 10 remains normative except where this revision replaces it. Round 10 returned REVISE on intent-mode parity, the external commit boundary, start-gate and executable identity, exact lifecycle fixtures, Claude-row projection, the OpenCode commit pin, and role-filter provenance. This revision closes each finding without changing product scope.

## 1. Intent mode is part of the wire contract

```go
type IntentMode string

const (
    EnsureSelected IntentMode = "ensure-selected"
    ReconcileExact IntentMode = "reconcile-exact"
)

type InstallRequest struct {
    Schema       uint32
    Authority    DeliveryAuthority
    Mode         IntentMode
    Operation    InstallOperation
    Selected     []CellID
    EnabledRoles []RoleID
}
```

Companion TUI, flags, and JSON use `ENSURE_SELECTED`: selected cells are installed/upgraded and every unselected cell is out of scope. `--select-none` is therefore a literal no-op. Explicit companion uninstall remains a separate operation over selected cells.

Home Manager uses `RECONCILE_EXACT`: after legacy/default option normalization, its declaration is the complete desired set for Home-Manager-owned cells. Omitted Home Manager cells are removed; companion- or foreign-owned cells are conflicts, not implicit uninstall targets. An empty Home Manager declaration disables only Home-Manager-owned cells. Mode and authority are included in plan and consent digests.

Fixtures run two independent exhaustive suites: all 512 matrices through actual Cobra/TUI/JSON parsing under `ENSURE_SELECTED`, and all 512 normalized Home Manager matrices under `RECONCILE_EXACT`. There is no cross-mode plan-equality assertion. Each suite freezes create/update/remove/no-op actions, ownership effects, empty selection, and repeated clean application.

## 2. Role selection has one typed projection edge

```go
type SkillDescriptor struct {
    ID        SkillID
    Role      *RoleID // nil is a core skill and is always retained
    Artifacts map[HarnessName]ArtifactID
}

type ArtifactProjection struct {
    Artifact ArtifactID
    Skill    SkillID
    Role     *RoleID
}

type DeliveryPackage struct {
    ID          PackageID
    Harness     HarnessName
    Members     []PackageMember
    Effects     []CellID
    Granularity ProjectionGranularity // member-prunable or indivisible
}
```

The canonical `SkillDescriptor`/`RoleSpec` graph generates `ArtifactProjection`; emitters cannot author a second map. Aura reads this edge from the generated bundle manifest and removes filename-prefix filtering. A role filter affects role-scoped skills only; core skills remain selected and the agent component remains the complete five-agent set.

Claude Code and OpenCode direct skill packages are member-prunable. The Codex skills plugin is indivisible, so selecting Codex skills with any narrowed role set fails before mutation with `UNSUPPORTED_INDIVISIBLE_PROJECTION`, explaining that the plugin would expose the full skill set and how to select all roles or omit that cell. It never claims pruned parity. Fixtures cover all 32 role subsets, each single-role toggle, mixed direct/plugin matrices, manifest membership, active destinations, effect reporting, and Home Manager normalization without ID/path parsing.

## 3. Legacy Claude compares only the Claude row

Legacy discovery is required for a plan whose projected Claude row is nonempty (and for an exact-reconcile transition that touches an already owned Claude cell). It is never keyed to the whole nine-cell selection.

- Active legacy composite + all three Claude cells: those three cells are `EXTERNALLY_MANAGED`; any selected OpenCode/Codex cells still plan normally.
- Active legacy composite + a sparse Claude row: the Claude row is `CONFLICT_LEGACY_COMPOSITE`.
- Inactive legacy composite: modern direct/plugin units plan normally.
- Empty Claude row: no legacy observation prerequisite is introduced by other harnesses.
- Unknown, declined, stale, unavailable-CLI, and apply-race evidence retain Proposal 10's zero-write/discovery rules.

Tests cross all seven nonempty Claude-row subsets with all 64 subsets of the other six cells under active, inactive, unknown, declined, stale, unavailable-CLI, and apply-time-changed observations. They assert that an all-three Claude row is recognized regardless of other-harness selections and that non-Claude action shapes are unchanged by the projection.

## 4. Staging is pre-commit; persistent publication is post-commit

`EXT_CREATED` still embeds the bounded deterministic package ZIP. Before `PREPARED`, `STAGE_SOURCE` expands and fsyncs only a transaction-local source under the Pasture control root, and `STAGE_EXECUTABLE` creates the exact private harness snapshot described below. Both remain abortable transaction state. Full plan/state/lease revalidation runs after staging; only then is `PREPARED` appended and fsynced.

The first post-`PREPARED` external step is `PUBLISH_PERSISTENT_SOURCE`. It atomically promotes the staged source on the same filesystem into the cell- and digest-qualified persistent path, fsyncs the destination and parents, and records its postcondition. Existing-exact is an explicit no-op. Absent, exact stage-only, exact destination-only, published-but-unrecorded, prefix/partial, wrong digest, symlink, and foreign/tampered states are distinct fixtures. No persistent marketplace source exists before `PREPARED`; after it, recovery only rolls forward. Missing or altered committed staging is tampered and preserved, never silently reconstructed from a different binary.

Install begins `PUBLISH_N`; upgrade/downgrade publish N while retaining P until N is verified; uninstall has no publish step. `MATERIALIZE_SOURCE` is removed from the post-commit graph and from all prior fixtures.

## 5. Fail-closed gate and immutable executable object

The runner resolves the pinned CLI through a bounded no-follow path walk, opens the final regular native executable, and copies bytes from that descriptor into a private transaction-owned executable snapshot. It rejects scripts/wrappers, validates the exact pinned release digest and native format, fsyncs file and parent, makes the snapshot non-writable, and records digest/device/inode. This snapshot—not PATH, the original symlink, or a mutable Nix profile—is the operation's executable object. Linux uses descriptor execution where available; Darwin executes the private immutable snapshot path under the still-held transaction/registry authority. The snapshot remains until the unit and recovery are complete.

For each CLI step the runner creates two private channels: an expected-token descriptor preloaded before spawn and a release pipe whose write end exists only in the runner. The wrapper inherits the expected-token read end, release read end, and executable descriptor, but never a release writer. The runner spawns it in a new process group, obtains PID/platform start token, and appends and fsyncs:

```text
STEP_i_CHILD_ARMED { pid, start_token, pgid, executable_digest, device, inode, token_hash }
```

Only after that fsync succeeds does the runner issue one fixed authenticated frame, bounded by `PIPE_BUF`, in one write, and immediately close its sole release writer. The wrapper reads through EOF and performs an exact constant-time comparison, so it can distinguish exactly one complete frame from a short or extended stream before exec. EOF with zero/short/extra/invalid bytes, timeout, runner death, closed expected-token descriptor, or any executable identity mismatch exits with a dedicated no-exec result and closes the executable descriptor. A full release write can race runner death only after `CHILD_ARMED` is durable; recovery then waits for/classifies the exact PID/start token and never retries concurrently. The wrapper closes both gates before exec and creates no shell or daemon child.

Fault tests kill frontend, runner, wrapper, and harness around create/spawn, PID observation, journal append/fsync, release write, exec, exit, and postcheck. They prove zero-child and exactly-one-child shapes, fail-closed EOF, bounded orphan exit, PID/PGID reuse, and recovery after a released child. Path, symlink, inode, executable-content, and Nix-generation swaps before and after `PREPARED` either reject before commit or execute the exact transaction snapshot; they can never switch the exec object.

## 6. Exact external lifecycle graphs and argv

Each external cell has digest-qualified marketplace name `M_<digest>`, persistent source `S_<digest>`, and selector `Q_<digest>=plugin@marketplace`. Old and desired states are P and N. The checked-in YAML oracle freezes these vectors:

| Adapter operation | Claude Code 2.1.207 argv | Codex 0.144.1 argv |
|---|---|---|
| `MARKETPLACE_ADD_N` | `plugin marketplace add --scope user S_N` | `plugin marketplace add --json S_N` |
| `MARKETPLACE_LIST` | `plugin marketplace list --json` | `plugin marketplace list --json` |
| `PLUGIN_ADD_N` | `plugin install --scope user Q_N` | `plugin add --json Q_N` |
| `PLUGIN_REMOVE_P` | `plugin uninstall --scope user Q_P` | `plugin remove --json Q_P` |
| `PLUGIN_LIST` | `plugin list --available --json` | `plugin list --available --json` |
| `MARKETPLACE_REMOVE_P` | `plugin marketplace remove --scope user M_P` | `plugin marketplace remove --json M_P` |

No adapter uses `plugin update`: neither command binds an explicit immutable local desired source. The operation graphs are:

```text
INSTALL:
  PUBLISH_N -> MARKETPLACE_ADD_N -> MARKETPLACE_LIST_N ->
  PLUGIN_ADD_N -> PLUGIN_LIST_N -> ASSERT_N

UPGRADE / authorized DOWNGRADE:
  PUBLISH_N -> MARKETPLACE_ADD_N -> MARKETPLACE_LIST_PN ->
  PLUGIN_REMOVE_P -> PLUGIN_LIST_NOT_P ->
  PLUGIN_ADD_N -> PLUGIN_LIST_N ->
  MARKETPLACE_REMOVE_P -> MARKETPLACE_LIST_N ->
  CLEAN_P -> ASSERT_N

UNINSTALL:
  PLUGIN_REMOVE_P -> PLUGIN_LIST_ABSENT ->
  MARKETPLACE_REMOVE_P -> MARKETPLACE_LIST_ABSENT ->
  CLEAN_P -> ASSERT_ABSENT
```

Every list is its own journaled observer child, not an opaque postcheck spawn. Pure `ASSERT_*` steps compare the exact observed source/marketplace/plugin vector. Each graph has independent Claude and Codex fixtures for clean install, upgrade, downgrade, uninstall, already-satisfied no-op, crash recovery, cancellation, and P/N/both/absent/foreign/tampered states. The full fault matrix covers source promotion, every step record/fsync/gate/spawn/exit/observation, and exact authorized cleanup. Known intermediates roll forward; additional identities remain foreign and are never removed.

## 7. Correct OpenCode provenance

The OpenCode 1.17.18 tag resolves to commit `b1fc8113948b518835c2a39ece49553cffe9b30c`; the GitHub release `targetCommitish` value used in Proposal 10 is not the tag commit and is removed. Fixtures rederive the four archive hashes, `@opencode-ai/plugin@1.17.18` integrity, `@opencode-ai/sdk@1.17.18` integrity, and locked transitive closure from that single publication. A mismatch-negative fixture substitutes the discarded commit and must fail provenance validation.

## 8. Acceptance additions

Proposal 10's acceptance cases remain, with these replacements/additions:

1. Separate 512-case `ENSURE_SELECTED` and 512-case `RECONCILE_EXACT` suites prove their distinct empty/omitted semantics.
2. All role projections come from `SkillDescriptor -> ArtifactProjection`; direct packages prune correctly and narrowed Codex skills fail actionably as indivisible.
3. Legacy composite matching is the Claude-row projection across `7 × 64` selection shapes and every discovery state.
4. The transaction exposes no persistent source before `PREPARED`; `PUBLISH_N` is the first post-commit step and survives every promotion crash point.
5. Gate EOF/runner death before a full authenticated release executes zero harnesses; after release, durable child identity prevents concurrent retry.
6. The verified transaction snapshot is the exec object despite PATH, symlink, inode, or Nix-generation swaps.
7. Exact Claude/Codex install, upgrade, downgrade, and uninstall graphs pass their P/N vector and full fault suites.
8. OpenCode provenance accepts only tag commit `b1fc8113948b518835c2a39ece49553cffe9b30c` with the frozen matching artifacts.

## Plan UAT decisions

Proposal 10's inherited Plan UAT decisions remain unchanged. Acceptance additionally confirms: companion sparse intent and Home Manager exact intent are deliberately different; a narrowed role filter makes the monolithic Codex skills cell unavailable; external upgrade/downgrade may have a bounded post-commit interval with P removed before N is active but deterministically rolls forward; and harness discovery/verification can leave documented harness-owned initialization/cache files that Pasture reports but does not uninstall.
