# FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-11 — Unified multi-harness installation

Supersedes Proposal 10. Proposal 10 remains normative except where this revision replaces it. Round 10 returned REVISE on intent-mode parity, the external commit boundary, start-gate and executable identity, exact lifecycle fixtures, Claude-row projection, the OpenCode commit pin, and role-filter provenance. This revision closes each finding without changing product scope.

## 1. Intent mode is part of the wire contract

```go
type IntentMode string

const (
    EnsureSelected IntentMode = "ensure-selected"
    ReconcileExact IntentMode = "reconcile-exact"
)

type InstallRequest struct {
    Schema       uint32
    Authority    DeliveryAuthority
    Mode         IntentMode
    Operation    InstallOperation
    Selected     []CellID
    EnabledRoles []RoleID
}
```

Companion TUI, flags, and JSON use `ENSURE_SELECTED`: selected cells are installed/upgraded and every unselected cell is out of scope. `--select-none` is therefore a literal no-op. Explicit companion uninstall remains a separate operation over selected cells.

Home Manager uses `RECONCILE_EXACT`: after legacy/default option normalization, its declaration is the complete desired set for Home-Manager-owned cells. Omitted Home Manager cells are removed; companion- or foreign-owned cells are conflicts, not implicit uninstall targets. An empty Home Manager declaration disables only Home-Manager-owned cells. Mode and authority are included in plan and consent digests.

Fixtures run two independent exhaustive suites: all 512 matrices through actual Cobra/TUI/JSON parsing under `ENSURE_SELECTED`, and all 512 normalized Home Manager matrices under `RECONCILE_EXACT`. There is no cross-mode plan-equality assertion. Each suite freezes create/update/remove/no-op actions, ownership effects, empty selection, and repeated clean application.

## 2. Role selection has one typed projection edge

```go
type SkillDescriptor struct {
    ID   SkillID
    Role *RoleID // nil is a core skill and is always retained
}

type ArtifactProjection struct {
    Harness  HarnessName
    Artifact ArtifactID
    Skill    SkillID
    Role     *RoleID
}

type DeliveryPackage struct {
    ID          PackageID
    Harness     HarnessName
    Members     []PackageMember
    Effects     []CellID
    Granularity ProjectionGranularity // member-prunable or indivisible
}
```

The canonical `SkillDescriptor`/`RoleSpec` graph generates one canonically sorted `[]ArtifactProjection`; emitters cannot author a second map. Aura reads this edge from the generated bundle manifest and removes filename-prefix filtering. A role filter affects role-scoped skills only; core skills remain selected and the agent component remains the complete five-agent set.

Claude Code and OpenCode direct skill packages are member-prunable. The Codex skills plugin is indivisible, so selecting Codex skills with any narrowed role set fails before mutation with `UNSUPPORTED_INDIVISIBLE_PROJECTION`, explaining that the plugin would expose the full skill set and how to select all roles or omit that cell. It never claims pruned parity. Fixtures cover all 32 role subsets, each single-role toggle, mixed direct/plugin matrices, manifest membership, active destinations, effect reporting, and Home Manager normalization without ID/path parsing.

## 3. Legacy Claude compares only the Claude row

Legacy discovery is required for a plan whose projected Claude row is nonempty (and for an exact-reconcile transition that touches an already owned Claude cell). It is never keyed to the whole nine-cell selection.

- Active legacy composite + all three Claude cells: those three cells are `EXTERNALLY_MANAGED`; any selected OpenCode/Codex cells still plan normally.
- Active legacy composite + a sparse Claude row: the Claude row is `CONFLICT_LEGACY_COMPOSITE`.
- Inactive legacy composite: modern direct/plugin units plan normally.
- Empty Claude row: no legacy observation prerequisite is introduced by other harnesses.
- Unknown, declined, stale, unavailable-CLI, and apply-race evidence retain Proposal 10's zero-write/discovery rules.

Tests cross all seven nonempty Claude-row subsets with all 64 subsets of the other six cells under active, inactive, unknown, declined, stale, unavailable-CLI, and apply-time-changed observations. They assert that an all-three Claude row is recognized regardless of other-harness selections and that non-Claude action shapes are unchanged by the projection.

## 4. Staging is pre-commit; persistent publication is post-commit

`EXT_CREATED` still embeds the bounded deterministic package ZIP. Before `PREPARED`, `STAGE_SOURCE` expands and fsyncs only a transaction-local source under the Pasture control root, and `STAGE_EXECUTABLE` creates the exact private harness snapshot described below. Both remain abortable transaction state. Full plan/state/lease revalidation runs after staging; only then is `PREPARED` appended and fsynced.

The first post-`PREPARED` external step is `PUBLISH_PERSISTENT_SOURCE`. It atomically promotes the staged source on the same filesystem into the cell- and digest-qualified persistent path, fsyncs the destination and parents, and records its postcondition. Existing-exact is an explicit no-op. Absent, exact stage-only, exact destination-only, published-but-unrecorded, prefix/partial, wrong digest, symlink, and foreign/tampered states are distinct fixtures. No persistent marketplace source exists before `PREPARED`; after it, recovery only rolls forward. Missing or altered committed staging is tampered and preserved, never silently reconstructed from a different binary.

Install begins `PUBLISH_N`; upgrade/downgrade publish N while retaining P until N is verified; uninstall has no publish step. `MATERIALIZE_SOURCE` is removed from the post-commit graph and from all prior fixtures.

## 5. Fail-closed gate and immutable executable object

The runner resolves the pinned CLI through a bounded no-follow path walk, opens the final regular native executable, and copies bytes from that descriptor into a private transaction-owned executable snapshot. It rejects scripts/wrappers, validates the exact pinned release digest and native format, fsyncs file and parent, makes the snapshot non-writable, and records digest/device/inode. This snapshot—not PATH, the original symlink, or a mutable Nix profile—is the operation's executable object. Linux uses descriptor execution where available; Darwin executes the private immutable snapshot path under the still-held transaction/registry authority. The snapshot remains until the unit and recovery are complete.

For each CLI step the runner creates two private channels: an expected-token descriptor preloaded before spawn and a release pipe whose write end exists only in the runner. The wrapper inherits the expected-token read end, release read end, and executable descriptor, but never a release writer. The runner spawns it in a new process group, obtains PID/platform start token, and appends and fsyncs:

```text
STEP_i_CHILD_ARMED { pid, start_token, pgid, executable_digest, device, inode, token_hash }
```

Only after that fsync succeeds does the runner issue one fixed authenticated frame, bounded by `PIPE_BUF`, in one write, and immediately close its sole release writer. The wrapper reads through EOF and performs an exact constant-time comparison, so it can distinguish exactly one complete frame from a short or extended stream before exec. EOF with zero/short/extra/invalid bytes, timeout, runner death, closed expected-token descriptor, or any executable identity mismatch exits with a dedicated no-exec result and closes the executable descriptor. A full release write can race runner death only after `CHILD_ARMED` is durable; recovery then waits for/classifies the exact PID/start token and never retries concurrently. The wrapper closes both gates before exec and creates no shell or daemon child.

Fault tests kill frontend, runner, wrapper, and harness around create/spawn, PID observation, journal append/fsync, release write, exec, exit, and postcheck. They prove zero-child and exactly-one-child shapes, fail-closed EOF, bounded orphan exit, PID/PGID reuse, and recovery after a released child. Path, symlink, inode, executable-content, and Nix-generation swaps before and after `PREPARED` either reject before commit or execute the exact transaction snapshot; they can never switch the exec object.

Each external cell has digest-qualified marketplace name `M_<digest>`, persistent source `S_<digest>`, and selector `Q_<digest>=plugin@marketplace`. Old and desired states are P and N. The checked-in YAML oracle freezes these vectors:

| Adapter operation | Claude Code 2.1.207 argv | Codex 0.144.1 argv |
|---|---|---|
| `MARKETPLACE_ADD_N` | `plugin marketplace add --scope user S_N` | `plugin marketplace add --json S_N` |
| `MARKETPLACE_LIST` | `plugin marketplace list --json` | `plugin marketplace list --json` |
| `PLUGIN_ADD_N` | `plugin install --scope user Q_N` | `plugin add --json Q_N` |
| `PLUGIN_REMOVE_P` | `plugin uninstall --scope user Q_P` | `plugin remove --json Q_P` |
| `PLUGIN_LIST` | `plugin list --available --json` | `plugin list --available --json` |
| `MARKETPLACE_REMOVE_P` | `plugin marketplace remove --scope user M_P` | `plugin marketplace remove --json M_P` |

No adapter uses `plugin update`: neither command binds an explicit immutable local desired source. The operation graphs are:

```text
INSTALL:
  PUBLISH_N -> MARKETPLACE_ADD_N -> MARKETPLACE_LIST_N ->
  PLUGIN_ADD_N -> PLUGIN_LIST_N -> ASSERT_N

UPGRADE / authorized DOWNGRADE:
  PUBLISH_N -> MARKETPLACE_ADD_N -> MARKETPLACE_LIST_PN ->
  PLUGIN_REMOVE_P -> PLUGIN_LIST_NOT_P ->
  PLUGIN_ADD_N -> PLUGIN_LIST_N ->
  MARKETPLACE_REMOVE_P -> MARKETPLACE_LIST_N ->
  CLEAN_P -> ASSERT_N

UNINSTALL:
  PLUGIN_REMOVE_P -> PLUGIN_LIST_ABSENT ->
  MARKETPLACE_REMOVE_P -> MARKETPLACE_LIST_ABSENT ->
  CLEAN_P -> ASSERT_ABSENT
```

Every list is its own journaled observer child, not an opaque postcheck spawn. Pure `ASSERT_*` steps compare the exact observed source/marketplace/plugin vector. Each graph has independent Claude and Codex fixtures for clean install, upgrade, downgrade, uninstall, already-satisfied no-op, crash recovery, cancellation, and P/N/both/absent/foreign/tampered states. The full fault matrix covers source promotion, every step record/fsync/gate/spawn/exit/observation, and exact authorized cleanup. Known intermediates roll forward; additional identities remain foreign and are never removed.

The OpenCode 1.17.18 tag resolves to commit `b1fc8113948b518835c2a39ece49553cffe9b30c`; the GitHub release `targetCommitish` value used in Proposal 10 is not the tag commit and is removed. 2. All role projections come from `SkillDescriptor -> ArtifactProjection`; direct packages prune correctly and narrowed Codex skills fail actionably as indivisible.

6. The verified transaction snapshot is the exec object despite PATH, symlink, inode, or Nix-generation swaps.
7. Exact Claude/Codex install, upgrade, downgrade, and uninstall graphs pass their P/N vector and full fault suites.
8. OpenCode provenance accepts only tag commit `b1fc8113948b518835c2a39ece49553cffe9b30c` with the frozen matching artifacts.

Proposal 10's inherited Plan UAT decisions remain unchanged. Acceptance additionally confirms: companion sparse intent and Home Manager exact intent are deliberately different; a narrowed role filter makes the monolithic Codex skills cell unavailable; external upgrade/downgrade may have a bounded post-commit interval with P removed before N is active but deterministically rolls forward; and harness discovery/verification can leave documented harness-owned initialization/cache files that Pasture reports but does not uninstall.

# FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-12 — Unified multi-harness installation

Supersedes Proposal 11. Proposals 7–11 remain normative except where replaced here. Round 11 found two executable-object blockers and eight test/algebra/integration findings. This revision removes executable copying entirely, binds every process launch to verified open objects, supports the pinned Nix Codex closure explicitly, closes the public request algebra, and freezes the missing matrices and independent oracles.

## 1. Executables are bound descriptors, not staged files

Delete `STAGE_EXECUTABLE`, `STAGE_HELPER`, every executable-copy candidate, and Proposal 11's Darwin path snapshot. Executable bytes never enter transaction staging, so no 100–400 MB partial executable exists and R52's prefix oracle remains limited to package/ledger payloads whose canonical bytes are embedded by `EXT_CREATED`.

```go
type BoundExecutableClosure struct {
    Provider       ExecutableProvider // official-native or nix-wrapper-v1
    Harness        HarnessName        // pasture-helper, claude-code, codex
    Version        Semver
    Protocol       uint32             // required for pasture-helper
    Objects        []BoundObject      // canonical purpose order
    Environment    []EnvironmentEdit
    CanonicalArgv0 string
    Digest         Digest             // canonical closure digest
}

type BoundObject struct {
    Purpose    ObjectPurpose // helper, wrapper-source, interpreter, native-target, runtime-support
    SourceFD   uintptr       // process-local provenance fd; never serialized
    ImageFD    uintptr       // immutable execution image; never serialized
    ImageKind  ImageKind     // immutable-source, linux-sealed-memfd, darwin-apfs-clone
    SHA256     Digest
    Device     uint64
    Inode      uint64
    Provenance ProvenanceID
}
```

The process resolves each closure with a bounded no-follow walk, opens every required regular source object, validates bytes/provenance, and derives an immutable execution image before computing the closure digest. Root-owned immutable Nix/system objects may be used directly. A mutable Linux source is copied only into an anonymous `memfd`, hash-verified, and write/grow/shrink/seal sealed; a crash drops the anonymous object and leaves no candidate. A mutable Darwin source is atomically cloned from the verified source descriptor with `fclonefileat` onto the same APFS volume, opened read-only, hash-verified, then unlinked and parent-fsynced before any release; the live descriptor is the image. `CLONE_INTENT` accepts only absent or a complete exact clone—never a prefix—and any disproven platform behavior disables that provider. The brief linked clone is the only executable filesystem candidate and uses its own absent/exact/unlinked record/fault matrix. No byte-stream copy is written to transaction staging.

The journal stores the closure digest plus every object purpose/source/image digest/device/inode and image strategy; descriptors remain live for the whole runner/unit. No later PATH lookup occurs. A mutable Darwin source on a non-APFS/cross-volume location without atomic clone support is unavailable with installation guidance; there is no streaming-copy fallback.

### Same-open-object execution

- Linux executes the verified native descriptor with `execveat(fd, "", ..., AT_EMPTY_PATH)` (or the conformance-equivalent `fexecve` implementation), never `/proc/...` or a mutable path.
- Darwin duplicates the verified native descriptor to a reserved non-CLOEXEC number and calls `execve("/dev/fd/<reserved>", ...)`. That pathname is the child process's descriptor namespace, not the original filesystem entry. The adapter is grounded in XNU source commit `f6217f891ac0bb64f3d375211650a4c1ff8ca1ea`, whose exec path uses `/dev/fd/<n>` to avoid reopening an executable object, and is mandatory-tested on both supported Darwin architectures. There is no fallback to the snapshot pathname. If the descriptor adapter fails, external cells report `UNAVAILABLE_PLATFORM_EXEC_IDENTITY` before mutation.

Immediately before exec, the wrapper re-fstats the immutable image descriptor and compares device/inode identity already bound in `CHILD_ARMED`. Same-user rename/unlink/symlink or in-place content changes to original sources cannot alter a sealed memfd, APFS clone, immutable Nix object, or the process-local descriptor mapping.

### Pasture helper and gate identity

The already-running release resolves its own native object, verifies its platform release checksum, installer protocol, and embedded bundle ID, and launches the detached `__install-runner` from that descriptor. The runner retains the same helper descriptor and launches every `__exec-wrapper` from it. Thus the runner and gate implementation are one bound Pasture code object; replacing/upgrading/removing the invocation path cannot substitute either process.

The frontend-to-runner launch uses the same fail-closed token protocol as a harness child. It durably records runner PID/start-token/process-group/helper closure before release and transfers journal/registry-lock authority exactly once. EOF/death before release executes no runner work; after release the durable identity prevents a second runner. Each harness child records both helper and harness closure digests before its one-frame/read-through-EOF release.

If a runner dies, anonymous/unlinked execution images vanish after any armed child exits. Recovery handles only an exact complete pre-unlink APFS clone authorized by `CLONE_INTENT`, then re-resolves the exact recorded source closure and derives a fresh identical image. Exact availability resumes; missing/changed provider state stops as `RECOVERY_PREREQUISITE_REQUIRED`, preserves the committed direction, and tells the user which pinned Pasture/harness package to restore. It never substitutes another executable. Pre-`PREPARED` abort remains clean without a large-file prefix oracle.

## 2. Official-native and Nix-wrapper providers are distinct tuples

# FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-13 — Unified multi-harness installation

Supersedes Proposal 12. Proposals 7–12 remain normative except where replaced here. Round 12 found three executable/provider blockers and seven identity, authority, platform-proof, test, and request-algebra findings. This revision separates semantic closures from live images, adds a non-recursive Nix-native helper provider, removes the unsafe mutable Darwin clone and unsupported `/dev/fd` claim, binds Home Manager to its active fixed activation closure, freezes Linux memfd and helper fault matrices, and makes uninstall semantics explicit.

## 1. Executables are bound execution objects, not staged files

Delete `STAGE_EXECUTABLE`, `STAGE_HELPER`, every filesystem executable-copy candidate, and Proposal 11's Darwin path snapshot. Executable bytes never enter transaction staging, so no 100–400 MB partial executable file exists and R52's prefix oracle remains limited to package/ledger payloads whose canonical bytes are embedded by `EXT_CREATED`.

```go
type BoundExecutableClosure struct {
    Provider       ExecutableProvider // official-native-v1, nix-native-v1, or nix-wrapper-v1
    Harness        HarnessName        // pasture-helper, claude-code, codex
    Version        Semver
    Protocol       uint32             // required for pasture-helper
    BundleID       BundleID           // required for pasture-helper
    Objects        []ExecutableObjectSpec // canonical semantic purpose order
    Environment    []EnvironmentEdit
    CanonicalArgv0 string
    SemanticDigest Digest             // provider/version/object bytes/environment; stable across rebinding
    Live           []LiveImageBinding // process-local incarnation; excluded from SemanticDigest
}

type ExecutableObjectSpec struct {
    Purpose       ObjectPurpose // helper, wrapper-source, interpreter, native-target, runtime-support
    ImagePolicy   ImagePolicy  // immutable-source, linux-sealed-memfd, or darwin-root-immutable-path
    CanonicalPath SafeAbsolutePath // semantic only for immutable-path policies
    SHA256        Digest
    Provenance    ProvenanceID
}

type LiveImageBinding struct {
    Purpose              ObjectPurpose
    SourceFD             uintptr // never serialized
    ImageFD              uintptr // never serialized
    ReservedChildExecFD  int32   // Linux child mapping; -1 on Darwin
    ImageKind            ImageKind
    ExecPath             SafeAbsolutePath // Darwin immutable-path only; empty on Linux
    RequiredSeals        uint64
    SourceDevice         uint64
    SourceInode          uint64
    ImageDevice          uint64
    ImageInode           uint64
    SourceOpenDigest     Digest
    ExecutionImageDigest Digest
}
```

The process resolves each closure with a bounded no-follow walk, opens every required regular source object, validates bytes/provenance, and derives a platform execution binding before computing the semantic closure digest. `SemanticDigest` uses the domain `pasture/executable-closure/v1` and a canonical length-prefixed encoding of only the provider tuple, harness/version/helper protocol and bundle, ordered object purposes/bytes/provenance/image policies/canonical immutable paths, typed environment edits, and argv0. It excludes descriptors and every source/image device/inode. Per object, `SourceOpenDigest` uses domain `pasture/source-open/v1` over semantic object identity plus current source device/inode; `ExecutionImageDigest` uses `pasture/execution-image/v1` over the closure digest, purpose, image kind, image device/inode, required seal mask or immutable exec path, and reserved child descriptor mapping. `LiveImageBinding` is a fresh launch incarnation tied to the semantic digest in `RUNNER_ARMED`, `CHILD_ARMED`, and `CLOSURE_REBOUND`, and its image kind must match the semantic policy.

Root-owned immutable Nix/system objects may be used directly. A mutable Linux source is copied only into an anonymous `memfd` created with `MFD_CLOEXEC|MFD_ALLOW_SEALING|MFD_EXEC`, hash-verified, made executable, sealed with `F_SEAL_WRITE|F_SEAL_FUTURE_WRITE|F_SEAL_GROW|F_SEAL_SHRINK|F_SEAL_SEAL`, and verified with `F_GET_SEALS`; a crash drops the anonymous object and leaves no candidate. The Linux conformance matrix has separate injected faults at source verify, `memfd_create`, every copy/write boundary, image hash, executable-mode change, `F_ADD_SEALS`, `F_GET_SEALS`, descriptor duplication/inheritance, gate release, and `execveat`. It includes unknown/denied `MFD_EXEC`, missing `MFD_ALLOW_SEALING`, seal-policy denial, missing/mismatched seals, no-exec policy, truncated image, inherited-descriptor mismatch, and exec denial on both release architectures. No legacy-flag or unsealed fallback is permitted; failure makes the provider unavailable before persistent mutation.

A mutable Darwin executable source is unsupported: APFS clones have no write seal, and unlinking does not revoke a hostile same-UID writer's open descriptor. `fclonefileat`, `CLONE_INTENT`, and every Darwin clone state are deleted. A Darwin external lifecycle cell is available only when the Pasture helper and every executable/interpreter/runtime object it needs resolve to canonical root-owned, non-group/user-writable paths with non-writable ancestors on an independently immutable Nix/system volume. The semantic object spec includes the canonical executable path, mount/store provenance, content digest, and `darwin-root-immutable-path` policy. A user-owned Claude/Codex/Pasture executable makes only the affected external cell `UNAVAILABLE_MUTABLE_DARWIN_EXECUTABLE` before persistent mutation, with guidance to use an immutable Nix/system package or select file-only cells. No copied, cloned, `/dev/fd`, or mutable-path fallback exists.

The journal stores the canonical semantic object specs/digest separately from every per-attempt source-open and execution-image digest plus their explicit fields; process-local raw descriptors are not replay data, but the reserved child mapping is. Linux descriptors remain live for the whole runner/unit. Repeat/recovery fixtures prove that new memfd or provider-permitted source physical identities retain the semantic digest while changing the appropriate live digests; mutations to every semantic field change the closure digest, and mutations to any armed live field fail the current attempt. No later PATH lookup occurs.

### Platform execution contracts

- Linux executes the verified native descriptor with `execveat(fd, "", ..., AT_EMPTY_PATH)` (or the conformance-equivalent `fexecve` implementation), never `/proc/...` or a mutable path.
- Darwin does not claim Mach-O descriptor execution. The cited XNU `/dev/fd/<n>` branch protects an interpreter script handoff and is not evidence that `execve` loads a Mach-O image from an open fd. The wrapper executes only the canonical `darwin-root-immutable-path` after rewalking it and rechecking path, owner/mode, mount/store provenance, digest, device, and inode against `CHILD_ARMED`. Because every path component and object is outside the same-UID writer's mutation authority, pathname execution introduces no in-scope substitution window. Any mutable component is unavailable; there is no `/dev/fd` or clone fallback.

Immediately before exec, the Linux wrapper rechecks seals and fstats the immutable image descriptor against `CHILD_ARMED`; the Darwin wrapper repeats the full immutable-path proof. Same-user rename/unlink/symlink, retained writable descriptors, and in-place content changes cannot alter a sealed Linux memfd and cannot obtain write access to an accepted Darwin closure. Real Nix/system fixtures on Darwin amd64 and arm64 attempt every same-UID path/content swap and retained-writer case; any environment where the immutability premise cannot be demonstrated reports the cell unavailable rather than claiming support.

### Pasture helper and gate identity

Pasture adds a small, private `pasture-install-helper` binary containing only the detached runner/wrapper protocol; the public frontend is never re-executed as gate code. Official release packaging builds the helper first, hashes it, then builds the frontend with that expected helper digest/protocol/bundle identity and ships both. This is non-recursive: the helper never embeds its own digest, and embedding a separate helper's digest does not affect the helper bytes. Nix builds the helper as its own output and a separate provider-manifest derivation binds it; Home Manager retains that manifest in its activation closure. No third-party Claude/Codex executable is embedded.

The already-running frontend resolves the provider-specific helper, verifies its externally supplied expected identity, and launches `__install-runner` through the platform execution contract. `official-native-v1` uses the helper digest fixed by the two-stage release build; `nix-native-v1` uses the immutable provider manifest produced over the already-built helper output and, under Home Manager, pinned by the generation closure. The runner retains that same semantic helper closure/live binding and launches every `__exec-wrapper` through it. Thus runner and gate implementation are one bound first-party helper object; replacing/upgrading/removing the frontend or helper path cannot substitute either process.

The frontend-to-runner launch uses the same fail-closed token protocol as a harness child. It durably records runner PID/start-token/process-group/helper closure before release and transfers journal/registry-lock authority exactly once. EOF/death before release executes no runner work; after release the durable identity prevents a second runner. Each harness child records both helper and harness closure digests before its one-frame/read-through-EOF release.

If a runner dies, anonymous Linux images vanish after any armed child exits. Recovery re-resolves the recorded semantic closure and derives a fresh live binding; Darwin revalidates the exact immutable path instead of creating an image. A reinstalled exact package may have a new source inode only where its provider provenance permits physical rebinding. Recovery first journals/fsyncs `CLOSURE_REBOUND` with the unchanged semantic digest and new physical identities before any gate release. Exact semantic availability resumes; missing/changed provider state stops as `RECOVERY_PREREQUISITE_REQUIRED`, preserves the committed direction, and tells the user which pinned Pasture/harness package to restore. It never substitutes another executable. Pre-`PREPARED` abort remains clean without a large-file prefix oracle.

Real fixtures cover every supported Pasture-helper provider/platform/policy tuple independently: two-stage-release official helper plus Nix-native helper on Linux amd64/arm64, and a Darwin tuple only after the exact Nix/system immutable-path fixture passes on that architecture. They verify that frontend and helper are distinct bytes/digests and reject a recursive/self-digest or wrong helper artifact. An ordinary user-local Darwin helper is an expected unavailable case, not a supported tuple. Each supported row faults resolve/open/verify, runner arm append/fsync, runner release/EOF/exec, wrapper arm append/fsync, wrapper release/EOF/exec, and authority transfer. Each then removes or replaces the invocation path, helper package, current Pasture installation, and every harness closure object independently. Exact semantic restoration, including a new inode/live image where the provider permits it, resumes only after `CLOSURE_REBOUND`; wrong helper provider/protocol/bundle/object/provenance stays `RECOVERY_PREREQUISITE_REQUIRED`, and no fault starts a second runner or wrapper.

## 2. Executable providers are a closed tuple algebra

Mutating wrapper bytes, target, interpreter, PATH edit, store provenance, or native digest fails before mutation. Unknown/crossed variants, a helper under `nix-wrapper-v1`, a wrapper under `nix-native-v1`, self-asserted digests, and provenance/digest disagreement fail before mutation. Its TUI hides role narrowing, visibly resets a prior narrowed choice when the operation changes only after confirmation/back-navigation, and its adapters reject any non-full subset before discovery. Empty selection is invalid for uninstall. Role-scoped removal is deliberately not represented as cell uninstall. Unknown, duplicate, unsorted, null, omitted, role flags combined with `--roles-none`, spoofed Home Manager, and every invalid kind/field combination fail actionably with zero observation/mutation. Tests cover the default input plus all 32 explicit subsets through companion ensure and Home Manager reconcile, and prove uninstall accepts full roles only.

## 4. Legacy Claude composition includes roles and removal

The legacy composite has `Granularity=indivisible` and effective effects `{claude skills with all roles, claude agents, claude hooks}`. It is `EXTERNALLY_MANAGED` only when the desired Claude row is all three and `Roles` is the full five-role set. Any narrowed role set conflicts because the legacy plugin exposes the complete role-scoped skill inventory.

For `home-manager-reconcile`, an empty desired Claude row with any currently Home-Manager-owned Claude cell still requires discovery. Active legacy state conflicts before modern links are removed because exact absence cannot be achieved; inactive legacy state may reconcile owned modern cells to absent; unknown/declined/stale/unavailable/apply-changed evidence blocks. Empty desired plus no prior Claude owner introduces no discovery.

The independent matrix is exhaustive over all three `IntentKind` values (not a collapsed mode), all 8 desired/selected Claude rows, applicable prior companion and Home Manager ownership rows, all 64 other-harness subsets, all role inputs applicable to that kind, and every legacy evidence state. Companion ensure covers all 32 role subsets; only its full-row/full-role case may classify the legacy composite as `EXTERNALLY_MANAGED`. Companion uninstall proves every non-full subset is rejected before discovery; for full roles, any selected Claude cell conflicts with effective absence while the legacy composite is active, inactive legacy permits removal of only exact companion-owned modern cell membership, and Home-Manager-owned/foreign or unknown/declined/stale/unavailable/apply-changed evidence blocks. It never adopts or removes the legacy plugin. Home Manager covers all 32 role subsets and desired-empty removals. Other-harness action shapes remain invariant except for their own role-granularity conflicts.

## 5. Exact source-publish states and external test oracles

Proposal 11's long external graphs and literal argv remain exact. Add `EXACT_STAGE_AND_DESTINATION`: when a desired persistent source already exists exact after `PREPARED`, the exact staged source and exact destination coexist. `PUBLISH_N` records an existing-exact no-op, leaves the staged copy as a journal-authorized commit-cleanup candidate, and continues. A crash before/after that record accepts only the exact dual state or the already-cleaned one-entry successor at the appropriate cleanup checkpoint. Any digest/member/mode mismatch between stage and destination is tampered. Fixtures distinguish stage-only, destination-only after atomic promotion, exact dual reuse, published-but-unrecorded, partial/prefix, wrong type/digest, symlink, and foreign states.

Claude and Codex lifecycle oracles are separate manually authored YAML files in test-only packages. They freeze every ordered step, canonical argv, P/N source-marketplace-plugin vector, permitted intermediate, observer result, and cleanup authority for install, upgrade, downgrade, and uninstall. Production graph/adapter packages cannot import testdata or the oracle decoder. Mutation tests independently alter each production step kind/order, argument/token, prior/desired vector, observer placement, intermediate classifier, no-op rule, and cleanup target and require a fixture failure. Reverse fixture-parser tests prove duplicate/missing states and shared production constants are rejected. Every `MARKETPLACE_LIST` and `PLUGIN_LIST` remains a separately gated/journaled child; `ASSERT_*` remains pure. The research document uses only these long graphs.

## 6. Acceptance replacements

Proposal 11 acceptance remains except that executable snapshots are replaced by bound closures. Add:

1. Linux `execveat` executes sealed helper/harness descriptors under final path/inode/content swaps. Darwin makes no Mach-O `/dev/fd` claim and permits external CLI cells only for fully root-owned immutable Nix/system path closures; mutable Darwin executables fail before mutation with no copy/clone/path fallback.
2. Linux mutable images use the exact executable-memfd flags/seal mask and full syscall/policy fault matrix on both release architectures. No unauthenticated partial executable is ever deleted; recovery either rebinds the exact semantic closure to a fresh live identity or stops with the exact restore prerequisite.
3. Detached runner and every wrapper share the journaled Pasture helper closure identity; Pasture self-upgrade/removal cannot substitute gate code.
4. The two-stage official release and separate Nix helper/provider-manifest derivations prove a distinct first-party install-helper identity with no self-hash cycle. Official-native, Nix-native helper, and Nix-wrapper fixtures remain separate; real Nix Codex behavior is preserved without comparing its patched native bytes to official archive bytes.
5. Only companion kinds decode publicly. Home Manager reconciliation is derived solely from the independently verified active fixed activation closure; arbitrary/stale/copied Nix-store inputs fail before discovery. Role arrays are required/sorted/unique, omitted defaults are materialized by adapters, and explicit empty means core-only.
6. Legacy Claude is externally managed only for full row plus full roles; the full kind/desired/prior/other/applicable-role/evidence matrix covers exact-empty reconciliation and whole-cell companion uninstall.
7. Exact source dual-reuse state survives every publish/cleanup crash point.
8. Separate test-only Claude/Codex YAML oracles and production mutation tests detect every lifecycle graph/argv/vector drift.

## Plan UAT decisions

All inherited Plan UAT decisions remain. Acceptance additionally confirms that external recovery depends on restoring the exact recorded Pasture/helper/harness closure if it disappears after a crash; Pasture packages its own small first-party install helper but does not embed hundreds of megabytes of third-party executables. The supported Nix Codex wrapper is modeled as a pinned closure and executed through its native target with equivalent environment edits. Linux external CLI cells require executable-memfd/sealing kernel policy; unsupported kernels leave those cells unavailable rather than use weaker flags. Darwin external CLI cells require root-owned immutable Nix/system helper and harness paths; ordinary mutable user-local Pasture/Claude/Codex executables leave those cells unavailable, while file-only skill/agent/OpenCode-plugin cells remain usable. Home Manager exact-reconcile authority comes only from the fixed active generation closure, never an arbitrary store file. Phase 8 may promote the already locked `golang.org/x/sys v0.44.0` from indirect to direct use for Linux `memfd`/descriptor-exec primitives, subject to the same recorded dependency approval as the Charm and test-only Node additions.

# FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-14 — Persistent multi-harness delivery, structurally reset

## 0. Reset contract

This proposal supersedes Proposals 7–13 in full. It does not inherit a prior
proposal, recovery graph, provider matrix, or acceptance section. Reviewers need
only canonical `FOLLOWUP_URD-2` (`aura-plugins-iyd7j`), this proposal, the linked
research evidence, and the current repositories.

Proposal 7 reached a clean three-reviewer consensus for one dedicated Codex agent
subtree. Plan UAT then expanded the product to three harnesses by three components.
Proposals 8–13 retained the old transaction assumptions and repeatedly added
mechanisms for every new mismatch. The result mixed five concerns:

1. protocol/code generation;
2. desired user configuration;
3. generated package composition;
4. direct-file ownership and convergence;
5. third-party plugin activation.

This proposal separates them. It deletes the detached runner, authenticated
gate, helper/executable-closure providers, memfd/APFS execution schemes,
active-generation capability, per-cell concurrent authority transfer, legacy
equivalence matrices, and automatic recovery of ambiguous third-party commands.
None is required by the canonical URD.

## 1. Product boundary

Pasture remains the semantic/codegen source of truth. Aura remains Home Manager,
marketplace, and operational integration. The shipped user surfaces are:

- generated Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex skills, agents, and lifecycle hooks;
- a truthful Codex `pasture` skills plugin, a separate opt-in Codex
  `pasture-hooks` plugin, and standalone Codex agent TOMLs;
- `pasture install` (`pasture kickstart` alias) for persistent interactive or
  noninteractive selection;
- Aura Home Manager options over the same harness/component catalog;
- one desired YAML document and a separate applied-state root.

The first release assumes a cooperative same-user environment. It protects
against accidents, stale plans, crashes in Pasture-owned direct writes, foreign
content, and unsupported harness state. It does not claim to defend against a
malicious process running as the same user while installation is in progress.

No path changes Git hooks, `core.hooksPath`, Beads hooks, or a harness's private
plugin cache. “Hooks” means harness lifecycle hooks only.

## 2. One support table

`skills`, `agents`, and `hooks` are the only user-selectable components. A plugin
is a delivery package, not a component. Every cell is present in capabilities and
in the TUI even when unavailable.

| Harness | Skills | Agents | Lifecycle hooks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `direct-tree`: generated whole skill directories under `~/.claude/skills/` | `direct-file`: generated Markdown agents under `~/.claude/agents/` | `external-plugin`: generated `pasture-hooks` installed through the supported Claude plugin CLI |
| OpenCode | `direct-tree`: generated whole skill directories under `~/.config/opencode/skills/` | `direct-file`: generated Markdown agents under `~/.config/opencode/agent/` | `direct-tree`: generated target-native plugin under `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` |
| Codex | `external-plugin`: generated `pasture` skills plugin through the supported Codex plugin CLI | `direct-file`: five generated TOMLs under `~/.codex/agents/` | `external-plugin`: separately generated `pasture-hooks` plugin through the supported Codex plugin CLI |

Rules:

- Whole skill directories are delivery members. `SKILL.md`, `agents/openai.yaml`,
  references, scripts, figures, and assets are not reconstructed or dropped.
- Codex plugin installation registers skills only. The plugin may carry the
  canonical TOML bundle and an explicit setup skill, but agent registration is a
  separate direct-file cell.
- Selecting skills without hooks executes no hook activation.
- The existing monolithic Claude Pasture plugin is legacy. If active, mutations
  for the Claude row stop with removal/upgrade guidance; the installer never
  adopts, edits, or removes it implicitly.
- A cell is supported only when its cataloged platform and harness-version probe
  pass. The initial external-plugin conformance catalog is Linux-only. Direct
  file cells remain available on other supported filesystems; unproven external
  rows are visibly `UNAVAILABLE_UNTESTED_PLATFORM`.

## 3. Surface-to-data-model mapping

### 3.1 Existing semantic owners

| Surface | Existing source | Projection |
|---|---|---|
| role behavior | `RoleSpec` and generated role bodies | Claude/OpenCode Markdown agents; Codex TOML `developer_instructions`; role skills |
| command skills | `CommandSpec`, workflows, procedures, constraints | harness-native skill trees |
| lifecycle intent | current canonical hook behavior | Claude hook plugin, OpenCode plugin, Codex hook plugin |
| target routing | `HarnessName`, `TargetHarness`, `EmitHarness` | add `HarnessCodex`; retain one generator entrypoint |
| release version | canonical Pasture release metadata | manifests, bundle, marketplace pin checks |

No installation boolean, destination, plugin rule, or Codex policy is added to
`RoleSpec` or `CommandSpec`.

### 3.2 Small new generated-delivery model

```go
type ComponentName string // skills | agents | hooks
type DeliveryStrategy string // direct-tree | direct-file | external-plugin

type ArtifactSpec struct {
    ID             ArtifactID
    Harness        HarnessName
    Component      ComponentName
    LogicalID      string
    SourcePath     SafeRelativePath
    PackagePath    SafeRelativePath
    Mode           fs.FileMode
}

type ResolvedArtifact struct {
    Spec   ArtifactSpec
    SHA256 Digest
    Bytes  []byte
}

type DeliveryUnit struct {
    Cell               CellID // harness + component
    Strategy           DeliveryStrategy
    Artifacts          []ArtifactID
    DestinationRoot    DestinationTemplate
    PackageID          PackageID
    Projection         ProjectionKind // complete | member-prunable
    SupportedPlatforms []Platform
    Prerequisites      []Prerequisite
    Postconditions     []ObservationSpec
}

type DeliveryCatalog struct {
    Schema    string // pasture.delivery/v1
    Version   Semver
    Units     []DeliveryUnit
    Artifacts []ResolvedArtifact
}
```

The generator first renders semantic content, then resolves package membership,
placement, modes, and hashes. It emits a deterministic machine-readable catalog
and embeds the same catalog plus payload bytes in the released `pasture` binary.
Home Manager reads the checked-in catalog from the pinned Pasture input. The CLI
uses its embedded catalog. A test proves both represent the same release digest.

`SkillDescriptor` becomes the one sorted skill inventory. It maps canonical role,
command, and support identities to target outputs. A typed `RuntimeText`/
`RuntimeDialect` seam owns runtime-sensitive invocation, agent dispatch,
follow-up, waiting, messaging, user input, and instruction-source operations.
Generated-text guards scan every active Markdown/XML/YAML/JSON/TOML output; they
do not excuse whole support directories.

### 3.3 Codex plugin and agent projection

Pasture emits:

```text
plugins/pasture/
  .codex-plugin/plugin.json
  skills/<skill>/SKILL.md
  skills/<skill>/agents/openai.yaml
  assets/agent-bundle/manifest.json
  assets/agent-bundle/pasture_*.toml

plugins/pasture-hooks/
  .codex-plugin/plugin.json
  hooks/hooks.json
  <hook support assets>
```

`plugin.json` contains only supported plugin surfaces. It never invents an
`agents` component. Skill frontmatter and `agents/openai.yaml` are produced from
typed metadata validated against `$skill-creator`; plugin manifests and Aura's
aggregate marketplace shape are validated against `$plugin-creator` plus the
current Codex CLI. Public native agent names are `pasture_epoch`,
`pasture_architect`, `pasture_supervisor`, `pasture_worker`, and
`pasture_reviewer`; optional model/reasoning/sandbox/MCP policy is omitted so the
live session policy applies.

## 4. Persistent desired configuration

### 4.1 Canonical schema

The normal fallback is `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/pasture/config.yaml`.
An explicit `--config` path wins everywhere, including the TUI save path.

```yaml
version: 1

audit_trail: sqlite
audit_db_path: ""

provenance:
  db_path: ""

install:
  targets:
    claude-code:
      components: [skills, agents]
    opencode:
      components: [skills, agents]
    codex:
      components: []
```

`install.targets` is the desired complete matrix for the companion authority.
Components are normalized to catalog order, unique, and known. Hooks are absent
by default. The companion's initial no-file default is an empty matrix; the first
wizard may display recommendations but writes nothing until confirmation.

The root config is one typed document:

```go
type Config struct {
    Version    uint32           `yaml:"version"`
    AuditTrail AuditTrailBackend `yaml:"audit_trail"`
    AuditDBPath string          `yaml:"audit_db_path"`
    Provenance ProvenanceConfig `yaml:"provenance"`
    Install    InstallConfig    `yaml:"install"`
}

type InstallConfig struct {
    Targets map[HarnessName]TargetSelection `yaml:"targets"`
}

type TargetSelection struct {
    Components []ComponentName `yaml:"components"`
}
```

The current `PasturedConfig` resolver becomes a compatibility view over the same
root audit fields; its CLI > environment > YAML > default precedence remains.
This deliberately avoids renaming the already supported YAML keys. The unwired
provenance path becomes a real nested view. An unversioned legacy document is
accepted when it contains only known legacy audit/provenance keys; it is mapped
in memory and the first confirmed write adds `version: 1` plus the install
section. Unknown keys and a versioned/unversioned hybrid fail with the exact keys
and migration command.

### 4.2 Load/update/publication contract

- YAML decoding uses strict known fields and an explicit schema version.
- Missing config returns defaults without writing.
- The TUI loads the complete typed document and replaces only `Install`; daemon
  and provenance values remain semantically intact.
- Canonical rewrites are documented; comments are not semantic configuration.
- The writer respects the resolved `--config` path, uses a mode-0700 parent and
  mode-0600 file, rejects a symlink/non-regular target, takes a companion config
  lock, writes and fsyncs a same-directory temporary file, renames atomically,
  and fsyncs the directory.
- Validation runs before publication. Save failure prevents apply. After the user
  confirms, desired config is saved before reconciliation; if application later
  fails, the desired choice remains and `status` reports drift.
- No installed digest, owner, PID, journal, observation, or recovery decision is
  serialized in YAML.

This deliberately keeps the useful Peasant boundary—versioned desired YAML and
a TUI over typed answers—while rejecting its current direct-write, ignored-save,
default-path, and rebuild-from-defaults failure modes.

## 5. Applied ownership and observations

Companion mutable state lives under
`${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/pasture/install/`:

```text
install/
  companion/
    lock
    ledger.json
    pending.json          # at most one serialized mutation under the lock
    external/<cell>.json  # unresolved external-command evidence
  home-manager/
    external-ledger.json  # external plugin cells only; never direct links
    external/<cell>.json  # unresolved HM adapter evidence
```

The companion `ledger.json` records only committed companion ownership:
catalog/bundle digest,
cell, destination, artifact membership, expected hashes/modes, and committed
external plugin identity. A matching filename or byte sequence without a ledger
entry is foreign and is not adopted. Desired config never grants delete authority.

Home Manager direct links never enter either ledger. Its small external ledger
exists only because Claude/Codex plugin registries are outside Home Manager's
link farm; it records exact plugin identities successfully applied from an
immutable generation intent. A generation change or disable reconciles that
external ledger from Nix intent. Neither ledger is treated as desired state.

Observed harness versions, plugin lists, destination hashes, and TUI capability
states are recomputed. They are not copied into YAML. A pending/external record
is recovery evidence, not desired state.

## 6. One declarative planner

```go
type DesiredSelection map[HarnessName]ComponentSet

type InstallRequestV1 struct {
    Schema  string // pasture.install-request/v1
    Desired DesiredSelection
}

type InstallPlan struct {
    Schema       string
    ConfigBefore Digest
    Desired      DesiredSelection
    Catalog      Digest
    Observed     ObservationDigest
    Actions      []InstallAction
    Digest       Digest
}
```

There is no public `authority × mode × operation` algebra. The companion always
converges its committed ownership to the saved desired matrix:

- a selected unowned cell is installed if conflict-free;
- a selected owned cell is updated or no-op;
- an unselected previously companion-owned cell is removed;
- an unselected cell never owned by companion is untouched;
- an empty matrix removes all exact companion-owned cells and otherwise no-ops.

`uninstall` is an adapter that removes cells from the proposed desired matrix; it
is not a second executor state machine. Upgrade is a catalog change observed by
the same planner. Downgrade is rejected in v1 with release-specific guidance.

Plan actions are deterministically ordered by harness, component, destination,
and logical ID. The plan digest binds the proposed config, catalog bytes,
ownership ledger, pending state, relevant destination identities, exact external
observations, and consent flags. After confirmation, apply acquires the config
lock and companion state lock in that fixed order, re-observes, and rejects a
stale digest before changing either plane. It then atomically changes config from
the exact recorded `ConfigBefore` to `Desired`; the saved desired document is the
expected first transition of the plan, not a stale-plan event. Destination
mutation starts only after that save and while both locks remain held. A crash
after the save simply leaves declared drift for the next run to re-plan.

## 7. TUI and CLI contract

The Cobra command owns paths, catalog loading, configuration, discovery,
planning, saving, and an injected applier. Bubble Tea owns only presentation and
in-memory answers. It receives typed capability/observation DTOs and sends a
normalized desired matrix back.

Flow:

```text
load config → discover capabilities → matrix → hook consent/details
→ exact diff summary → confirm → atomic config save → reconcile → result
```

The matrix shows `available`, `selected`, `installed`, `drifted`, `disabled`,
`conflict`, `externally-managed`, and `recovery-required` with reasons. Back and
terminal resize preserve choices; cancelling apply cancels only work that has not
crossed an external command boundary.

Public commands:

```text
pasture install                         # TTY wizard
pasture kickstart                       # alias
pasture install capabilities [--json]
pasture install plan [selectors] [--json]
pasture install apply [selectors] --yes [--json]
pasture install status [--json]
pasture install recover <cell> <accept-observed|retry|forget-aborted> --yes
pasture install uninstall [selectors|--all] --yes
```

Repeated `--select harness:component` supplies the complete proposed matrix for
`plan/apply`; `--request FILE` supplies `InstallRequestV1`. Explicit selectors or
request files never launch the TUI. No selectors in a non-TTY fails with the
missing decision and exact flags. TUI, selector, and JSON fixtures that express
the same desired matrix produce the same normalized plan.

Selecting a previously disabled hook cell requires an explicit hook checkbox in
the TUI and final confirmation. Noninteractive enablement additionally requires
`--allow-hooks`. An unchanged saved hook selection may be reconciled without
re-consent; the persisted component selection is the standing desired intent.

Observers never create locks/directories, rewrite config, invoke plugin-changing
commands, or repair. The ordinary interactive command saves only after plan
confirmation. It never renders success if save or apply fails.

## 8. Direct-file reconciler

Direct destinations are either one regular file or one dedicated generated tree
(for example, one skill directory). They are not arbitrary shared-directory
snapshots.

Under the global companion lock, each action follows one small transaction:

1. validate ledger ownership and current destination identity;
2. write and fsync `pending.json` in `PREPARING`, recording prior/desired
   identities and unique sibling stage/backup paths before either candidate is
   created;
3. stage and fsync the complete desired file/tree, verify it, then fsync a
   `PREPARED` record; no destination has changed before this commit point;
4. for a replacement tree, rename the prior tree to the recorded backup and the
   exact stage to the destination, fsyncing the parent after each rename; for a
   file, use the equivalent recorded atomic replacement;
5. atomically publish the new ledger and fsync the state directory;
6. remove only the recorded stage/backup candidates and then clear
   `pending.json`.

For uninstall, the current destination must match the ledger. The journal records
the exact removal before unlink/rename; after removal it commits the ledger and
cleans only recorded candidates. Parent directories are removed only when the
ledger says Pasture created them and they are empty.

Recovery recognizes only exact prior, exact desired, or exact committed shapes:

- `PREPARING` + prior destination/ledger: remove only the recorded partial stage
  and abort; destination content has not changed;
- `PREPARED` + prior destination/ledger + exact stage: roll forward;
- recorded backup + exact stage + absent destination: publish desired and roll
  forward;
- recorded backup + desired destination + prior ledger: finish the recorded
  ledger commit;
- desired destination + desired ledger: finish recorded cleanup;
- recorded uninstall destination absent + prior ledger: finish removal commit;
- anything else: preserve all evidence and return `MANUAL_RECOVERY_REQUIRED`.

`PREPARED` is the per-action roll-forward point. It is written only after the
stage is complete and verified, so recovery never needs an old binary, source
checkout, or unrecorded payload oracle to finish a committed action. Missing or
changed post-PREPARED stage/backup content is manual, never guessed or deleted.

There is no whole-matrix atomicity claim. A crash can leave earlier units
committed and one unit pending; subsequent status names each state. New harness
processes are expected to start after a healthy reconciliation, not during it.

The reconciler refuses unowned collisions even when bytes happen to match,
modified owned content, symlinks, unexpected hard links, path traversal,
wrong-owner or unsafe parent paths, malformed bundle members, and hash/mode
mismatch. Errors include operation, cell, path, observed/expected state, impact,
and exact remediation.

## 9. External plugin adapters

Claude hooks and Codex skills/hooks use narrow synchronous adapters over the
official harness CLIs. Each adapter has a manually authored, test-only contract
fixture with:

- supported CLI version range and capability probe;
- exact marketplace/plugin identity;
- exact ordered argv for observe, add/update, and remove;
- accepted exit classes;
- before/after observations and postconditions;
- whether retry from a known prior state is documented idempotent.

The planner resolves the executable and version. Apply re-resolves and requires
the same semantic identity immediately before spawn. The same-user executable and
harness are trusted; there is no copied executable, detached runner, token gate,
helper, memfd, or path-authentication scheme. Stdout/stderr and exit status are
captured with size limits and secrets redacted.

Before spawn, Pasture fsyncs `external/<cell>.json` containing the exact prior
observation, desired identity, argv, catalog digest, and plan digest. On a known
exit plus exact postcondition it commits the ledger and removes the record. If
the Pasture process dies or the harness result cannot be proven, the cell becomes
`AMBIGUOUS_EXTERNAL_RESULT`:

- status re-observes and displays exact prior/desired/other classification;
- no automatic retry, uninstall, adoption, or ledger commit occurs;
- `recover ... accept-observed` is allowed only when exact desired state is
  observed;
- `recover ... retry` requires explicit confirmation and an adapter contract that
  permits retry from the exact observed state;
- any other state remains manual with the exact supported harness commands.

This is honest convergence around a third-party registry, not a claim of global
crash atomicity or survival independent of the installed harness CLI.

## 10. Home Manager architecture

### 10.1 Shared intent, separate mutation engines

Aura adds:

```nix
CUSTOM.programs.aura-config-sync.targets = {
  "claude-code".components = [ "skills" "agents" ];
  opencode.components = [ "skills" "agents" ];
  codex.components = [ ];
};
```

Each component list is unique and typed. Existing Claude/OpenCode skills+agents
defaults remain; Codex and hooks default disabled. Existing `commands.enable`,
`agents.enable`, `opencode.skills.enable`, and `opencode.agents.enable` remain
compatibility inputs with deterministic translation, deprecation warnings, and
an actionable conflict when old and new declarations disagree. Existing role
filtering remains a Home Manager compatibility projection; per-role selection is
not added to the companion v1 matrix.

Home Manager reads the Pasture-generated delivery catalog and sources whole
generated directories/files. Direct cells remain ordinary `home.file` links and
Home Manager owns their rollback/removal. They are **not migrated into the
companion's locked reconciler**. The shared contract is catalog and selection
semantics, not one universal mutation mechanism.

External plugin cells generate one immutable, no-user-argument intent per Home
Manager generation. A pre-link activation step performs zero-write validation;
an after-link step invokes a narrow `pasture install hm-activate <immutable-intent>`
adapter for only external cells. Dry-run/test mode validates and previews but does
not mutate. The adapter uses the same catalog, external argv fixtures, observers,
and ambiguous-result rules as the companion, while Home Manager remains the
declared authority. It never accepts an arbitrary public authority field or edits
a private cache. A symlinked/read-only/independently managed Claude/Codex settings
file that the official CLI must mutate is a visible preflight conflict.

The module emits the cleanup activation path even when its target matrix becomes
empty. Disable/rollback removes direct links through Home Manager and reconciles
the prior `home-manager/external-ledger.json` to absence before clearing adapter
state. Thus disabling the module cannot strand a plugin merely because the new
generation no longer selects its activation unit.

### 10.2 First-release authority boundary

The proposed MVP has one active manager per user profile:

- a Home Manager generation with any target writes an immutable authority marker
  and refuses nonempty companion ownership/pending state;
- companion apply refuses while that active marker exists or any target is a Nix
  symlink;
- switching to Home Manager requires companion desired state empty and a healthy
  zero-owned ledger;
- switching to companion requires disabling/activating the Home Manager module so
  its links, external plugins, and marker are removed;
- neither path adopts the other's artifacts.

This removes cross-authority leases and concurrent transfer. Mixed ownership by
harness/cell is a proposed Plan-UAT DEFER, not a hidden promise.

## 11. Release, marketplace, and artifact availability

- Adopt `aura-plugins-oj7we` generation roots: sources are read below
  `SourceRoot`; outputs are written below `OutputRoot`.
- `make generate` emits all three targets, catalogs, plugins, agent bundles, and
  hook packages deterministically; the existing dirty-tree gate covers them.
- The released Go binary embeds the deterministic delivery archive and catalog.
  Repo development and release-installed CLI plans use the same digest.
- Pasture release metadata supplies one base semver to the plugin manifests and
  bundle. Development cachebusters are local-only.
- Aura owns `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`; its Pasture entries use immutable
  `git-subdir` pins and are not made available until matching Pasture content is
  published. Aura's Claude marketplace remains separate and current-compatible.
- The implementation records the exact tested Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex
  versions and package checksums in conformance fixtures. Unsupported versions
  fail capabilities before mutation with upgrade/downgrade guidance.

## 12. Independent validation strategy

Production catalogs never serve as their own oracle. Hand-authored fixtures pin:

1. nine capability cells, strategies, destinations, and platform availability;
2. Claude/Codex external marketplace/plugin argv and postconditions;
3. expected canonical skill/role/hook inventory;
4. legacy flat-config migration examples;
5. Home Manager legacy-option translations and default matrix.

Required suites:

- config: strict parsing, explicit version, missing-file defaults, flat migration,
  semantic preservation, exact `--config` write target, symlink refusal,
  permissions, short write/fsync/rename faults, save-before-apply behavior;
- planner: all nine individual cells, representative sparse/full/empty matrices,
  prior owned/unowned/drifted states, deterministic ordering/digest, stale plan,
  TUI/flags/JSON parity, hook consent;
- TUI: page flow, saved preselection, disabled reasons, back/restart/resize/cancel,
  summary, save/apply error presentation, injected applier;
- direct reconciliation: file/tree create/update/no-op/remove, foreign identical
  content, modified owned content, link/path attacks, every pending recovery shape,
  partial multi-cell convergence, mtime stability;
- adapters: exact argv/order, version/capability probe, exit/postcondition mismatch,
  kill/ambiguous classification, explicit recovery actions, mutation tests against
  every fixture field;
- codegen: catalog bijection, target routing, deterministic payloads, whole skill
  directories, skill/plugin creator validation, runtime-dialect coverage and
  leakage guards, five agent formats, hook separation;
- harness smoke: isolated current Claude/OpenCode/Codex homes prove selected
  components present and unselected components absent; Codex plugin-only versus
  native-agent loading remains distinct;
- Home Manager: option eval/default/compatibility conflicts, whole-directory
  links, authority conflicts, enable/update/disable/rollback, external dry-run and
  ambiguous result, Linux system assertion;
- release: embedded/repo catalog equality, generate twice, version parity,
  immutable marketplace pins, source/output isolation;
- repository gates: Pasture Go format/lint/race/build/generate and Aura Nix
  `flake check --no-build`, `aura-swarm` build, and help smoke.

Tests exercise meaningful boundaries, not exhaustive products of unsettled
dimensions. A new state or mechanism requires a requirement-to-test trace before
addition.

## 13. Requirement traceability

| Requirement | Mechanism | Independent evidence |
|---|---|---|
| UR1 canonical generation | SkillDescriptor + RuntimeDialect + TargetHarness | inventory fixture, target goldens, leakage scan |
| UR2 truthful Codex | separate skills/hooks plugins + standalone TOMLs | creator validation and isolated Codex smoke |
| UR3 surface mapping | artifact/package/unit catalog | hand-authored nine-cell fixture and bijection tests |
| UR4 persistent choices | unified versioned Config + atomic install-section update | migration/path/fault tests and rerun preselection |
| UR5 TUI/machine parity | pure desired model and planner, injected TUI services | TUI/flags/JSON golden plans |
| UR6 safe convergence | ledger + one pending direct transaction + explicit external evidence | ownership, fault, and ambiguity tests |
| UR7 Home Manager | catalog-driven whole links + external-only activation adapter | Nix eval/activation/rollback fixtures |
| UR8 distribution | embedded deterministic archive + immutable marketplace pins | release/archive/pin tests |
| UR9 quality | independent fixtures and clean three-axis reviews | recorded votes and gate logs |

## 14. Implementation boundaries and integration points

The supervisor will create vertical slices after ratification. The architectural
boundaries are:

1. **Generation/catalog slice** — `GenerationRoots`, SkillDescriptor,
   RuntimeDialect, Codex target, three hook projections, deterministic catalog and
   archive.
2. **Configuration/planner slice** — unified config load/migration/atomic writer,
   desired normalization, discovery DTOs, immutable planner, Cobra/JSON surfaces.
3. **Companion application slice** — TUI, ledger/pending direct reconciler,
   synchronous external adapters and explicit recovery.
4. **Home Manager/distribution slice** — catalog-driven whole links, target
   options/compatibility, external activation intent, marketplaces and pins.
5. **Conformance/landing slice** — independent fixtures, real harness smoke,
   release drift/versioning, documentation, two-repository validation.

Horizontal integration points:

| Contract | Owner | Consumers | Merge timing |
|---|---|---|---|
| SkillDescriptor/RuntimeDialect | generation | every target emitter and leakage test | first |
| DeliveryCatalog schema | generation | planner, embedded bundle, Home Manager, release tests | before planner/HM merge |
| Config/DesiredSelection | configuration | TUI, flags, JSON, planner | before application |
| InstallPlan/action schema | planner | TUI preview, direct and external appliers | before application |
| Ledger/pending schema | application | status/recover and authority checks | before HM authority fixture |
| external adapter fixture | application | companion and HM activation | before live harness smoke |
| immutable Pasture revision | Pasture delivery | Aura marketplace/flake input | before Aura landing |

No Aura slice may introduce protocol semantics or Python protocol-engine code.

## 15. BDD acceptance

1. **Given** canonical Pasture semantics, **when** generation runs for all targets
   twice, **then** it emits deterministic native artifacts and a clean second
   run, **and should not** leave a Claude-only operation in active Codex/OpenCode
   output.
2. **Given** the generated Codex `pasture` plugin, **when** installed from Aura's
   immutable marketplace, **then** all expected namespaced skills load while no
   native agent is registered, **and should not** declare an unsupported agent
   plugin component.
3. **Given** the Codex agents cell selected, **when** companion or Home Manager
   applies it, **then** the five namespaced TOMLs load independently of the
   plugin cache, **and should not** shadow a built-in role or require a source
   checkout.
4. **Given** a user confirms a TUI matrix, **when** config saves and reconciliation
   succeeds or fails, **then** the next run preselects that desired matrix and
   status accurately reports applied drift, **and should not** put ledger or
   journal data in config.
5. **Given** an explicit config path and existing daemon/provenance values,
   **when** install selection changes, **then** that exact file is atomically
   updated with those values preserved, **and should not** write the default path
   or claim success after a save error.
6. **Given** equivalent TUI, flags, and JSON desired selections, **when** planned
   against the same snapshot, **then** they produce the same normalized actions
   and digest, **and should not** launch a TUI for explicit/non-TTY input.
7. **Given** skills and/or agents selected without hooks, **when** applied through
   any frontend, **then** no lifecycle hook or Git hook changes, **and should not**
   treat general confirmation as new noninteractive hook consent.
8. **Given** a foreign, linked, or modified destination, **when** any direct action
   plans/applies/uninstalls, **then** it preserves the content and gives exact
   remediation, **and should not** infer ownership from name or identical bytes.
9. **Given** a crash at any direct publish/ledger boundary, **when** status/recover
   runs, **then** it recognizes an exact recorded shape or preserves evidence as
   manual recovery, **and should not** report a partial matrix as atomically
   rolled back.
10. **Given** a killed or indeterminate external plugin command, **when** Pasture
    restarts, **then** it re-observes and requires an explicit safe disposition,
    **and should not** retry, adopt, or uninstall automatically.
11. **Given** Home Manager's default matrix, **when** evaluated and activated,
    **then** Claude/OpenCode whole skills+agents remain installed, Codex/hooks
    remain disabled, and direct cells remain Home Manager links, **and should not**
    route them through the companion reconciler.
12. **Given** one authority has active ownership, **when** the other attempts to
    apply, **then** it stops before mutation with the exact switch procedure,
    **and should not** establish concurrent leases or partial adoption.
13. **Given** a generated release and Aura marketplace, **when** validation runs,
    **then** embedded bytes, catalog, versions, source pins, and actual harness
    observations agree, **and should not** make an untested external platform
    row available.
14. **Given** any architecture or implementation review finding, **when** the
    review budget continues, **then** the finding is fixed and a fix-free 0/0/0
    round is required, **and should not** close a wave on a fix-applying round.
15. **Given** all gates and user UAT pass, **when** landing runs, **then** Pasture
    and Aura branches are pushed and evidence-backed PRs are open, **and should
    not** land from the dirty original Pasture checkout.

## 16. Proposed Plan-UAT dispositions

These are proposals, not confirmed deferrals:

| Item | Proposed disposition | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| mixed companion/Home Manager ownership | DEFER | one profile authority removes races, leases, and transfer state; both frontends still cover all cells |
| Darwin external plugin activation | DEFER until a real fixture exists | do not claim an untested platform; direct-file cells remain usable |
| companion per-role selection | DEFER | the requested product unit is component; full components remove plugin projection ambiguity |
| automatic recovery/retry of ambiguous third-party commands | DEFER | explicit observation/disposition is safer and much smaller |
| legacy plugin adoption/removal | DEFER | preserve foreign state and provide removal guidance |
| automatic authority transfer | DEFER | explicit uninstall/disable/activate procedure is auditable |
| project-local agent export | DEFER | original elicitation left it outside MVP |
| same-UID hostile-process defense and executable snapshotting | OUT OF SCOPE | not a user requirement or a realistic boundary for this installer |
| role-pruned Codex plugin | DEFER | current plugin unit is indivisible; direct agents remain truthful |

Every DEFER requires explicit user confirmation at Plan UAT. A rejected deferral
returns to a revised proposal; it is not silently routed to a follow-up epic.

# Handoff: Architect → Supervisor

## Request

Continue the deferred work to generate and install Pasture skills, agents, and harness lifecycle hooks for Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex, including a kickstart-style installer and Home Manager parity.

## Ratified plan

Implement FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-20 (`aura-plugins-67w2y`) exactly against the canonical requirements in FOLLOWUP_URD-3 (`aura-plugins-hznvh`). The proposal passed clean correctness, test-quality, and elegance reviews and the user accepted it in `aura-plugins-svtb8`.

Preserve the dirty primary checkout and unrelated user changes.

1. Pasture Go remains the semantic source of truth.
2. Generate independent skills, agents, and hooks packages for every harness cell.
3. Codex skills and hooks are native plugins; Codex agents are standalone user TOML files.
4. Claude uses three split native plugins.
5. OpenCode skills and agents use exact standalone discovery paths; hooks use `@dayvidpham/pasture-opencode-hooks`.
6. Installer config contains preferences only with harness defaults false, skills/agents true, hooks false.
7. Disabled cells actively uninstall; apply is deterministic and fail-fast without rollback or persistent intermediate state.
8. Home Manager uses ordinary nested booleans and delegates plugin-backed cells to stateless `pasture install apply-cell`.
9. Hook opt-in never authorizes Git hooks, Beads hooks, or `core.hooksPath`.
10. Split `EmitHarness` source and output roots so clean staging needs no test source seeding.
11. Codex skills include validated `agents/openai.yaml`; Codex plugins include `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` and rely on default `hooks/hooks.json` discovery for hook packages.

## Deferred item

Project-local Codex agent export under repository `.codex/agents/` is the sole user-confirmed DEFER item. Do not implement it in this wave.

The user chose Deep implementation effort and requested adversarial reviews until a fix-free clean 0 BLOCKER / 0 IMPORTANT / 0 MINOR wave. Treat the review budget as unlimited.

## Integration boundaries

- The private nine-row extension table owns stable build/install facts shared by generation and adapters.
- Codegen owns generated package roots and embedded standalone assets.
- Installer adapters consume those facts but do not enter the protocol model.
- Aura Home Manager reads generated trees from the pinned Pasture input and calls the same stateless adapter entry point for plugin cells.
- Native managers retain ownership of plugin state and updates.

## Acceptance criteria

Use the 16 BDD acceptance criteria in Proposal 20. In particular: validate each of nine cells in isolation; preserve unrelated YAML and OpenCode JSON/JSONC; verify exact Claude legacy-scope behavior; prove source-free release installs; run target-native manifest/loader checks; run all Pasture and Aura gates; and finish with three independent clean reviewers before implementation UAT and landing.

# FOLLOWUP_IMPL_PLAN — Multi-harness Pasture extension delivery

Status: Ratified implementation plan.

Implementation effort: Deep.

Review effort: unlimited review → fix → re-review rounds until a fix-free clean round reports 0 BLOCKER / 0 IMPORTANT / 0 MINOR.

Worktree boundary:

- Aura: `/home/minttea/codebases/dayvidpham/aura-plugins/worktree/codex-codegen`
- Pasture: `/home/minttea/codebases/dayvidpham/aura-plugins/worktree/codex-codegen/pasture`

## Exploration evidence

Three ephemeral read-only explorers mapped:

- Pasture codegen (`internal/codegen`, `tools/codegen`, generated roots and hook assets);
- Pasture CLI/config plus Peasant's kickstart TUI patterns; and
- Aura Home Manager, marketplaces, flake pins, and validation gates.

No explorer modified files or Beads. The supervisor/root agent performs all implementation work.

## Layer integration points

| Contract | Owning slice | Consumers | Shared contract | Merge timing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| explicit source/output generation | Slice 1 | all later slices | `EmitHarness(sourceRoot, outputRoot, ...)` and clean-output behavior | first |
| nine-cell delivery facts | Slice 1 | Slices 2, 3, 4, 5 | private typed table with generated roots, delivery kind, package ID, embedded root, destination | before installer work |
