# Targeted delta review — Axis B: test quality and corpus

VOTE: REVISE

Reviewed only the PROPOSAL-10 corpus/test-quality delta and the committed internal/acceptance framework. Earlier closed material and declined test additions were not reopened.

## BLOCKER B-DELTA-1 — CoverageSpec has no typed per-case assignments, so its hard coverage gate cannot execute

**Where:** PROPOSAL-10 §16.0.2(b), §16.0.3 condition 5, §16.0.4, and §18.4 IP-W1/W2/W3; baseline internal/acceptance/schema.go:164-173, internal/acceptance/loader.go:30-39 and 246-270, internal/acceptance/report.go:52-190.

The new types declare dimensions, allowed values, milestones, and a result, but no Case field or observation maps a case to a typed (CoverageDimensionID, CoverageValue) assignment. The current case/schema/loader only carries Mutations []MutationOperatorID, and the report observes only mutant IDs. Consequently the promised check that every gated dimension has a case per value cannot derive coverage from executed cases. reader_cursor.yaml and guard_mutation.yaml can therefore list milestone-scoped dimensions without the framework being able to detect an uncovered value; IP-W1/W2/W3 only schedule widening, not executable coverage.

**Fix:** extend the shared schema with a typed case-level coverage assignment (not a string map), strict YAML/typed validation against the closed CoverageSpec dimension/value sets, and evaluation that counts only successfully executed source cases. Require exactly-once source-case observations and fail for every uncovered gated pair. Add framework tests for M1 gating, later-milestone ungated reporting, each widening transition, and duplicate/unknown assignment rejection.

## BLOCKER B-DELTA-2 — Source mutation has no case binding or executable adapter, so it cannot prove a must-fail row flips for its stated reason

**Where:** PROPOSAL-10 §16.0.2(c), §16.0.3 conditions 2-4, §16.1 item 1, §16.2 capability-scope rows, and §16.4; baseline internal/acceptance/schema.go:119-153 and 164-173, internal/acceptance/mutation.go:34-132 and 172-257, internal/acceptance/report.go:52-190.

SourceMutationOperator contains only ID, Guard, and Rationale; SourceMutationResult contains no corpus/case ID, baseline/mutated outcome, or mutation adapter. The existing Case.Mutations is a closed MutationOperatorID enum and ExpandMutations can only transform case data through its fixed applyMutation switch; EvaluateMutations executes/accounting only generated mutants, not source cases. Thus a capability-scope YAML row cannot declare a compatible source operator, and removing one axis comparison cannot be shown to make that exact Bound/unexpired/in-scope row pass. The same missing execution path leaves MutateRemovePayloadField asserted rather than demonstrably killed by the authentic-capture process test. The proposed extensible roster also conflicts with the existing closed enum and S1-only framework ownership.

**Fix:** add a shared, bounded source-mutation contract and runner registration that maps each declared source operator to (a) an isolated-worktree mutator and (b) the exact corpus case(s)/production-path target it must execute. Record baseline and mutated case outcomes keyed by corpus/case/operator; fail unless every required must-fail row first fails with its declared oracle and flips only under its own source mutation. Keep existing closed MutationOperatorID for data mutations; make source operators registry-backed and extensible by later slice owners through the shared internal/acceptance contract, with S1 ownership/transfer made explicit. Test a deliberately unlinked operator, an unexecuted source case, a wrong-row flip, and a green MutateRemovePayloadField as failures.

## Closed in this delta

The plan removes internal/lifecycle/corpus/**, extends internal/acceptance, adds capture metadata/P0-CAPTURE, scopes deferred coverage with IP-W1/W2/W3, resolves retention as M1-owned S1/S1R work, assigns named item 11 to S3 L2/M2, retains delete-or-invert owners for obsolete tests, and corrects corpus filenames/counts. Those closures do not repair the two executable-framework gaps above.

## Checks

- Read internal/acceptance/{schema,loader,mutation,report,snapshot}.go and its tests.
- Read PROPOSAL-10 §16, §§17-19, §3.2, §15, §18.1/§18.3/§18.4/§18.5, design field, URD/UAT context, and prior reviews.
- Confirmed no current internal/lifecycle/corpus/** files.

- No files edited, commits, pushes, ratification, or severity tree."}

{"description":"DEFERRED at Plan UAT. User selected the combination of two surveyed patterns.

USER VERBATIM (initial deferral): "How do other successful projects dealing with multimedia content in API request bodies deal with storing them? For right now, we can do metadata only. But I would like the body to be saved in the future. Should be its own DEFERRED followup epic."

USER VERBATIM (design direction): "The options I like for the followup epic: they should combine these two: [content-addressed blob store + metadata row] [keep bodies for the interesting minority]. Ideally, there would be an industry-standard and battle-tested open-source project that we can use or extract patterns from."

## The combination, and why the two halves reinforce each other

    occurrence row  (append-always; DB row id is the only occurrence identity)
        |
        +-- payload_digest  -->  CAS blob  (content-addressed; dedup is free)

Two retried hooks produce two distinct occurrence rows pointing at ONE blob. Append-always and deduplication stop competing because they act at different layers - occurrence identity is positional, body identity is content.

Selective retention (the Sentry pattern: keep full payloads for the interesting minority) then keeps blob COUNT low, which is what makes garbage collection and refcounting tractable.

The non-obvious reinforcement: dedup is most valuable exactly where selective retention fires. If the codebook is missing a field, that event fires repeatedly and produces MANY near-identical unclassified payloads. Content addressing collapses the identical ones automatically, so the pathological case for retention volume is the case dedup handles best.

## Recommended building blocks - verified against this tree

1. github.com/opencontainers/go-digest v1.0.0 for the digest type.
   ALREADY IN THE MODULE GRAPH as an indirect requirement. `go list -deps` returns nothing outside the standard library, so it is pure Go, cgo-free, and adds ZERO new transitive dependencies - adopting it only promotes an existing module to direct. Gives the canonical `sha256:<hex>` form, parsing and validation, and a streaming Verifier so a body can be hashed while written and rejected on mismatch. Battle-tested across the entire OCI and Docker ecosystem.
   Note: AGENTS.md requires supervisor approval for new dependencies. Approval granted on the above grounds; record it in the implementing proposal.

2. OCI image-layout `blobs/<algorithm>/<hex>` for the on-disk layout, if external storage is chosen. A published spec rather than an invented scheme, and inspectable with ordinary tools. Caveat worth knowing: OCI layout does not sharibly shard, whereas Git shards on the first two hex characters to avoid directory and inode pressure. At low blob counts flat is fine; adopt Git's sharding if volume grows.

3. distribution/distribution (the CNCF reference registry) for the BlobStore / BlobWriter INTERFACE SHAPE. Extract the pattern, do not take the dependency. Its interfaces already solve resumable writes, Stat, Open, and digest verification on commit.

4. Refcount through the occurrence rows themselves. A blob is live iff some occurrence references its digest; GC is "delete blobs no occurrence references". That is Git reachability GC and the OCI untagged-blob problem - both well understood. Privacy deletion is: delete the blob, null the references, keep the occurrence metadata.

Surveyed and REJECTED, with reasons:
- folbricht/desync (casync in pure Go): chunk-level dedup via content-defined chunking. Built for large, similar files. Our payloads are bounded at 1 MiB and usually far smaller, so chunking overhead exceeds its benefit.
- go-git storage layer: correct model and pure Go, but a large dependency for blob storage alone. Take the sharding idea, not the module.
- Bazel Remote Execution API CAS: battle-tested at scale, but gRPC and distributed - unjustified for a local single-user store.
- restic / Perkeep: sound designs, but whole systems rather than embeddable components.

## The honest counter-argument: SQLite may win at this size class

SQLite is genuinely good at small blobs - its published benchmark shows blobs under roughly 100 KiB read FASTER from SQLite than from individual files. Our payloads are bounded at 1 MiB and typically much smaller. A CAS TABLE inside the existing database (digest primary key, refcount derived from occurrence references) would be simpler: one file to back up, transactional consistency with the occurrence insert, and no dangling-reference or orphan class at all.

Against that: this epic has already spent real effort bounding the shared-SQLite write budget (see aura-plugins-cvlu6 and commit f513772). Blobs inside the contended file add write volume and grow it. But selective retention makes that volume small, which argues back toward SQLite.

Two forces point in opposite directions and the answer is MEASURABLE, not arguable. Therefore:
  - Define a BlobStore interface that both implementations satisfy.
  - Ship the SQLite-internal implementation FIRST: simpler, transactional, no new failure modes, no second system to back up.
  - Switch to filesystem CAS only if measurement shows write volume or file growth actually hurts.
  - The digest type and layout spec are identical either way, so the switch stays contained.

## Ordering hazard to design for explicitly

The classic CAS integration bug. With an external store you can crash between writing the blob and committing the occurrence, or between committing the occurrence and writing the blob. Only one order is safe:

    write blob  ->  then commit occurrence

An orphan blob is harmless and GC reclaims it. A dangling reference is corruption. State the order and test the crash window. This hazard does not exist in the SQLite-internal variant, which is a genuine point in its favour.

## Scope
Storage backend selection by measurement; deletion and tombstone semantics; refcount and GC; the crash-ordering guarantee; redaction boundary before storage (structured allow-lists, never deny-lists - deny-lists always miss a field); explicit truncation recording per the OpenTelemetry convention; and the interaction with append-always occurrence identity.

## Prerequisite
M1 ships metadata-only, with bounded inline bytes retained ONLY for occurrences that fail to classify. That inline path is the minimal precursor to this epic and its predicate ("is this occurrence interesting?") is the same predicate this epic generalises.","title":"FOLLOWUP: content-addressed payload retention for the interesting minority"}

Note that pruning is strictly better than the original selective-ingestion design: the decision is made with real data in hand rather than guessed at ingest.

2. EXTERNAL CONTENT-ADDRESSED STORAGE, only if measurement demands it.

- go-git storage layer: correct model, pure Go, but a large dependency for blob storage alone. Take the sharding idea, not the module.
- Bazel Remote Execution API CAS: proven at scale but gRPC and distributed; unjustified for a local single-user store.
- restic, Perkeep: sound designs, whole systems rather than embeddable components.

## Trigger

Revisit when database growth or shared-file write volume is measured to affect the start_slice deadline budget (aura-plugins-cvlu6) or backup and sync cost. Not before - the MVP position is deliberate and the data does not exist yet.","title":"FOLLOWUP: payload truncation, filtering, and external content-addressed storage"}

`internal/lifecycle/receipt/interpreted_test.go:308-347` calls `json.Decoder.DisallowUnknownFields` and then checks a decoded map for the four top-level keys, but `encoding/json` accepts duplicate object members and applies last-member-wins semantics. The map check also collapses duplicates. Because the PostToolBatch test structurally decodes returned bytes rather than comparing an independent raw fixture, a payload with a duplicate `contract`, `semantic`, identity, or unresolved `reason` member can still satisfy the current oracle while different JSON readers disagree about the durable evidence.

## User impact
Interpreted evidence is a persisted wire payload. The test suite can report green for a non-canonical payload whose duplicate fields make consumers observe different semantic, identity, unresolved-fact, or contract values.

## Concrete fix
Use the existing `ir.StrictJSONWithPresence` decoder for the returned payload with required fields `semantic`, `identities`, `unresolved_facts`, and `contract`, retaining the independent primitive oracle and exact value assertions. That shared decoder rejects duplicate members at every nesting depth, unknown fields, omitted top-level fields, and trailing JSON. Add a focused duplicate-member regression case if needed to keep this requirement visible.

# Handoff: Supervisor to SLICE-3 Worker

## Production Code Path

Plan backward from the next built-binary path:

`valid waist.L2 -> receipt.NewInterpreted -> receipt.Record -> Record.Effect() -> SLICE-7 passes the effect beside the occurrence to receipt.Service.Receive`.

This slice owns construction of the interpreted durable evidence. It performs no append and opens no database. SLICE-7 later supplies the effect to the existing record stage in one operation.

## Exclusive M1a Write Set

- `internal/lifecycle/receipt/interpreted.go` (new)
- `internal/lifecycle/receipt/interpreted_test.go` (new)
- `internal/lifecycle/receipt/journal.go` (interpreted evidence kind/result slot only)
- `internal/lifecycle/model/occurrence.go` (`NativeBinding.NativeName` only)
- `internal/lifecycle/model/occurrence_test.go` (native-name preservation only, if needed)

Do not edit another path without reporting the concrete blocker before doing so.

## Required Public Surface

```go
type Record struct { /* opaque, constructor-owned */ }

func NewInterpreted(l2 waist.L2, contract ir.RuntimeContractID) (Record, error)
func (r Record) Semantic() runtime.EventSemantic
func (r Record) Identities() []waist.SemanticIdentity
func (r Record) UnresolvedFacts() []waist.UnresolvedFact
func (r Record) Contract() ir.RuntimeContractID
func (r Record) IsValid() bool
func (r Record) Effect() provenance.Effect
```

Extend `model.NativeBinding` with `NativeName string`; SLICE-2 will populate it.

Use unexported fields plus `constructed` state. Slice accessors return defensive copies. `Record{}.Effect()` returns the zero effect rather than forging evidence or panicking.

Use unexported constants `provenance.ResultSlotID("interpreted")` and `provenance.EvidenceKind("pasture.lifecycle.interpreted.v1")`, following current namespaced-v1 evidence conventions. The canonical private JSON payload has explicit `semantic`, `identities`, `unresolved_facts`, and `contract` fields. `ContentDigest` is SHA-256 of the exact payload bytes.

## Construction Contract

- Reject `!l2.IsValid()` with an actionable typed validation error.
- Reject an invalid contract and a contract that differs from `l2.Origin().Contract()`; the redundant parameter must not permit contract forgery.
- Snapshot the L2 semantic arm, exact `[]waist.SemanticIdentity`, exact unresolved facts, and pinned runtime contract.
- Keep identities in waist/runtime vocabulary; never convert them to `[]model.NativeBinding`.
- Preserve identity values byte-for-byte without normalization.
- `Effect()` is pure value conversion with no context, I/O, database, clock, environment, or dependency.

## Explicit M1a Omissions

- No projection, SQL, migration, reader, or `pasture hook lifecycle list` work.

## Evidence
internal/lifecycle/receipt/service_test.go:99,127 build the mocked committed result with the private production receiptSlot; :159-160 verify the first effect against private receiptSlot and receiptKind. Those constants are the same unexported values used by receipt.Service.Receive and JournalAppender in internal/lifecycle/receipt/journal.go:18-19.

## User impact
The receipt can be persisted under a wrong result slot or evidence kind while these tests remain green. Downstream Provenance queries can then omit or misclassify every occurrence, so durable lifecycle evidence is wrong without a failing gate.

## Rationale
The accepted contract requires the literal public values occurrence and pasture.lifecycle.occurrence.v1; comparing a production result with the same production constants is tautological and does not independently prove the wire contract.

## Concrete fix
Replace every occurrence-slot/kind expectation in service_test.go, including mocked result slots, with independently authored typed values such as provenance.ResultSlotID("occurrence") and provenance.EvidenceKind("pasture.lifecycle.occurrence.v1"). # M1b SLICE-4 Contract Freeze

## End-User Production Path

This slice owns the pure middle stages consumed later by the final hook wiring:

`waist.L2 -> legalize.Event -> gate Legalized or typed NoAuthority -> backend.BuildConsultation -> receipt.ConsultationRecord + typed HostResponse`.

Observation terminates at the interpreted record and yields no L3. Gate-consultation yields one immutable L3 value and backend returns a canonical consultation record plus typed Proceed response. Explicit human response yields typed NoAuthority and no L3/backend mapping. SLICE-7 later passes the consultation effect beside the interpreted effect to the existing single `receipt.Service.Receive` call.

## Exclusive Ownership

- `internal/lifecycle/legalize/**`
- `internal/lifecycle/backend/**`

Do not edit waist, receipt, model, runtime profiles, tasks, handlers, commands, activation, generated files, or documentation. Report a blocker before touching any other path.

## Frozen Legalize API

Package `internal/lifecycle/legalize` defines no second semantic/arm enum and consumes `runtime.EventSemantic` from `waist.L2`.

- `type Legalized struct` with private construction state.
- `Legalized.IsValid() bool`.
- `Legalized.AuthorityExercised() bool`, always false at M1.
- `Legalized.MarshalJSON() ([]byte,error)` emits exactly compact `{"authority":"not-exercised"}`.
- `Legalized.ConsultationLegalized()` satisfies the existing waist port.
- `type NoAuthority struct` with private construction state and `IsValid() bool`.
- `type Result struct` with private semantic, legalized, no-authority, and construction state.
- `Result.Semantic() runtime.EventSemantic`, `Result.Legalized() (Legalized,bool)`, `Result.NoAuthority() (NoAuthority,bool)`, and `Result.IsValid() bool` return defensive valid variants.
- `func Event(waist.L2) (Result,error)` is the sole production entry point.

`Event` rejects invalid L2. Observation returns a valid observation result with neither L3 nor NoAuthority. Gate-consultation returns a valid Legalized result. Explicit human response returns valid NoAuthority with no L3 and no ordinary error. Unknown semantics fail actionably. Dispatch is keyed on semantic, never blocking mode.

There is deliberately no context, actor resolver, committed-state dependency, clock, or writer in this M1 API. The accepted proposal requires static no-authority/no-write behavior at M1, the authority mechanism is explicitly deferred, and `receipt.IdentityResolver` remains the sole persisted actor source. Historical replay, observation recorder, awaited-reply refusal, BackendView, mutation selection, and actor lookup are not ported.

## Frozen Backend API

Package `internal/lifecycle/backend` defines:

- `type Decision uint8` with the sole M1 value `DecisionProceed` and validity/String behavior.
- `type HostResponse struct` with private construction state.
- `HostResponse.Decision() Decision`, `IsValid() bool`, `MarshalJSON() ([]byte,error)`, and `ConsultationResponse()`.
- `func BuildConsultation(interpreted receipt.Record, legalized legalize.Legalized) (receipt.ConsultationRecord, HostResponse, error)` as the sole production entry point.

`BuildConsultation` validates the real interpreted gate record and concrete legalized L3, constructs a valid Proceed response whose JSON is exactly compact `{"decision":"proceed"}`, and delegates canonical record/effect construction to `receipt.NewConsultation`. It never accepts an arbitrary response, reconstructs receipt evidence, appends, mutates authority, or performs I/O.

## Event and Terminal Matrix

- `SessionStart` observation: valid observation result; no L3, response, consultation, or authority.
- Gate events in the accepted ten-event M1 set: ordinal 8 PreToolUse, 13 PostToolBatch, 25 PreCompact, 29 Elicitation. Each uses the generic gate semantic path and yields Legalized plus backend Proceed and consultation. No event-name whitelist is encoded.
- PostToolBatch interpreted evidence retains its unresolved tool-call fact; these stages do not rewrite it.
- Ordinal 30 ElicitationResult: typed NoAuthority; no L3, backend call, response, consultation, or authority.
- A valid nonblocking gate cannot be built through the runtime/waist public API; semantic dispatch is enforced by implementation inspection rather than a production mutator or test seam.

## Composition and Write Boundary

Tests construct real L2 values through runtime contract -> waist.BindEvent -> EventBinding.NewEvent, then real interpreted records through receipt.NewInterpreted. A backend integration test passes the resulting interpreted and consultation effects to real `receipt.Service.Receive` with injected external fakes and proves compatibility with one operation containing occurrence, interpreted, consultation in order. Legalize/backend themselves expose no dependency capable of Append, Apply, task mutation, phase transition, or authority write. Built-command reachability and the final one-Receive proof remain SLICE-7.

## Explicit Omissions

No write-gate mechanism, committed-state read, real deny, actor lookup, mutation emission, ReplayKey/dedup, BackendView, handler wiring, host stdout/stderr/exit behavior, activation, corpus work, event whitelist, generated edits, second Append, or test-only production seam.

## Validation

Every Go test invocation includes `-race`. # M1b SLICE-5 Contract Freeze

## End-User Production Path

`registration.ClaudeCode2_1_210 -> activation.ClaudeCode2_1_210 -> codegen hooks.json and pasture-activation.json -> pasture hook lifecycle static admission`.

The shipped handler consumes a static exhaustive 30-event activation manifest and performs no filesystem access. A separate test-time capture-corpus loader and evaluator proves which target events may be represented by event-bound static capture evidence. Later SLICE-2 breadth tests consume this API against the real corpus; SLICE-7 consumes the static activation entries through the existing handler.

## Exclusive Ownership

Hand-authored:
- `internal/lifecycle/activation/**`
- `internal/codegen/claude_hooks.go`
- `internal/codegen/claude_hooks_test.go`

Generated by `make generate`, never hand-edited:
- `internal/target/claudecode/assets/pasture-hooks/hooks/hooks.json`
- `internal/target/claudecode/assets/pasture-hooks/hooks/pasture-activation.json`

Do not edit acceptance, runtime, registration, handlers, ingress Claude testdata, installer/CLI, or SLICE-7 wiring. Generated registration and payload Go files remain read-only.

## Static Activation Contract

Declare exactly one private typed ten-event target table using generated registration constants: SessionStart, SessionEnd, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch, PreCompact, PostCompact, Elicitation, and ElicitationResult. No native-name whitelist or duplicate registry.

Current partition is exact:
- SessionStart: Enabled with event-bound named capture proof and event-bound named production proof.
- Remaining nine targets: WithheldMissingFixture.
- Remaining twenty generated registration events: WithheldOutsideTargetSet.

Replace generic `FixtureEvidenceAuthentic` and `ProductionProofPassing` tokens with closed event-bound proof types. The SessionStart capture proof names the reviewed 2.1.210 authentic fixture evidence. The production proof names `cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_production_test.go:TestEnabledClaudeEventToOccurrenceAndInterpretedEvidence`. `NewEnabled` requires both proof values to bind to the same requested event. Enabled entries carry zero reason and both proofs; withheld entries carry one valid reason and zero proofs.

`ClaudeCode2_1_210TargetEvents() []model.ContractEventKind` returns a defensive copy. `ClaudeCode2_1_210()` returns a fresh exhaustive 30-entry manifest, imports no filesystem package, and derives state only from the typed declaration table.

## Capture Corpus API

Add `internal/lifecycle/activation/corpus.go` with strongly typed `Classification`, `Decision`, `CorpusReason`, `ProvenanceSource`, scalar case components, opaque `Corpus`, and immutable `Evaluation`.

Public API:
```go
func LoadCorpus(path string) (Corpus, error)
func (c Corpus) Cases() []Case
func Evaluate(root string, c Case) (Evaluation, error)
```

`LoadCorpus` boundedly and strictly decodes one YAML document with known fields, preserves source order, and performs no fixture/provenance I/O. It rejects malformed/unknown/duplicate fields, aliases/tags, trailing documents, missing required keys, invalid enums, empty required strings, duplicate case names, inconsistent classification/decision/reason combinations, and oversized case collections. An escaping fixture path remains valid metadata because it is a negative evaluator input.

A typed `CoverageError` exposes a `MissingCoverage` bitset. A valid corpus requires at least one must-pass case, at least one must-fail case, and all four bypass reasons: non-authentic-origin, digest-mismatch, version-out-of-range, path-escape. The owned syntactically valid all-pass `testdata/captures_vacuous.yaml` must fail with the exact missing fail-class and four-category bits.

`Cases()` returns a fresh slice. Case fields are scalar/value-only.

## Evidence Evaluation

`Evaluate` ignores expected decision/reason, classification, case provenance, and mutation prose. Those fields are oracles and review provenance, never SUT inputs.

Binding precedence:
1. Absolute, lexical, or resolved fixture/provenance path escape -> withheld/path-escape without opening escaped paths.
2. Sibling JSON provenance origin is not authentic-capture -> withheld/non-authentic-origin.
3. Valid declared SHA-256 differs from exact fixture bytes -> withheld/digest-mismatch.
4. Valid parsed Claude host version is outside the pinned runtime range -> withheld/version-out-of-range.
5. Provenance harness/event must resolve through the generated Claude manifest and belong to the typed ten-event target set; malformed/non-target evidence is an actionable error.
6. Authentic evidence passing `acceptance.CaptureProvenance.ValidateFixture` -> enabled.

The explicit root controls containment. Both fixture and sibling `<stem>.provenance.json` must remain lexically and after symlink resolution beneath it. Missing contained files, malformed digest/version/timestamp/JSON, trailing JSON, wrong harness, and unknown event are actionable errors rather than expected rejections. Provenance JSON decoding is deliberately non-strict to permit existing `redaction` and `event` fields, but consumes only one bounded object and retains `event`. `ValidateFixture` remains the success authority; preflight checks exist only to classify expected controls.

Capture metadata is reviewed caller assertion plus tamper evidence, not cryptographic proof that a human captured the payload.

## Code Generation

The Claude hook emitter must reject duplicate activation entries, missing registration entries, and invalid state/reason/proof combinations. Support JSON emits stable reason names instead of numeric `reason-N` values and emits named capture/production proof fields only for enabled events. Guard SessionStart augmentation exactly as PreCompact is guarded so generation cannot panic if SessionStart is absent. Preserve the independent unconditional PreToolUse git-discipline hook when lifecycle PreToolUse remains withheld.

# M1b SLICE-7 Contract Freeze

## End-User Production Path

Complete the final merge-last path `built pasture hook lifecycle -> static activation -> ingress/claude.Parse -> valid frontend/claude.Bind -> EventBinding.NewEvent -> legalize.Event + receipt.NewInterpreted -> optional backend.BuildConsultation -> one receipt.Service.Receive`. Non-valid captures retain the accepted occurrence-only branch. The human-invoked `hook lifecycle list` behavior remains unchanged.

## Exclusive Ownership

- `internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go`
- `cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle.go`
- `cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_production_test.go`
- `docs/privacy.md` (new)

Extend the existing production test; do not add a new test file. Report a concrete blocker before editing any other path. Do not edit activation, ingress fixtures/corpus, legalize, backend, receipt, list command/handler, main, generated outputs, or capture tooling.

## Valid-Capture Wiring

For every valid L2, call both `legalize.Event` and `receipt.NewInterpreted` before any write. Observation persists occurrence + interpreted. Gate consultation requires the typed `Legalized` terminal, calls `backend.BuildConsultation`, validates its constructor-built Proceed response, and persists occurrence + interpreted + consultation in that exact order. Explicit human response requires the typed `NoAuthority` terminal, calls no backend rule, and persists occurrence + interpreted. All durable effects enter one `receipt.Service.Receive` call, preserving blob-first then one journal operation; never issue a second Append.

Only `CaptureValid` enters the waist. Every non-valid disposition remains one occurrence-only Receive with zero interpreted/consultation evidence.

## Enabled-Set Breadth Proof

Keep the named built-binary test `TestEnabledClaudeEventToOccurrenceAndInterpretedEvidence` as the production proof. Its literal event rows must equal the complete static enabled set and use only admitted authentic corpus fixtures/provenance. Assert event-specific payload-derived interpreted identity kind/value pairs, not occurrence bindings or arm metadata alone. At the current reviewed evidence state this is exactly SessionStart; the other nine targets remain `WithheldMissingFixture`. Contract-shaped in-memory breadth rows from SLICE-2 are not authentic and must never enable or satisfy this proof.

Prove byte-identical deliveries create distinct occurrence records and operation identities; occurrence and interpreted effects for each delivery share one operation. Prove `pasture hook lifecycle list` returns readable occurrence plus interpreted records, and the public lifecycle reader returns exact payload bytes by digest. Gate consultation wiring is established by its generic production caller plus already-merged legalize/backend/receipt composition tests while gate events remain withheld; do not bypass activation or invent a production test seam.

## Lifecycle Command Safety

The Claude-invoked leaf always exits zero and reports faults on stderr. Remove `exitWithCode` and the `MarkFlagRequired` loop. Bind flag-error handling to the lifecycle leaf only, not the parent subtree, so `hook lifecycle list` preserves standard non-zero semantics. Replace `cobra.NoArgs` with permissive parsing and report unexpected positional arguments inside `RunE`. Route missing flags through the handler.

`RunE` must defer a recover that names the recovered value on stderr and forces a nil return. Verify this exact shape by inspection only: no panic-injection flag/env, deliberate crash path, or crash-expecting test. Command-path drift resolved before this leaf remains explicitly out of scope.

Extend the built-binary fault matrix for unwritable database, missing flag, unknown flag, extra positional argument, and over-limit payload; each exits zero and reports the fault class. Malformed payload is not a fault: exit zero, empty stderr, one malformed occurrence, no interpreted or consultation evidence.

## Privacy and Evidence

Publish `docs/privacy.md` stating that payloads delivered through registered hooks are persisted by default and may include prompts, tool inputs, and file contents. This documentation is required before PreToolUse may be enabled, but this slice does not change activation. Authentic capture gathering remains permission-blocked and non-gating; never synthesize fixtures or provenance.

## Deferred items

### Citation offsets (verified wrong, no behavioural consequence)
- cobra command.go :1167 -> :1169 for 'ExecuteC returns the error regardless'
  (:1165-1167 is the UsageString print). Cited in SLICE-7 and section 6.
- NewIdentity applies validateIdentityValue at :162, not :161 (:161 is the
  preceding brace).
- verifyIdentities rejects !IsValid() at :540-548, not :538-545.
- 43dbbf1^:event.go:424 is the doc comment; the IsValid accessor is :425.
- Semantics.EquivalentTo runs :283-317, not :283-320 — the cited range swallows
  Semantics.IsValid at :319-320, which the opacity argument depends on and which
  must NOT be dropped.

### Naming and provenance of citations
- 'baseline' names two different commits: frontmatter baseline: 5271a12 versus
  section 3 / section 6 'baseline 511e2bb'. Code is byte-identical between them,
  so both technical claims hold. Suggest renaming one, e.g. code-baseline.
- 'do not silently drop it' is presented in quotation marks as ratified text; the
  URD's actual words are 'automate data entry, not semantic guessing' and 'It does
  not drop the input, collapse it, or manufacture authority.' The paraphrase is
  faithful; the quotation marks are not.
- The declared ten-ordinal set (1, 3, 8, 11, 12, 13, 25, 26, 29, 30) is never
  cited inside the impl plan; it lives at proposal-11:192-203. SLICE-5's worker
  must hunt for the enumeration defining its own deliverable.

### Completeness of reference material
- Section 1's package map omits ingress/ and model/, though SLICE-2 owns
  ingress/claude/capture.go + testdata and SLICE-3 owns model/{reader,occurrence}.go.
  The M1a data path is not readable off the map.
- V4, V7 and V12 are discharged but unlabelled (V1/V2/V3/V6/V8 are labelled).
  V4 = section 6 M1a gate 2; V7 = SLICE-5's typed withholding reasons;
  V12 = SLICE-1's unresolved fact + SLICE-2's tool-call-unresolved.
- docs/privacy.md is an unlisted cross-slice contract (SLICE-7 -> SLICE-5, M1b) and
  is the only one whose direction the merge-last rule inverts.
- The M1a read-back handle (interpreted evidence kind + payload decode,
  SLICE-3 -> SLICE-7) is missing from the section 4 contract table. Both would need
  exporting; the convention today is unexported (receipt/journal.go:19).

### Scope caveats worth stating
- The recover() covers same-goroutine panics inside RunE only — not a panic in a
  library goroutine, not a runtime fatal error, not a panic in init() or in
  cobra's machinery before RunE.
- The non-strict provenance decode buys tolerance for two keys (redaction, event)
  and gives up unknown-key detection; the tradeoff is not named. A declared
  eight-field local struct with DisallowUnknownFields would get both.
- 'defers a recover() that returns nil' is loose Go: a deferred function cannot
  assign an unnamed result. It works (error's zero value is nil) but a worker may
  add a named result believing it required.

### Convention and placement
- The capture corpus is placed at testdata/captures.yaml 'beside fixtures/', while
  the tree already has testdata/corpora/ (claude_2_1_210_catalogue.yaml).
- The fixture naming convention for the nine outstanding 2.1.220 captures is
  unstated. The script writes ${event}.json; the committed fixture is
  session_start_2_1_210.json — only the latter distinguishes a 2.1.210 from a
  2.1.220 capture of the same event.

### Stale after rev9/rev10
- SLICE-2 still says the event 'goes withheld the moment SLICE-5's gate lands'.
  Since the fixture gate now runs in activation's tests rather than at runtime, a
  missing provenance record fails a test rather than withholding an event. Same
  obligation, wrong stated mechanism.
- SLICE-3's 'what section 6's M1a gate explicitly rejects' overstates the pointer:
  section 6 rejects asserting off the occurrence, and says nothing about the
  record's field type.

{"id":"aura-plugins-ub89r","title":"FOLLOWUP: payload truncation, filtering, and external content-addressed storage","description":"Rescoped after the user changed the MVP retention decision.

USER VERBATIM: "Actually: we should just keep all bodies, for all objects. at a later date, we can decide to truncate or filter uninteresting bodies. SQLite is great for the MVP. just put the blob there."

## What the MVP now does, so this epic starts from the right baseline

M1 stores the raw native payload body for EVERY occurrence, content-addressed, in the existing SQLite database. No external store, no selective predicate, no truncation. The occurrence row references a body by digest; identical bodies collapse.

This epic therefore no longer covers "should we store bodies" - that is answered and shipped. It covers what to do once volume makes storing everything untenable.

## Scope

1. TRUNCATION AND FILTERING - the named later lever.
   Decide which bodies are uninteresting and what to do with them. Options to weigh when volume data exists: size-capped truncation with the truncation recorded explicitly (the OpenTelemetry convention - a bound that silently discards is indistinguishable from a bug); age-tiered retention, full body hot for N days then digest-only, which is the APM standard; and predicate-based filtering, where the Sentry pattern of keeping the interesting minority becomes a pruning rule rather than an ingestion rule. Note that pruning is strictly better than the original selective-ingestion design: the decision is made with real data in hand rather than guessed at ingest.

2. EXTERNAL CONTENT-ADDRESSED STORAGE, only if measurement demands it.
   SQLite is genuinely good at this size class - blobs under roughly 100 KiB read faster from SQLite than from individual files, and payloads are bounded at 1 MiB. Move out only when database growth or write volume is demonstrated to hurt, not on principle.
   If moved: use the OCI image-layout blobs/<algorithm>/<hex> - a published spec rather than an invented scheme, inspectable with ordinary tools. Adopt Git's two-hex-character sharding if blob counts grow enough to pressure directories and inodes; OCI layout is flat and that is fine only at low counts. Extract the BlobStore / BlobWriter interface shape from distribution/distribution, the CNCF reference registry, which already solves resumable writes, Stat, Open and verification on commit - take the pattern, not the dependency.
   The crash-ordering hazard applies the moment storage leaves the transaction: write blob, then commit occurrence. An orphan blob is harmless and reclaimable; a dangling reference is corruption. This ordering is already required in the MVP because the blob write is split out of the occurrence commit for lock-hold reasons, so the discipline is in place before the storage moves.

3. GARBAGE COLLECTION AND DELETION.
   A blob is live iff some occurrence references its digest. GC is "delete blobs no occurrence references" - Git reachability GC and the OCI untagged-blob problem, both well understood. Privacy deletion is delete the blob, null the references, keep the occurrence metadata so the ledger stays complete.

4. REDACTION BOUNDARY.
   Structured allow-lists, never deny-lists - Stripe and Datadog both learned that deny-lists always miss a field. Relevant because store-all makes every prompt, tool input and file content persistent by default.

## Already settled, do not relitigate

- github.com/opencontainers/go-digest v1.0.0 is the digest type. Verified in-tree: already an indirect module requirement, `go list -deps` returns nothing outside the standard library, so it is pure Go, cgo-free and adds zero new transitive dependencies. Adoption only promotes it to direct. Supervisor approval granted per the AGENTS.md dependency rule.
- Content addressing stays regardless of backend. With store-all the dedup value increased, not decreased.

## Surveyed and rejected, with reasons

- folbricht/desync (casync, pure Go): chunk-level dedup for large similar files. Payloads are bounded at 1 MiB and usually far smaller, so chunking costs more than it returns.
- go-git storage layer: correct model, pure Go, but a large dependency for blob storage alone. Take the sharding idea, not the module.
- Bazel Remote Execution API CAS: proven at scale but gRPC and distributed; unjustified for a local single-user store.
- restic, Perkeep: sound designs, whole systems rather than embeddable components.

## Trigger

Revisit when database growth or shared-file write volume is measured to affect the start_slice deadline budget (aura-plugins-cvlu6) or backup and sync cost. Not before - the MVP position is deliberate and the data does not exist yet.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"epic","owner":"dayvidpham@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-07-30T03:33:15Z","created_by":"David Huu Pham","updated_at":"2026-07-30T03:41:04Z"}

# Status and stop condition

This proposal is planning authority only. It does not authorize fixture import, production edits, generated-output changes, activation, or worker dispatch. M2 requires plan review and Plan UAT before an implementation plan. M3 implementation remains additionally blocked on accepted M2 implementation UAT.

# Revision 2

Round-1 correctness and elegance reviews accepted the architecture. Test-quality review required one correction: baseline `make test` runs non-race Go tests and cannot be accepted evidence. This revision uses `CGO_ENABLED=1 make test-race`, explicitly forbids using the non-race target in this work, and clarifies that durable receipt commit completes before any typed response reaches stdout.

# Problem space

## Engineering axes

- Parallelism: M2 documentation can run beside M2 runtime foundation, but generated transport, handler wiring, and activation converge on shared files. M3 is intentionally sequential after accepted M2.
- Distribution: each harness invokes a local Pasture subprocess, potentially from separate host processes. One SQLite/Provenance operation durably groups occurrence, interpretation, and optional consultation evidence.
- Multiplicity: providers are many; semantic operation/effect planning is one. Provider ingress and response encoding remain separate N-side adapters around one middle-end.
- Frequency and cost: hooks may fire many times per session. The middle-end is pure and allocation-bounded; durable cost remains one existing receipt operation per invocation.
- Trust boundary: native payloads and foreign adapters are untrusted transport. Constructor-owned Go values become trusted only after provider ingress, frontend binding, and `waist.EventBinding.NewEvent`.

## Relationships

- A provider has one ingress parser, one frontend mapping, one activation table, and one mechanical response encoder.
- A verified `waist.L2` is the input to the shared middle-end; it is not a provider payload.
- A `middleend.Plan` has one interpreted effect, optionally one consultation effect, and optionally one constructor-built `backend.HostResponse`.
- An authentic fixture is evidence for one observed provider/runtime. OpenCode callback capture bytes are not a separate native wire protocol.

# Current-tree facts

At baseline `0414ad9`, `internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go` directly composes `legalize.Event`, `receipt.NewInterpreted`, and `backend.BuildConsultation`. There is no `internal/lifecycle/lower.go`, generic `Lower`, `EquivalentTo`, provider-neutral response result, OpenCode ingress/frontend, or Codex ingress/frontend.

The reusable production contracts already exist in `waist`, `legalize`, `backend`, `receipt`, `projection`, and the public lifecycle reader. The current handler is Claude-only and returns only `error`; the CLI reports internal errors to stderr, exits successfully by accepted policy, and emits no stdout response.

The generated OpenCode and Codex lifecycle artifacts still read caller-selected `PASTURE_ADAPTER_EVENT`, `PASTURE_ADAPTER_OPERATION`, and `PASTURE_ADAPTER_INPUT` and call `pasture __adapter invoke`. That command remains valid for non-lifecycle semantic adapter use. Only the generated lifecycle route is replaced.

# Architecture decisions

## D1. Add one thin pure post-L2 plan

Create `internal/lifecycle/middleend/evaluate.go`. It composes the existing pure stages and owns effect ordering. It does not add a provider, context, tracker, clock, operation ID, persistence API, or new semantic/decision enum.

```go
package middleend

type Plan struct {
    // unexported constructor-owned interpreted record,
    // optional consultation record and optional host response
}

func Evaluate(event waist.L2) (Plan, error)
func (p Plan) Effects() []provenance.Effect
func (p Plan) Response() backend.HostResponse
func (p Plan) IsValid() bool
```

`Evaluate` calls, in order:

1. `legalize.Event(event)`;
2. `receipt.NewInterpreted(event, event.Origin().Contract())`;
3. for a gate only, `backend.BuildConsultation(interpreted, legalized)`.

Observation and existing explicit-human-response semantics produce only the interpreted effect and an invalid zero `HostResponse`; explicit human response must retain the existing valid `NoAuthority` check. Gate consultation produces interpreted then consultation effects and a valid `DecisionProceed` response. `Effects` returns a defensive slice in canonical order. No caller can construct or reorder a valid plan through exported fields.

This is the missing middle-end boundary without reviving stale `Lower`, `BackendView`, replay-key, or actor machinery.

## D2. Return the existing typed response and use static provider dispatch

Change the internal handler boundary to:

```go
func HookLifecycle(
    ctx context.Context,
    in HookLifecycleInput,
) (backend.HostResponse, error)
```

A successful observation returns the invalid zero response and nil error. `HookLifecycle` passes `middleend.Plan.Effects()` to `receipt.Service.Receive` and returns `middleend.Plan.Response()` only after `Receive` succeeds; a receipt error returns no response. A successful gate returns the constructor-built Proceed response after its receipt commits. The CLI writes the canonical `backend.HostResponse` JSON to stdout only when `IsValid()` is true. Existing accepted error handling remains stderr plus successful hook process exit; new negative behavior is not part of this MVP.

Keep one explicit `switch in.Harness` in the handler. Each case selects a generated registration/activation manifest, provider ingress parser, and provider frontend. Do not add a runtime provider registry, reflection, `init` registration, arbitrary map, or generic native-name reverse lookup. Provider frontends mirror the current Claude boundary:

```go
func Parse(
    raw []byte,
    event registration.Event,
    observedVersion string,
    envelope model.OccurrenceEnvelopeRef,
) Capture

func Bind(
    event model.ContractEventKind,
    bindings []model.NativeBinding,
) (waist.L1, []waist.Identity, error)
```

OpenCode and Codex each maintain one explicit registration-event to runtime-event mapping, as Claude does. This does not reopen deferred GitHub #62.

## D3. Replace stale exact profiles; do not build compatibility

Replace internal OpenCode 1.17.18 and Codex 0.144.1 profile constructors/IDs with exact `opencode@1.18.10` and `codex@0.146.0` contracts. Update `PinnedContracts`, lifecycle constructors, generated metadata, manifests, target descriptors, tests, and headers together.

Do not retain dual old/new profiles, fallback selection, skew negotiation, or a support matrix. There is no persisted OpenCode/Codex lifecycle receipt compatibility requirement on the landed Claude-only path. Source-reprofile the closed host catalogs needed by existing code generation, but activate and authentically validate only the two selected events per provider. A source-derived catalog entry is not authentic event evidence. Only the four user-cleared raw candidates may satisfy authentic fixture or activation proof.

Extend the static host-contract generator from one hard-coded Claude contract to a compile-time list of Claude plus the two selected OpenCode and Codex ingress contracts. Generate provider manifests/payload field maps and collision-checked shared event/field symbols. Do not hand-edit generated registration files and do not require exhaustive authentic fixtures.

## D4. Preserve the four exact raw candidates with provider-correct replay

Import exactly the four user-cleared candidates and provenance sidecars under provider ingress packages:

```text
internal/lifecycle/ingress/opencode/testdata/fixtures/
  session_created_1_18_10.capture.json
  session_created_1_18_10.provenance.json
  tool_execute_before_1_18_10.capture.json
  tool_execute_before_1_18_10.provenance.json

internal/lifecycle/ingress/codex/testdata/fixtures/
  session_start_0_146_0.json
  session_start_0_146_0.provenance.json
  pre_tool_use_0_146_0.json
  pre_tool_use_0_146_0.provenance.json
```

The OpenCode files preserve each selected JSONL record including its line bytes. Tests extract the nested callback `value` as `json.RawMessage` without normalizing it, because the host supplies an in-process object and the production plugin serializes that callback value. Provenance records both the parent lifecycle JSONL digest and extracted record digest, identifies callback-object observation, and never claims a native wire byte stream.

The Codex files copy exact command-hook stdin bytes. Every sidecar records observed runtime, inspected source revision, UTC capture time, method, source selector, exact digest, `origin: authentic-capture`, `redaction: none`, and user-clearance reference. No transcript, PostToolUse, Stop, final message, database, cache, or auth file is imported.

## D5. Replace lifecycle caller-selected operations with mechanical transport

OpenCode generated lifecycle code uses only `PASTURE_BIN` as an executable override. It invokes:

```text
pasture hook lifecycle --harness opencode 
  --event <statically generated event> --host-version 1.18.10
```

For `session.created`, stdin is the serialized callback event object and failure is logged without terminating the observation stream. For `tool.execute.before`, stdin is the serialized `{input, output:{args}}` callback value. The plugin requires canonical `{"decision":"proceed"}` stdout, then returns with `output.args` unchanged. It neither chooses an operation nor extracts semantic identities.

Codex generated event runners invoke the same command with harness `codex`, exact version `0.146.0`, and their statically generated event. The Python adapter forwards exact stdin, requires the canonical Proceed response for `PreToolUse`, and mechanically emits `{"continue":true}`. `SessionStart` is observe-only and emits the native default continuation object. Denial and `updatedInput` are absent.

Remove `PASTURE_ADAPTER_EVENT`, `PASTURE_ADAPTER_OPERATION`, and `PASTURE_ADAPTER_INPUT` from OpenCode/Codex lifecycle artifacts. Do not remove `pasture __adapter invoke` or its non-lifecycle tests.

## D6. Use direct positive evidence; do not weaken the Claude corpus

The current `activation.LoadCorpus` mandates multiple negative categories. Reusing it would silently implement the user-deferred rejection matrix. Leave that Claude contract and all existing tests unchanged.

For each new provider, use focused positive fixture/provenance checks plus built production-path tests. Verify exact fixture digests, provider/version/source metadata, production ingress/frontend/L2, `middleend.Plan`, one ordered durable operation, bounded public read-back, and mechanical native Proceed output. No new malformed, mismatch, provenance-tamper, deny, mutation, PostToolUse, Stop, or exhaustive-catalog tests are acceptance gates.

Execute generated foreign code in the positive integration seam rather than testing only source strings:

- M2 loads the generated TypeScript plugin under Bun with the built Pasture binary and a real temporary SQLite database, invokes the two captured callback values, verifies unchanged tool args/Proceed behavior, then verifies public read-back.
- M3 executes the generated Codex runner/Python adapter with the built binary and exact raw stdin, verifies valid continuation JSON, then verifies public read-back.

Test-local helpers may load authentic fixtures and construct isolated process state; they must not replace or mock the production parser, frontend, middle-end, receipt service, generated adapter, or CLI.

## D7. Keep issue and file ownership explicit

M2 runtime issue #56 owns the shared middle-end, OpenCode runtime/profile/ingress/frontend/activation, lifecycle handler/CLI changes, exact OpenCode lifecycle codegen source/output, and cross-provider Proceed proof. OpenCode issue #27 is coordination-only for these paths.

M3 runtime issue #65 owns the sequential Codex profile/ingress/frontend/activation, Codex lifecycle codegen source/output, handler/CLI extension, and two-live-provider proof. Codex issue #24 is coordination-only for these paths.

Shared files are modified sequentially: #65 starts from accepted M2 and becomes their sole M3 owner. Before worker dispatch, add ownership comments to #27 and #24 and ensure no concurrent branch owns a listed file.

Documentation issue #53 owns only documentation files and cannot change runtime behavior.

## D8. Ratify together, implement and accept separately

This proposal defines both milestones so the shared interface is reviewed once. After ratification, the supervisor creates only the M2 implementation plan. M3 receives a fresh implementation plan from the accepted M2 commit only after M2 code review and implementation UAT pass. No M3 worker, fixture import, profile change, or generated output starts earlier.

Within each milestone, activation is the last unlanded integration step after authentic fixture and production proofs pass. Independent review and implementation UAT evaluate the exact candidate with enabled selected entries. User acceptance authorizes landing that already-reviewed candidate; no unreviewed activation flip occurs after UAT.

# Tradeoffs

| Choice | Selected | Reason |
|---|---:|---|
| Thin `middleend.Plan` over existing stages | Yes | Makes one testable post-L2 owner without a second semantic model |
| New universal operation/response IR | No | No observed caller needs it; conflicts with minimal API requirement |
| Static harness switch and explicit mappings | Yes | Compile-time inventory, easy tests, no speculative registry |
| Generic native-name lookup | No | Deferred #62 and unnecessary for four generated events |
| Replace old exact profiles | Yes | Matches user-selected observed-only versions without #63 compatibility work |
| Four raw exact fixtures | Yes | User-cleared, replayable authentic evidence; no redaction transform |
| Existing full rejection corpus for new providers | No | Would absorb explicitly deferred negative proof work |
| Canonical typed stdout response | Yes | Makes Proceed observable while keeping host mapping mechanical |
| Exit-code-only Proceed | No | Current accepted lifecycle CLI exits successfully even on internal errors |
| Parallel OpenCode/Codex implementation | No | User requires accepted M2 before M3 begins |
| Separate M3 runtime issue | Yes | Prevents #24 artifact scope from swallowing the runtime vertical |

# Problem space

## Engineering axes

- Parallelism: M2 documentation can run beside M2 runtime foundation, but generated transport, handler wiring, and activation converge on shared files. M3 is intentionally sequential after accepted M2.
- Distribution: each harness invokes a local Pasture subprocess, potentially from separate host processes. One SQLite/Provenance operation durably groups occurrence, interpretation, and optional consultation evidence.
- Multiplicity: providers are many; semantic operation/effect derivation is one. Provider ingress and response encoding remain separate N-side adapters around one middle-end.
- Frequency and cost: hooks may fire many times per session. The middle-end is pure and allocation-bounded; durable cost remains one existing receipt operation per invocation.
- Trust boundary: native payloads and foreign adapters are untrusted transport. Constructor-owned Go values become trusted only after provider ingress, frontend binding, and `waist.EventBinding.NewEvent`.

## Relationships

- A provider has one ingress parser, one frontend mapping, one activation table, and one mechanical response encoder.
- A verified `waist.L2` is the input to the shared middle-end; it is not a provider payload.
- A `middleend.Derivation` has one interpreted effect, optionally one consultation effect, and optionally one constructor-built `backend.HostResponse`.
- An authentic fixture is evidence for one observed provider/runtime. OpenCode callback capture bytes are not a separate native wire protocol.

# Current-tree facts

At baseline `0414ad9`, `internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go` directly composes `legalize.Event`, `receipt.NewInterpreted`, and `backend.BuildConsultation`. There is no `internal/lifecycle/lower.go`, generic `Lower`, `EquivalentTo`, provider-neutral response result, OpenCode ingress/frontend, or Codex ingress/frontend.

The reusable production contracts already exist in `waist`, `legalize`, `backend`, `receipt`, `projection`, and the public lifecycle reader. The current handler is Claude-only and returns only `error`; the CLI reports internal errors to stderr, exits successfully by accepted policy, and emits no stdout response.

The generated OpenCode and Codex lifecycle artifacts still read caller-selected `PASTURE_ADAPTER_EVENT`, `PASTURE_ADAPTER_OPERATION`, and `PASTURE_ADAPTER_INPUT` and call `pasture __adapter invoke`. That command remains valid for non-lifecycle semantic adapter use. Only the generated lifecycle route is replaced.

# Architecture decisions

## D1. Add one thin pure post-L2 derivation

Create `internal/lifecycle/middleend/evaluate.go`. It composes the existing pure stages and owns effect ordering. It does not add a provider, context, tracker, clock, operation ID, persistence API, or new semantic/decision enum.

```go
package middleend

type Derivation struct {
    // unexported constructor-owned interpreted record,
    // optional consultation record and optional host response
}

func Derive(event waist.L2) (Derivation, error)
func (d Derivation) Effects() []provenance.Effect
func (d Derivation) Response() backend.HostResponse
func (d Derivation) IsValid() bool
```

`Derive` calls, in order:

1. `legalize.Event(event)`;
2. `receipt.NewInterpreted(event, event.Origin().Contract())`;
3. for a gate only, `backend.BuildConsultation(interpreted, legalized)`.

Observation and existing explicit-human-response semantics produce only the interpreted effect and an invalid zero `HostResponse`; explicit human response must retain the existing valid `NoAuthority` check. Gate consultation produces interpreted then consultation effects and a valid `DecisionProceed` response. `Effects` returns a defensive slice in canonical order. No caller can construct or reorder a valid derivation through exported fields.

This is the missing middle-end boundary without reviving stale `Lower`, `BackendView`, replay-key, or actor machinery.

## D2. Return the existing typed response and use static provider dispatch

Change the internal handler boundary to:

```go
func HookLifecycle(
    ctx context.Context,
    in HookLifecycleInput,
) (backend.HostResponse, error)
```

A successful observation returns the invalid zero response and nil error. `HookLifecycle` passes `middleend.Derivation.Effects()` to `receipt.Service.Receive` and returns `middleend.Derivation.Response()` only after `Receive` succeeds; a receipt error returns no response. A successful gate returns the constructor-built Proceed response after its receipt commits. The CLI writes the canonical `backend.HostResponse` JSON to stdout only when `IsValid()` is true. Existing accepted error handling remains stderr plus successful hook process exit; new negative behavior is not part of this MVP.

Keep one explicit `switch in.Harness` in the handler. Each case selects a generated registration/activation manifest, provider ingress parser, and provider frontend. Do not add a runtime provider registry, reflection, `init` registration, arbitrary map, or generic native-name reverse lookup. Provider frontends mirror the current Claude boundary:

```go
func Parse(
    raw []byte,
    event registration.Event,
    observedVersion string,
    envelope model.OccurrenceEnvelopeRef,
) Capture

func Bind(
    event model.ContractEventKind,
    bindings []model.NativeBinding,
) (waist.L1, []waist.Identity, error)
```

OpenCode and Codex each maintain one explicit registration-event to runtime-event mapping, as Claude does. This does not reopen deferred GitHub #62.

## D3. Replace stale exact profiles; do not build compatibility

Replace internal OpenCode 1.17.18 and Codex 0.144.1 profile constructors/IDs with exact `opencode@1.18.10` and `codex@0.146.0` contracts. Update `PinnedContracts`, lifecycle constructors, generated metadata, manifests, target descriptors, tests, and headers together.

Do not retain dual old/new profiles, fallback selection, skew negotiation, or a support matrix. There is no persisted OpenCode/Codex lifecycle receipt compatibility requirement on the landed Claude-only path. Source-reprofile the closed host catalogs needed by existing code generation, but activate and authentically validate only the two selected events per provider. A source-derived catalog entry is not authentic event evidence. Only the four user-cleared raw candidates may satisfy authentic fixture or activation proof.

Extend the static host-contract generator from one hard-coded Claude contract to a compile-time list of Claude plus the two selected OpenCode and Codex ingress contracts. Generate provider manifests/payload field maps and collision-checked shared event/field symbols. Do not hand-edit generated registration files and do not require exhaustive authentic fixtures.

## D4. Preserve the four exact raw candidates with provider-correct replay

Import exactly the four user-cleared candidates and provenance sidecars under provider ingress packages:

```text
internal/lifecycle/ingress/opencode/testdata/fixtures/
  session_created_1_18_10.capture.json
  session_created_1_18_10.provenance.json
  tool_execute_before_1_18_10.capture.json
  tool_execute_before_1_18_10.provenance.json

internal/lifecycle/ingress/codex/testdata/fixtures/
  session_start_0_146_0.json
  session_start_0_146_0.provenance.json
```

The OpenCode files preserve each selected JSONL record including its line bytes. Tests extract the nested callback `value` as `json.RawMessage` without normalizing it, because the host supplies an in-process object and the production plugin serializes that callback value. The Codex files copy exact command-hook stdin bytes. Every sidecar records observed runtime, inspected source revision, UTC capture time, method, source selector, exact digest, `origin: authentic-capture`, `redaction: none`, and user-clearance reference. ## D5. Replace lifecycle caller-selected operations with mechanical transport

OpenCode generated lifecycle code uses only `PASTURE_BIN` as an executable override. It invokes:

```text
pasture hook lifecycle --harness opencode 
  --event <statically generated event> --host-version 1.18.10
```

For `session.created`, stdin is the serialized callback event object and failure is logged without terminating the observation stream. For `tool.execute.before`, stdin is the serialized `{input, output:{args}}` callback value. The plugin requires canonical `{"decision":"proceed"}` stdout, then returns with `output.args` unchanged. It neither chooses an operation nor extracts semantic identities.

Codex generated event runners invoke the same command with harness `codex`, exact version `0.146.0`, and their statically generated event. The Python adapter forwards exact stdin, requires the canonical Proceed response for `PreToolUse`, and mechanically emits `{"continue":true}`. `SessionStart` is observe-only and emits the native default continuation object. Denial and `updatedInput` are absent.

Remove `PASTURE_ADAPTER_EVENT`, `PASTURE_ADAPTER_OPERATION`, and `PASTURE_ADAPTER_INPUT` from OpenCode/Codex lifecycle artifacts. Do not remove `pasture __adapter invoke` or its non-lifecycle tests.

- M3 executes the generated Codex runner/Python adapter with the built binary and exact raw stdin, verifies valid continuation JSON, then verifies public read-back.

M2 runtime issue #56 owns the shared middle-end, OpenCode runtime/profile/ingress/frontend/activation, lifecycle handler/CLI changes, exact OpenCode lifecycle codegen source/output, and cross-provider Proceed proof. OpenCode issue #27 is coordination-only for these paths.

This proposal defines both milestones so the shared interface is reviewed once. After ratification, the supervisor creates only the M2 implementation plan. The generated OpenCode and Codex lifecycle artifacts still read caller-selected `PASTURE_ADAPTER_EVENT`, `PASTURE_ADAPTER_OPERATION`, and `PASTURE_ADAPTER_INPUT` and call `pasture __adapter invoke`. That command remains valid for non-lifecycle semantic adapter use. Only the generated lifecycle route is replaced.

# Architecture decisions

## D1. Add one thin pure post-L2 derivation

Create `internal/lifecycle/middleend/evaluate.go`. It composes the existing pure stages and owns effect ordering. It does not add a provider, context, tracker, clock, operation ID, persistence API, or new semantic/decision enum.

```go
package middleend

type Derivation struct {
    // unexported constructor-owned interpreted record,
    // optional consultation record and optional host response
}

func Derive(event waist.L2) (Plan, error)
func (d Derivation) Effects() []provenance.Effect
func (d Derivation) Response() backend.HostResponse
func (d Derivation) IsValid() bool
```

`Evaluate` calls, in order:

1. `legalize.Event(event)`;
2. `receipt.NewInterpreted(event, event.Origin().Contract())`;
3. for a gate only, `backend.BuildConsultation(interpreted, legalized)`.

Observation and existing explicit-human-response semantics produce only the interpreted effect and an invalid zero `HostResponse`; explicit human response must retain the existing valid `NoAuthority` check. Gate consultation produces interpreted then consultation effects and a valid `DecisionProceed` response. `Effects` returns a defensive slice in canonical order. No caller can construct or reorder a valid plan through exported fields.

This is the missing middle-end boundary without reviving stale `Lower`, `BackendView`, replay-key, or actor machinery.

## D2. Return the existing typed response and use static provider dispatch

Change the internal handler boundary to:

```go
func HookLifecycle(
    ctx context.Context,
    in HookLifecycleInput,
) (backend.HostResponse, error)
```

A successful observation returns the invalid zero response and nil error. `HookLifecycle` passes `middleend.Derivation.Effects()` to `receipt.Service.Receive` and returns `middleend.Derivation.Response()` only after `Receive` succeeds; a receipt error returns no response. A successful gate returns the constructor-built Proceed response after its receipt commits. The CLI writes the canonical `backend.HostResponse` JSON to stdout only when `IsValid()` is true. Existing accepted error handling remains stderr plus successful hook process exit; new negative behavior is not part of this MVP.

Keep one explicit `switch in.Harness` in the handler. Each case selects a generated registration/activation manifest, provider ingress parser, and provider frontend. Do not add a runtime provider registry, reflection, `init` registration, arbitrary map, or generic native-name reverse lookup. Provider frontends mirror the current Claude boundary:

```go
func Parse(
    raw []byte,
    event registration.Event,
    observedVersion string,
    envelope model.OccurrenceEnvelopeRef,
) Capture

func Bind(
    event model.ContractEventKind,
    bindings []model.NativeBinding,
) (waist.L1, []waist.Identity, error)
```

OpenCode and Codex each maintain one explicit registration-event to runtime-event mapping, as Claude does. This does not reopen deferred GitHub #62.

## D3. Replace stale exact profiles; do not build compatibility

Replace internal OpenCode 1.17.18 and Codex 0.144.1 profile constructors/IDs with exact `opencode@1.18.10` and `codex@0.146.0` contracts. Update `PinnedContracts`, lifecycle constructors, generated metadata, manifests, target descriptors, tests, and headers together.

Do not retain dual old/new profiles, fallback selection, skew negotiation, or a support matrix. There is no persisted OpenCode/Codex lifecycle receipt compatibility requirement on the landed Claude-only path. Source-reprofile the closed host catalogs needed by existing code generation, but activate and authentically validate only the two selected events per provider. A source-derived catalog entry is not authentic event evidence. Only the four user-cleared raw candidates may satisfy authentic fixture or activation proof.

Extend the static host-contract generator from one hard-coded Claude contract to a compile-time list of Claude plus the two selected OpenCode and Codex ingress contracts. Generate provider manifests/payload field maps and collision-checked shared event/field symbols. Do not hand-edit generated registration files and do not require exhaustive authentic fixtures.

## D4. Preserve the four exact raw candidates with provider-correct replay

Import exactly the four user-cleared candidates and provenance sidecars under provider ingress packages:

```text
internal/lifecycle/ingress/opencode/testdata/fixtures/
  session_created_1_18_10.capture.json
  session_created_1_18_10.provenance.json
  tool_execute_before_1_18_10.capture.json
  tool_execute_before_1_18_10.provenance.json

internal/lifecycle/ingress/codex/testdata/fixtures/
  session_start_0_146_0.json
  session_start_0_146_0.provenance.json
  pre_tool_use_0_146_0.json
  pre_tool_use_0_146_0.provenance.json
```

The OpenCode files preserve each selected JSONL record including its line bytes. Tests extract the nested callback `value` as `json.RawMessage` without normalizing it, because the host supplies an in-process object and the production plugin serializes that callback value. Provenance records both the parent lifecycle JSONL digest and extracted record digest, identifies callback-object observation, and never claims a native wire byte stream.

The Codex files copy exact command-hook stdin bytes. Every sidecar records observed runtime, inspected source revision, UTC capture time, method, source selector, exact digest, `origin: authentic-capture`, `redaction: none`, and user-clearance reference. No transcript, PostToolUse, Stop, final message, database, cache, or auth file is imported.

## D5. Replace lifecycle caller-selected operations with mechanical transport

OpenCode generated lifecycle code uses only `PASTURE_BIN` as an executable override. It invokes:

```text
pasture hook lifecycle --harness opencode 
  --event <statically generated event> --host-version 1.18.10
```

For `session.created`, stdin is the serialized callback event object and failure is logged without terminating the observation stream. For `tool.execute.before`, stdin is the serialized `{input, output:{args}}` callback value. The plugin requires canonical `{"decision":"proceed"}` stdout, then returns with `output.args` unchanged. It neither chooses an operation nor extracts semantic identities.

Codex generated event runners invoke the same command with harness `codex`, exact version `0.146.0`, and their statically generated event. The Python adapter forwards exact stdin, requires the canonical Proceed response for `PreToolUse`, and mechanically emits `{"continue":true}`. `SessionStart` is observe-only and emits the native default continuation object. Denial and `updatedInput` are absent.

Remove `PASTURE_ADAPTER_EVENT`, `PASTURE_ADAPTER_OPERATION`, and `PASTURE_ADAPTER_INPUT` from OpenCode/Codex lifecycle artifacts. Do not remove `pasture __adapter invoke` or its non-lifecycle tests.

## D6. Use direct positive evidence; do not weaken the Claude corpus

The current `activation.LoadCorpus` mandates multiple negative categories. Reusing it would silently implement the user-deferred rejection matrix. Leave that Claude contract and all existing tests unchanged.

For each new provider, use focused positive fixture/provenance checks plus built production-path tests. Verify exact fixture digests, provider/version/source metadata, production ingress/frontend/L2, `middleend.Derivation`, one ordered durable operation, bounded public read-back, and mechanical native Proceed output. No new malformed, mismatch, provenance-tamper, deny, mutation, PostToolUse, Stop, or exhaustive-catalog tests are acceptance gates.

Execute generated foreign code in the positive integration seam rather than testing only source strings:

- M2 loads the generated TypeScript plugin under Bun with the built Pasture binary and a real temporary SQLite database, invokes the two captured callback values, verifies unchanged tool args/Proceed behavior, then verifies public read-back.
- M3 executes the generated Codex runner/Python adapter with the built binary and exact raw stdin, verifies valid continuation JSON, then verifies public read-back.

Test-local helpers may load authentic fixtures and construct isolated process state; they must not replace or mock the production parser, frontend, middle-end, receipt service, generated adapter, or CLI.

## D7. Keep issue and file ownership explicit

M2 runtime issue #56 owns the shared middle-end, OpenCode runtime/profile/ingress/frontend/activation, lifecycle handler/CLI changes, exact OpenCode lifecycle codegen source/output, and cross-provider Proceed proof. OpenCode issue #27 is coordination-only for these paths.

M3 runtime issue #65 owns the sequential Codex profile/ingress/frontend/activation, Codex lifecycle codegen source/output, handler/CLI extension, and two-live-provider proof. Codex issue #24 is coordination-only for these paths.

Shared files are modified sequentially: #65 starts from accepted M2 and becomes their sole M3 owner. Before worker dispatch, add ownership comments to #27 and #24 and ensure no concurrent branch owns a listed file.

Documentation issue #53 owns only documentation files and cannot change runtime behavior.

## D8. Ratify together, implement and accept separately

This proposal defines both milestones so the shared interface is reviewed once. After ratification, the supervisor creates only the M2 implementation plan. M3 receives a fresh implementation plan from the accepted M2 commit only after M2 code review and implementation UAT pass. No M3 worker, fixture import, profile change, or generated output starts earlier.

Within each milestone, activation is the last unlanded integration step after authentic fixture and production proofs pass. Independent review and implementation UAT evaluate the exact candidate with enabled selected entries. User acceptance authorizes landing that already-reviewed candidate; no unreviewed activation flip occurs after UAT.

# Horizontal Integration Points

| ID | Contract | Owner | Consumers | Merge timing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IP-1 | middleend.Derivation and Derive | S1 | S4, S6 | Wave 1 consolidation |
| IP-2 | OpenCode 1.18.10 registration, ingress, frontend, verified L2 | S2 | S4, S5, S6 | Wave 1 consolidation |
| IP-3 | Post-commit backend.HostResponse handler/CLI contract | S4 | S5 final proof, S6 | S4 wiring leaf checkpoint in Wave 2 |
| IP-4 | Bun-executable generated OpenCode transport | S5 | S6 | Wave 2 consolidation |
| IP-5 | Correct M1 and privacy documentation | S3 | M2 UAT | Wave 1 consolidation |

# Review Protocol

Three independent reviewers assess every completed slice in the same integrated wave candidate across correctness, test quality, and elegance. Review tasks and eager BLOCKER/IMPORTANT/MINOR groups remain per slice, with one shared wave round number and integrated commit. All findings are fixed; none route to a follow-up epic. Review proceeds for at most three rounds per implementation wave. Only a fix-free 0/0/0 round closes slices and the wave barrier.

# Consolidated Validation Gates

- Every focused and full Go test command includes -race.
- make generate followed by a second make generate produces no second-run diff.
- make fmt passes.
- make lint passes.
- CGO_ENABLED=1 make test-race passes.
- make build passes.
- nix flake check --no-build passes.
- git diff --check passes.
- Actual generated TypeScript executes under Bun against the built CLI and real temporary storage.
- Public read-back proves provider-correct durable evidence.
- No caller-selected lifecycle operation remains in OpenCode transport.
- No Git hook is installed, enabled, or modified.

# Explicit Deferrals

Exclude rejection matrices; deny and input mutation; PostToolUse, Stop, and other events; exhaustive authentic catalogs; dual-version support and #63; live Claude #55; #54 and #57 through #62; all raw captures except the two cleared OpenCode records; Codex M3/#65; Strike; Grok Build; M4; and M5+.
