## Finding
OpenCode activation is not enforced at the production lifecycle ingress. internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go:49-53 always loads Claude activation entries, and internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go:89-96 only rejects withheld events when in.Harness is Claude. For OpenCode, any source-known generated event bypasses the activation manifest, even though .opencode/pasture-opencode.json marks 45 events as withheld.

## End-user impact
The M2 UAT candidate promises exactly session.created and tool.execute.before are active and all other OpenCode 1.18.10 manifest events are withheld. A direct production invocation can still persist a withheld OpenCode occurrence, so the activation-last safety boundary is not fail-closed.

## Reproduction
In the isolated review worktree, after initializing a temp DB, this direct production command exited 0 and public read-back returned a session.updated occurrence despite session.updated being withheld:

PASTURE_DB_PATH=... nix develop -c env CGO_ENABLED=1 go run -race . task create init
PASTURE_DB_PATH=... nix develop -c env CGO_ENABLED=1 go run -race . hook lifecycle --harness opencode --event session.updated --host-version 1.18.10 < session_created_1_18_10.capture.json
PASTURE_DB_PATH=... nix develop -c env CGO_ENABLED=1 go run -race . hook lifecycle list --format json
Observed read-back included: {"items":[{"event":47,"registrationContract":"opencode/1.18.10","interpreted":[]}]}

## Exact fix
Make HookLifecycleResponse select the activation manifest for the requested harness (Claude -> activation.ClaudeCode2_1_210(), OpenCode -> activation.OpenCode1_18_10()) and apply the same !found/state != Enabled rejection for every harness before reading stdin/opening storage. Add a race-enabled production test that invokes a withheld OpenCode event such as session.updated and asserts non-admission/no lifecycle record, while keeping selected session.created and tool.execute.before green.

references:
  request: aura-plugins-leeeiw
  proposal_50: aura-plugins-jdj2x

## Questions And Responses

### Codex Export Goal

Definition/code shown verbatim:

```text
Already landed:
  Pasture codegen -> .codex/agents/pasture-<role>.toml
  global installer target -> ~/.codex/agents/pasture-<role>.toml

Still deferred:
  user selects another project -> that project's .codex/agents/
```

Question asked verbatim:

What end-user operation should the project-local Codex component provide?

Options presented verbatim:

- Install into a project (Recommended): A user selects a project root; Pasture safely ensures/removes its agent profiles under `<project>/.codex/agents/` while preserving unrelated files.
- Codegen output only: Provide a command that renders profiles to an output tree, with no ownership inventory or uninstall behavior.
- Already fulfilled: Treat committed `.codex/agents/` generation as satisfying the request; audit #24 and create no new epic.

User response verbatim:

Install into a project (Recommended)

### Project Selection And Command Shape

Question asked verbatim:

How should users select the destination project for agent installation?

Options presented verbatim:

- Explicit project path (Recommended): `pasture install codex-agents --project PATH --enabled=true|false`; works from any directory and is scriptable.
- Current project only: Operate on the current working directory after confirming it is the intended project root.
- Installer project list: Extend the interactive installer to maintain and select multiple saved project roots.

User response verbatim:

Installer project list, Explicit project path (Recommended), The installer command should be `pasture install `<harness>` , where `<harness>` is not `codex-agents`, but instead `codex`, with `--agents={true,false}`, `--skills` similarly. The installer project list should list the currently installed project roots. We should track them similar to `pasture-release`, where we have a registry of projects and the attributes which they've installed.

### Ownership State

Definition/code shown verbatim:

```text
Global state:
  ~/.local/state/pasture/projects/<project-id>/codex-agents.yaml
  project receives only .codex/agents/*.toml

Project state:
  <project>/.pasture/installations.yaml
  state can move with the checkout but becomes another project file
```

Question asked verbatim:

Project-scoped uninstall must distinguish Pasture-created profiles from identical or modified project files. Where should that ownership record live?

Options presented verbatim:

- Global per-project state (Recommended): Key records by canonical project root; avoid adding Pasture metadata to repositories and preserve exact digest/mode ownership.
- Project-local state: Store ownership with the project so moving/cloning can carry it, at the cost of another local or committed file.
- No persistent state: Only add absent files and never support managed update/removal.

User response verbatim:

Global per-project state (Recommended)

### Initial Harness Scope

Definition/code shown verbatim:

```text
pasture install codex --project /work/repo \
  --skills=true --agents=true --hooks=false
pasture install projects list
```

Question asked verbatim:

The generic command shape can support more later. What should this first project-install epic implement? Select one boundary.

Options presented verbatim:

- Codex skills and agents (Recommended): Deliver `.agents/skills/` and `.codex/agents/`; reject project hooks for now because the originating follow-up was agent export and hooks add trust/runtime concerns.
- All three Codex axes: Also manage project-local `.codex/hooks/`, default off, without mutating native trust.
- All harnesses now: Implement project-local skills/agents/hooks for Claude, OpenCode, and Codex in one epic.

User response verbatim:

All three Codex axes, All harnesses now

### Omitted Flags

Definition/code shown verbatim:

```text
pasture install codex --project /work/repo --skills=true
```

Question asked verbatim:

What should an omitted axis flag mean? For example, after agents are installed, the user runs the command shown above.

Options presented verbatim:

- Leave unchanged (Recommended): Flags are patch operations; omitted recorded axes retain their state, and omitted never-recorded axes remain absent.
- Apply safe defaults: Omitted axes become skills=true, agents=true, hooks=false on every invocation.
- Require every axis: Reject the command unless all supported axis flags are supplied as an exhaustive desired state.

User response verbatim:

Apply safe defaults

### Project Picker

Definition/code shown verbatim:

```text
# Scriptable
pasture install codex --project /work/repo --skills=true --agents=true

# Interactive
pasture install codex
  > /work/repo-a   codex: skills, agents
    /work/repo-b   opencode: skills, agents, hooks
    Add current directory: /work/repo-c
```

Question asked verbatim:

How should `pasture install <harness>` combine the explicit path and installed-project list?

Options presented verbatim:

- Flag or interactive picker (Recommended): `--project` bypasses prompts; without it, a TTY lists registered roots plus cwd; non-TTY without the flag fails actionably.
- Path always required: Keep `projects list` informational; every install requires `--project`.
- Current directory default: Without `--project`, immediately use cwd rather than ask or consult the registry.

User response verbatim:

Flag or interactive picker (Recommended)

### Shared Config

Question asked verbatim:

For project hooks, Pasture may need to modify shared files such as `.claude/settings.json`, `opencode.json`, or `.codex/hooks.json`. How should it coexist with project-owned settings?

Options presented verbatim:

- Typed owned merge (Recommended): Parse the pinned schema, preserve unrelated entries and formatting where feasible, add/remove only exact Pasture-owned entries, and refuse drift or ambiguous duplicates.
- Whole-file ownership: Create shared config only when absent or already exactly Pasture-managed; reject any foreign existing config.
- No shared config edits: Install hook payload files only and report manual activation steps; the hooks axis is not fully activated by Pasture.

User response verbatim:

Typed owned merge (Recommended)

### Project Identity

Definition/code shown verbatim:

```text
Input: /work/link-to-repo
Canonical path: /work/repo  # EvalSymlinks + absolute clean path
Registry key: canonical path
```

Question asked verbatim:

What identifies a registered project after `--project` is supplied? A moved checkout becomes a new path; the old record remains visible until removed.

Options presented verbatim:

- Canonical path only (Recommended): Resolve an existing directory to absolute symlink-free path; do not require Git, remote, or a repository marker.
- Git identity required: Require a Git worktree and key records by canonical path plus repository remote/root.
- Raw path preserved: Store the user spelling exactly, including relative paths and symlink aliases.

User response verbatim:

Canonical path only (Recommended)

### Uninstall And Registry

Question asked verbatim:

When all nine axes for a project become disabled, what should happen after Pasture safely removes every managed file/config entry?

Options presented verbatim:

- Keep absent project record (Recommended): Retain the canonical root with all axes absent and last outcome, so the picker shows prior projects and audits removal.
- Remove project record: Delete the registry entry after successful full removal; only active projects appear.
- Ask interactively: Prompt whether to retain or forget a project after full removal.

User response verbatim:

Keep absent project record (Recommended), Ask interactively

### Empty Project Record Clarification

Question asked verbatim:

After a successful full uninstall, should the registry retain the project automatically or prompt the user?

Options presented verbatim:

- Retain automatically (Recommended): Best for scripted and non-TTY use; `pasture install projects list` keeps the historical root and absent axes.
- Prompt on TTY: Interactive users choose retain/forget; non-TTY commands must require an explicit `--forget` or `--retain` flag.

User response verbatim:

Retain automatically (Recommended)

### Artifact Updates

Question asked verbatim:

When a later Pasture binary installs newer generated skills/agents/hooks into a registered project, how should update behavior work?

Options presented verbatim:

- Update on each install (Recommended): The selected axes reconcile to the invoking binary's immutable bundles when their recorded file digest/mode still match; modified files fail without overwrite.
- Install once only: Existing managed files remain at their original version until a future explicit update command.
- Require version flag: Every project install names an explicit Pasture artifact version rather than using the invoking binary.

User response verbatim:

Update on each install (Recommended)

### First Mutation

Question asked verbatim:

For a new project supplied via noninteractive `--project`, what confirmation boundary should protect the first file/config mutation?

Options presented verbatim:

- Explicit --yes required (Recommended): TTY shows a plan and requests confirmation; non-TTY must pass `--yes`, otherwise it prints the plan and changes nothing.
- Always apply: An explicit `--project` is itself consent; no confirmation flag or prompt.
- Dry-run first: First use only prints a plan; a separate rerun with `--apply` performs mutation.

User response verbatim:

Explicit --yes required (Recommended)

### Validation Boundary

Definition/code shown verbatim:

```text
pasture install <claude-code|opencode|codex> [--project PATH]
  --skills={true,false} --agents={true,false} --hooks={true,false} [--yes]
pasture install projects list
```

Question asked verbatim:

Proposed definition of done:

A path is resolved to an existing canonical directory. `--project` is scriptable; a TTY without it uses the registered-project picker plus cwd; non-TTY without it fails. Omitted axes normalize to skills=true, agents=true, hooks=false. The global registry stores every canonical project root, all 3x3 selected-axis states, per-file digest/mode ownership, and outcomes; it keeps fully absent roots.

Must pass: install/update/remove all nine cells using each pinned project-local host path; preserve unrelated project files and config entries; typed hook merges add/remove only Pasture-owned entries; linked/canonical aliases resolve to one record; repeat converges; modified managed files/config entries fail without overwrite; project list is deterministic; interactive confirmation and `--yes` non-TTY behavior work.

Must fail: missing/non-directory/broken project path; unrecognized harness; non-TTY without `--project`; first mutation without `--yes`; unrecognized config schema/ambiguous duplicate Pasture hook entry; path traversal or symlinked managed leaf; hook trust/approval mutation; foreign file overwrite; uninstall of unrecorded/external content.

Is this complete?

Options presented verbatim:

- Validation complete (Recommended): Use this as the URD and epic acceptance boundary.
- Add pass case: A successful behavior is missing.
- Add fail case: A forbidden behavior is missing.
- Revise scope: The command, registry, or supported axes need adjustment.

User response verbatim:

Validation complete (Recommended)

## Final Decisions

- Deliver one project-local installer across Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex, with skills, agents, and hooks for each harness.
- Use `pasture install <harness>` with `--project`, `--skills`, `--agents`, `--hooks`, and `--yes`; use `pasture install projects list` for the deterministic registry view.
- Without `--project`, interactive terminals show registered roots plus the current directory. Noninteractive callers must provide `--project`.
- Every invocation normalizes omitted extension flags to skills enabled, agents enabled, and hooks disabled.
- Store project installation and ownership evidence globally, keyed only by the existing directory's canonical absolute symlink-resolved path. Git identity is not required.
- Retain fully absent project records automatically after successful uninstall.
- Reconcile selected axes to immutable artifacts embedded in the invoking Pasture binary. Refuse to overwrite modified managed or foreign content.
- Project hooks use typed, ownership-aware merges into shared host configuration, preserve unrelated entries, and fail on unknown schemas, drift, or ambiguous duplicates.
- Hook installation never mutates host trust or approval state.
- Show a plan and require interactive confirmation. Noninteractive first mutation requires `--yes`.

## Validation Cases

- Definition of done: the public command installs, updates, and removes all nine project-local harness/extension cells while a global canonical-path registry reports every project's desired and confirmed attributes without placing Pasture state files in the project.
- Must pass: all nine isolated cells; safe defaults; explicit and interactive project selection; canonical alias collapse; deterministic list; exact update/removal ownership; typed shared-config coexistence; unrelated-file preservation; repeat convergence; absent-record retention; plan confirmation and noninteractive `--yes`.

## Questions And Responses

### Markdown-Only Purpose

Definition/code shown verbatim:

The earlier deferral named a “Markdown-only semantic-instructions mode,” but the later architecture correction says Pasture is specifically the deterministic CLI/FSM and that relying on LLM interpretation for SDLC state is erroneous. A Markdown-only package can therefore be either a clearly non-authoritative guidance bundle, or the request should be retired as contrary to the product direction.

Question asked verbatim:

What should happen to the deferred Markdown-only component given that it cannot enforce the FSM, persist provenance, replace Beads, or reliably perform user-gated transitions without the Pasture CLI?

Options presented verbatim:

- Retire the component (Recommended): Record that Markdown-only execution contradicts Pasture's deterministic product goal; generated skills remain documentation, but there is no separate no-CLI delivery epic.
- Guidance-only package: Ship installable Markdown that explains workflows and labels every stateful/authoritative operation unavailable; no claims of protocol completion or provenance.
- Manual protocol mode: Let agents/humans execute the full workflow from Markdown and track state externally despite weaker determinism.

User response verbatim:

Manual protocol mode

### External State

Question asked verbatim:

Where should manual protocol mode expect users to record tasks, decisions, reviews, and handoffs when Pasture is absent?

Options presented verbatim:

- Tracker-neutral templates (Recommended): Generate Markdown forms and semantic instructions with opaque placeholders; users choose GitHub Issues, files, another tracker, or manual records.
- GitHub Issues profile: Provide concrete `gh`-oriented instructions and issue templates as the manual state backend.
- Repository Markdown ledger: Define a committed `.pasture-manual/` task/decision/handoff layout as the manual source of truth.

User response verbatim:

all this should do is install skills only.

### Capability Reporting

Question asked verbatim:

How should generated artifacts communicate the weaker guarantees?

Options presented verbatim:

- Explicit mode manifest (Recommended): Every package carries `mode: manual-protocol`, enumerates unsupported guarantees, and generated instructions state that transitions/provenance are not machine-enforced.
- Documentation note only: Explain limitations in README/SKILL prose without a typed package-level mode marker.
- Same protocol identity: Present manual and CLI-backed packages as equivalent Pasture protocol implementations.

User response verbatim:

Unanswered

### Skills-Only Content

Definition/code shown verbatim:

The current skills are not actually CLI-independent: they contain operational `bd` commands, and the intended migrated form will contain `pasture task`/`pasture epoch` operations. Installing those unchanged on a machine without Pasture would produce unusable instructions. The skills-only mode therefore needs one precise content decision.

Question asked verbatim:

What should the skills-only/manual package contain when no Pasture CLI is available?

Options presented verbatim:

- Manual-rendered skills (Recommended): Generate a distinct profile from the same typed protocol source: preserve phases, roles, checklists, questions, reviews, and handoffs; replace stateful CLI operations with tracker-neutral human/agent instructions and explicitly state there is no machine enforcement or provenance.
- Existing skills unchanged: Install the normal skills even though their `pasture`/task commands cannot run; users adapt failures manually.
- Protocol docs only: Install only the non-operational protocol reference skill, excluding worker/supervisor/architect command skills.

User response verbatim:

Existing skills unchanged, manual rendered skills as deferred.

### Delivery Ownership

Definition/code shown verbatim:

```text
Project-local:
pasture install codex --project /work/repo \
  --skills=true --agents=false --hooks=false

Global interactive/scriptable installer:
select skills=true, agents=false, hooks=false
```

Question asked verbatim:

Should skills-only delivery be a separate epic, or an acceptance case of the installer epics already being defined?

Options presented verbatim:

- Fold into installers (Recommended): No separate Markdown-only epic; require global and project installers to prove each harness's skills-only cell works with agents/hooks absent.
- Separate skills command: Create another public install command and epic dedicated to skills-only delivery.
- Release archive only: Publish standalone skills archives outside installer ownership.

User response verbatim:

Fold into installers (Recommended)

### Final Disposition

Question asked verbatim:

Proposed complete record for the Markdown-only follow-up:

- Create no separate Markdown-only GitHub epic.
- Global and project-local installers must support `skills=true, agents=false, hooks=false` independently for Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex.
- Install the existing generated skill trees byte-for-byte; do not create a second compiler profile now.
- The installed skills may still reference Pasture/task operations and are not claimed to provide deterministic FSM enforcement or provenance when the CLI is unavailable.
- A tracker-neutral/manual-rendered skills profile is deferred and requires a future explicit request.

Is this complete?

Options presented verbatim:

- Disposition complete (Recommended): Record this in URE/URD evidence and fold its validation into installer epic drafts.
- Add requirement: Add another skills-only behavior or guarantee.
- Separate epic after all: Keep Markdown-only delivery as its own implementation issue.

User response verbatim:

Disposition complete (Recommended)

## Final Decisions

- Create no standalone Markdown-only component epic.
- Treat skills-only delivery as an acceptance case of both the global and project-local installers.
- Each harness must support skills enabled with agents and hooks disabled and absent.
- Install the existing generated skill tree byte-for-byte; do not introduce a second rendering profile in this program.
- Skills-only installation is not evidence that the Pasture FSM or provenance is enforced when the CLI is absent.
- A tracker-neutral manual rendering that removes or replaces unavailable stateful commands is deferred until a future explicit request.

## Validation Cases

- Definition of done: both installer scopes can install and remove the existing generated skills for each harness while agents and hooks remain absent.
- Must pass: Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex skills-only installation; byte identity with the published skills bundle; sibling absence; idempotent update/removal; preservation of unrelated content.
- Must fail: installing an agent or hook as a transitive dependency of skills; claiming deterministic FSM/provenance without the CLI; silently substituting a newly rewritten manual profile.
- Out of scope: external task backend, manual ledger schema, GitHub Issues profile, tracker-neutral operation rewriting, or equivalence with CLI-backed execution.
